News.title: Illegal migrants could be ‘deported from Britain within hours of failed appeals’ in new crackdown
News.content:
SWIFT EXIT Illegal migrants could be ‘deported from Britain within hours of failed appeals’ in new crackdown







Next

ILLEGAL migrants could be put on planes within hours of their final appeals failing under Labour’s new deportation plans.

Shabana Mahmood wants to shut a loophole which hands failed migrants five-working days’ notice before they can be deported.



Ms Mahmood’s plans would give the Home Office a six-month window to remove failed asylum seekers with no notice.

Many migrants use this period to lodge last-ditch claims to stall their removal from Britain.



Migrants will also have to set out every reason for staying at the very start of the asylum process, the Daily Mail revealed.

But the Tories and Reform have blasted the plans and urged Britain to leave the European Court for Human Rights.

Shadow Home Secretary Chris Phil said failed claimants should be on the first plane home.

He added: “As long as Labour keep Britain in the ECHR, removals will keep being dragged through the courts, leaving taxpayers to keep paying for the accommodation while they wait.

“The Conservatives will take the UK out of the ECHR, so that illegal immigrants can be deported as soon as possible.”

Reform’s home affairs spokesperson Zia Yusuf said: “The only way to reverse this invasion is to leave the ECHR and then embark on the biggest mass deportation programme Britain has ever seen.



“Reform UK will detain and deport all illegal migrants the Tories and Labour allowed in.”

Ms Mahmood’s plans are based on Denmark’s, where they have seen levels halve within a few years.

But there are concerns Labour MPs will not be able to stomach more hardline measures to protect Britain’s borders.

More than ten Labour rebels already voted against the Bill at second reading and the new amendment risks a bigger backbench mutiny.

Ms Mahmood also watered down her flagship migrant bill after she scrapped plans for migrant care workers already in the UK to wait 15 years for permanent settlement

News.title: Three killed after missing plane crashes in Grand Canyon as horror wreckage discovered day after flight vanished
News.content:
‘NO SURVIVORS’ Three killed after missing plane crashes in Grand Canyon as horror wreckage discovered day after flight vanished







Next

THREE people have died after a small plane plunged into a remote area of the Grand Canyon.

Search crews discovered the wreckage of a downed Piper Comanche aircraft on Monday morning – just one day after the plane was reported missing.



The burnt-out remains of the light aircraft were spotted after an extensive aerial search – with authorities confirming no survivors were found at the crash site.

In a statement, the National Park Service said: “Grand Canyon Regional Communications Center received a report of a missing Piper Comanche aircraft with three people aboard at approximately 11.30pm on November 15.



“The aircraft’s last known location was in the vicinity of the Basin area on the North Rim.

“The Arizona Department of Public Safety conducted an aerial search in the early morning hours of November 16 using forward-looking infrared and night vision.”

Officials said specialists from Coconino County Search and Rescue, Kane County Search and Rescue, and the Air Force Rescue Coordination Center all participated in the search effort.

Crews scoured the rocky landscape of the iconic national park before finally locating the wreckage shortly after 10am on Monday morning in an area described as “mountainous terrain”.

Authorities are yet to release the identities of those on board the plane out of respect for the victims’ families.

The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) has launched a probe to investigate the cause of the horror crash.



A statement read: “An NTSB investigator is expected to arrive at the accident site on Tuesday.

“After the wreckage is documented, it will be recovered and moved to a secure facility for further examination.”

The tragedy comes just days after two people were injured when a cargo plane crashed into a passenger jet at Miami International Airport.

The pilot of a Copa Airlines flight arriving from Panama City declared “somebody hit us” on the radio while crossing a taxiway.

Its wing had clipped the nose of a Bogota, Colombia, bound UPS plane at an intersection on the tarmac around 9.15pm on Saturday.



It was not clear if the incident had anything to do with ripple effects of the national aviation ground stop.

The accident came just weeks after nine people were killed when a Learjet plunged nearly 27,000ft in under a minute before smashing into a residential street in nearby Palm Beach County.

Horrifying ATC audio captured 20-year-old co-pilot Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras screaming that they were going to crash, while captain Jeffrey Gregory, 55, reportedly began praying.

Harrowing video footage showed the jet slamming into the tarmac before erupting into a terrifying fireball.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The tragedy claimed the lives of tech entrepreneur Adam Robinson, 45, his wife Helen Sharp, 40, and their children Emma, four, and Charlie, two.



Their nanny Anita Maria Cetina and family friends Rachael Reed and Charmi Fehr were also killed, along with captain Gregory and co-pilot Filgueiras.

News.title: Two passenger trains crash near railway station in Prague leaving dozens injured as emergency services scramble to scene
News.content:
Next

DOZENS of people are injured after two passenger trains collided in a horror crash in Prague.

Firefighters and emergency crews rushed the the scene near the Czech capital’s main railway station at around 7am this morning.



Several people have been rushed to hospitals across the city with serious injuries, local media reports.

Footage from the scene shows the damage to the trains with metal ripped back and torn off from the impact.



Both trains were reportedly travelling at low speeds when the smashed into on another on the railway bridge over Seifertova Street.

Emergency services deployed multiple crews to the scene under a second-level alert.



The accident has thrown Prague Main Station into chaos with restrictions, cancellations and delays expected to continue for several hours.

A number of trains have been diverted to Praha-Vysočany and Praha-Libeň instead with others terminating via Praha-Holešovice.



The cause of the collision remains unclear.

It comes after a series of devastating train crashes in recent months that have left dozens dead and hundreds injured.

Just weeks ago two trains collided in Egypt, killing six passengers and the driver.

More than 100 others suffered serious injuries after the crash in Al-Ayyat, south of Cairo, which has been dubbed the “Bermuda Triangle of train crashes”.

A train travelling from Giza to Fayoum smashed into service train heading to Aswan from Cairo, sending carriages hurtling off the tracks.



People living nearby rushed to the wreckage to pull survivors from the carriages as they alerted emergency services.

Astonishing images from the scene showed people clambering over entire sections of the trains that had plunged down a verge after the crash.

At least 80 people were trapped inside the wreckage before being pulled free by rescue crews.

And in October at least 68 people died after two high speed trains collided in central Spain.

A Renfe service travelling at an estimated 124mph slammed into the back of a stationary Iryo train on a line from Madrid to Seville.



The crash occurred in the province of Toledo, bringing the country’s high-speed rail link between Madrid and southern Spain of an immediate halt.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Half an hour before the crash, a computer glitch suspended all travel along 39 miles of track – before human error piled on further problems.

Haunting audio recordings revealed a critical lapse in communication between Adif’s control centre in Atocha and the train drivers.

News.title: Rush-hour chaos as up to 15cm of snow to hit UK with power cuts & travel misery after -7.7C big freeze
News.content:
COMMUTE CHAOS Rush-hour chaos as up to 15cm of snow to hit UK with power cuts & travel misery after -7.7C big freeze







Next

BRITS have been warned of travel chaos as snow sweeps across parts of the UK during the morning rush hour.

A yellow weather warning is in force across large parts of the country, with forecasters predicting heavy snowfall, strong winds and possible power cuts.



Shocking photos show snow carpeting affected areas this morning, as forecasters warn of trouble on the roads from the cold snap.

The Met Office alert stretches from Staffordshire in the West Midlands to south-west Scotland and will remain until 11am today.



Up to 3cm of snow was recorded at Spadeadam in Cumbria this morning, with major routes such as the A74(M), A66 and M62 also facing potential disruption.

It comes after the UK saw its coldest night of the season so far on Sunday, with temperatures plunging to minus 7.7C recorded in the Scottish Highlands.



Parts of Yorkshire, Derbyshire, Northumberland, Greater Manchester, Cumbria and Lancashire are among the areas affected from the current weather warning.

Roads and railways are likely to be disrupted, while there is also a small chance of power cuts and mobile phone services being affected.

Forecasters say areas above 100 metres are likely to see the worst of the wintry conditions, with snow falling at lower levels expected to melt quickly.

Between 1cm and 5cm of snow could settle in affected areas.



They add that higher ground above 300 to 400 metres could see up to 15cm.

Met Office meteorologist Alex Burkill warned there was likely to be disruption during Tuesday’s morning rush hour.

“We have a weather system out towards the west/south west of us that’s going to feed north-eastwards and, importantly, it’s going to hit against the cold air that’s across us and as a result we’re going to see some snow,” he said.

“The rain’s already quite heavy and persistent across some parts of the far South West, and all that wet weather then is going to feed north-eastwards.



“There will be some blustery, strong, gusty winds mixed in with it and as I mentioned some significant snow across parts of north Wales perhaps, but also northern parts of England and southern Scotland.

“We could see maybe five to 15 centimetres of snow building up above three to four hundred metres and even to slightly lower levels, a bit of lying snow is possible, which is why there is a warning out because there’s likely to be some disruption, particularly during the morning rush hour on Tuesday.”



The meteorologist also said there could be thunder and hail mixed in with rain, as well as brighter breaks between showers.

A yellow cold health alert has been issued for the North West, North East and Yorkshire and the Humber.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The UK Health Security Agency warning will remain in place until 9am on Thursday.

The agency warned the conditions could increase demand on health services and pose a greater risk to vulnerable people.

News.title: Married teacher, 34, caught on camera raping boy, 13, before giving birth to his baby after year of abuse is jailed
News.content:
Next

A MARRIED teacher who raped a 13-year-old boy before giving birth to his baby after a nightmarish year of abuse has been jailed.

Mum-of-two Naomi Tekea Craig, 34, was caught sexually assaulting the boy on camera by CCTV installed at his parents’ home.



She will now spend more than eight years behind bars after pleading guilty to 12 child sex offences in court.

Prosecutors described the abuse as a “nightmare without end”, adding that the “highly vulnerable” victim will likely suffer lifelong impacts.



Craig admitted to sexually abusing the boy between 2024 and 2025, beginning when he was aged 12.

She met the victim when he moved to the area in 2023 and enrolled at a Mandurah school, south of Perth, where she was a music teacher.



He was in a band which Craig supervised and she developed a friendship with his mother and family.

When the boy enrolled at a different school Craig maintained contact, driving him to school and even having a key to his home.

Prosecutor Mark Nicol told the court the victim’s mother trusted Craig to spend time with her son alone.

He said she used her position as a teacher to manipulate the boy and get him to respond to her.



“She pressured him about contact with girls, told him to be loyal and prioritise her over anyone else,” he said.

The court heard that some of the abuse occurred while they were alone at his house and one time Craig let herself into the home with a key.

She even sent photos and images of herself in swimwear and lingerie, exposing her breasts, to the child.

In May last year Craig, who had a young son, told a friend that she wanted another baby and fell pregnant to the boy that month, just after he turned 13.



The twisted teacher sent a child a series of disturbing messages in November that year.

She asked him to make her “feel loved” and said she was “sick of begging” for his “attention”.

Craig was arrested in December 2025 after the victim’s mum installed CCTV at the family home and found footage of Craig sexually abusing her son.

The mum immediately reported it to police, and Craig was arrested that day — just weeks before the baby was born.

On Tuesday, Craig pleaded guilty to child sex offences including sexual penetration of a child under 13, procuring a child to engage in sexual behaviour and possession of child exploitation material.



The Mandurah teacher wiped away tears as Judge John Prior handed down his sentence of eight and a half years.

Craig will be eligible for parole after serving six-and-a-half years.

As the judge detailed the offences he said it was likely there were other acts that had not resulted in charges.

The court heard the baby was likely to spend about a year with Craig in prison.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Craig, who was on maternity leave at the time of her arrest, grew up in Mandurah and previously worked as a private music teacher.



Craig was handed a lifetime restraining order to protect her victim and was placed on the sex offender register.

News.title: I spent 5 days on nuclear sub where sailors may not even be told if their parents die – but at least there’s bingo night
News.content:
Next

SPEEDING through the choppy Strait of Gibraltar on a Royal Navy rib, the grey hulk of submarine HMS Tireless suddenly loomed from the depths.

Three miles from land, the rib slowed down in the foaming waves and a knotted rope was lobbed from the huntrer-killer sub’s hatch.





Clambering onboard, the steel door heaved shut above our heads, blotting out the last rays of natural light.

Amid the gloom a voice barked, “diving now” as the sub slowly descended thousands of feet into the murky ocean waters.

Cocooned inside the 278ft nuclear-powered sub, Sun photographer Lee Thompson and I had tasted our last fresh air until we reached Plymouth five days later.

On Sunday HMS Vengeance returned to HM Naval Base Clyde in Faslane after its 140-strong crew spent a record-breaking 217 days submerged on patrol.

I got just a small taste of submariners’ life but afterwards was full of admiration for the fortitude and mental resilience displayed by the so-called Silent Service.

So what’s like living below the waves?

In May 2011 I shared HMS Tireless with 120 men – women were banned from serving as submariners until December that year – after they had been ten months at sea and were heading back to base.

After hitching a ride on the sub off Gibraltar, we squeezed past crew in the vessel’s tight corridors, descending on steel ladders through cramped hatches and into the bowels of the sub.





If you’re claustrophobic, it would be a nightmare.

In the “bomb shop” storage area we were assigned our tiny bunks with a menacing 23ft Spearfish torpedo to snuggle up to at night.

The £1.8m weapon – bearing the warning Danger, Keep Clear, Do Not Touch – is capable of sinking an aircraft carrier.

With a smile, we were told to raise the alarm if it began leaking chemicals.

Our bunks were considered luxurious by some.

The lower-ranking sailors – called ratings – slept in two-feet high “racks” piled in three tiers with a small curtain for privacy.

Some “hot bunk” – share beds – working shifts of six hours on, six off.

Able Seaman Duane Probert, then 23, commando crawled into his tiny rack sandwiched between two others.



The dad, originally from Aberdare, south Wales, said: “I get spots and cold sores down here which I don’t on land.

“I suppose it’s the lack of light.”

Duane could hear the slightest movement around him.

There were no secrets or privacy.

Able Seaman Martin Harvey, then 22, from Poole, Dorset, on the bunk above, told me how he would finally have his family Christmas when Tireless reached Britain.

Martin said: “Mum and Dad have a turkey ready and my presents to open.

“Then it’s my Easter eggs for dessert.”

It was impossible to tell if it was night or day inside the sub.

Underwater, there was no TV or radio, no internet, no mobiles, no windows and no smoking.

Alcohol is allowed but most leave it for “jollies” on shore leave.



Joining the crew on the mess deck for meals, they liked to laugh along to tapes of Fawlty Towers.

Drinking-water and oxygen were produced on board from seawater.

The smell onboard was a stale fug of sweat and damp towels.

When Tireless was on operations, showers were rationed because water production makes noise that could be detected by enemies.

Able Seaman Probert cheerfully admitted he once went four weeks without a shower, washing in a sink with baby wipes instead.

Lieutenant Commander Chris Layton, then 34, originally from Morpeth, Northumberland, said: “Showers are rationed to one every three or four days.

“First we soap ourselves up, then we dip under the shower for a few seconds.

“We call a long shower a Hollywood.”



We’d joined Tireless after the crew had completed an arduous ten-month Indian Ocean deployment.

Three submariners had become fathers while at sea – and six relationships had end.

Those that completed the full tour had missed the 2010 World Cup final in South Africa, Christmas, the Prince William and Kate’s April 2011 wedding and Osama Bin Laden’s death.

I brought them some back copies of The Sun so that they could catch up with the news they’d missed.

It is up to the captain’s discretion what bad news they reveal.

For example, news of a miscarriage might be shared because the lack of

baby updates would become obvious.

But often deaths of parents are withheld.

Bristling with listening devices, Tireless, launched in 1984 before being decommissioned in 2014, was expert at fighting terrorism, piracy, drug running and dropping special forces into combat zones undetected.

On her way back through the Mediterranean, she delivered a deadly payload of Tomahawk cruise missiles to a base.

Submariners have their own slang.



Food is scran, a drink a wet, a skimmer is anyone in the Navy on a surface ship.

The crew worked a seven-day week.

Meals which were excellent – act like a calendar.

Friday is fish night, Saturdays steaks, Sundays pizza, Wednesdays curry.

Dripping sweat in the galley, Leading Chef Mark Hamilton, then 40, and two ratings prepare Sunday roast for 120.

The jovial dad said: “Morale revolves around the food.

“If you get one meal wrong the whole sub talks about it for weeks. Submariners say, ‘There are 120 chefs on board and three idiots in the galley’.”

The sub came up to periscope level every day to pick up signals from ashore, including an exchange of emails, a brief news summary and the football scores.



I watched Newcastle fan Mark, from Northallerton, North Yorks, scour the results posted outside the galley.

He said: “One of the lads messed around with the results and had Newcastle going 25 points clear in the table. B.

“They were really mid-division.”

Their 35,000-mile deployment – equivalent to nearly one and-a-half times around the world – saw 54,000 rashers of bacon, 16,800 eggs, 16 tons of potatoes and 33,160 sausages eaten.

Work was relentless and sleep was often limited to five-hour stretches.

Spare time was filled with bingo sessions, watching DVDs and playing on games consoles.

Life aboard seemed calm.

Any tensions were taken out on the punch bag or rowing machine.

But marriage breakdown is an occupational hazard.

One submariner told me his husband had “ended it by phone when we came ashore.



“We had been separated too long.”

Another said his two young children and wife wrote him 35 letters before he left, adding: “I open one a week on board.

“It keeps me going.”

An officer added: “The financial rewards and job satisfaction are great but you have to put your life on hold.”

He told how he’d been at sea when his daughter started school and college.

As we finally reached the English Channel the outer hatch was opened and crisp, fresh air rushed in.

My ears popped as the pressure adjusted.

Waving on the jetty and Devonport, Plymouth, with tearful spouses and children as the unsung heroes of the Silent Service emerged blinking in the sunlight.

News.title: Putin humiliated as section of £3bn Crimea Bridge COLLAPSES after second blitz in 24 hours & drones swarm Moscow
News.content:
Next

VLADIMIR Putin’s £3billion Crimea Bridge has partially collapsed after it was blitzed twice in 24 hours.

A giant 745ft-wide arch and a chunk of roadway on the 11-mile crossing collapsed into the water after an incredible missile and drone onslaught, images show.



It marks a humiliating blow for Putin who personally inaugurated the bridge in 2018 – four years after his invasion of the peninsula.

The targeted strike formed part of an overnight operation that saw Ukraine unleash a record number of drones across Russia.



Mikhail Razvozhayev, the Putin-appointed “governor” of naval port Sevastopol, said: “The Ukrainian Armed Forces once again attacked the Crimean Bridge.”

Kremlin officials ordered people in Crimea not to attempt to travel to the mainland on the road and rail crossing.



The collapse of the bridge has blocked the route for shipping between the Black and Azov seas in another blow to Putin.



Two Putin puppet officials confirmed the second strike on Tuesday.

In the first attack on Monday, the arch on the road crossing appeared twisted out of position after a drone strike.

Ukrainian war commentator Denys Kazanskyi said: “Under wartime conditions, it is practically impossible to repair the Crimean bridge.



“Floating cranes are needed, but in the current situation, they would not be able to operate and would be destroyed by drones, as shipping in that area is virtually paralysed.”

Russian pro-war sources were left outraged at the failure of air defences for the bridge – with 100 strikes on the crossing in 24 hours.

Kazanskyi said: “It was believed that the bridge was reliably protected. In reality, nothing worked.”

If the Crimean Bridge is fully disabled it will be a huge embarrassment for Putin as he flies to China for a meeting with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping.

The crossing was seen as a key symbol of Putin’s illegal invasion of the territory in 2014 which annexed Crimea to Russia.



Ukraine has attacked Crimea Bridge three times since the start of the war, with major strikes in October 2022, July 2023 and June 2025.

Repeated blitzes have left the protected structure weakened, but it has so far remained open as a key lifeline supply route to the seized peninsula.

As well as striking the bridge, Kyiv launched thousands of drones and four Flamingo long-distance missiles at Russia in a relentless 24-hour operation.



According to Russian figures, the overnight salvo saw the largest number of drones unleashed by Ukraine since the start of the war.

The Russian defence ministry said it destroyed 1,441 Ukrainian drones overnight over 22 different regions in the country.

Around 800 flew towards the capital alone, Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin said.

The latest round of tit-for-tat strikes comes after US, Ukrainian and European officials held talks on ways to facilitate “direct engagement” between Russia and Europe to end the war.

Russia also targeted two bridges in overnight strikes, hitting the North and South crossings in Ukrainian capital Kyiv with ballistic missiles.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The missiles hit Kyiv’s Northern and Southern bridges spanning the Dnipro River, Klitschko said, adding that water and power supplies had been disrupted.

President Volodymyr Zelensky had earlier warned that Moscow might launch further strikes on the country on Monday night.

News.title: Masked attacker still on the run after broad-daylight rape on popular UK walking trail – as arrested man cleared by cops
News.content:
TRAIL TERROR Masked attacker still on the run after broad-daylight rape on popular UK walking trail – as arrested man cleared by cops







Next

A MASKED man who allegedly raped a woman in a sick broad daylight attack at a popular walking spot is still on the run.

It comes days after cops arrested a 53-year-old bloke in connection with the horror incident on Thursday, November 12.



The force has now confirmed the man has now been eliminated from the investigation and faces no further action.

Detectives are continuing to hunt for the suspect following the horrific rape on the Trans Pennine Trail.



The woman was reportedly attacked on Wednesday, November 4, near Harlington Road and Furlong Road.

An investigation was swiftly launched, with officers following multiple lines of enquiry in a bid to identify the attacker.

The victim was able to describe her alleged attacker as tall and stocky.

She said he was wearing a dark jumper, black gloves and a black face covering.



Detective Inspector Helen Hughes, the senior investigating officer, said the attack has caused concern in the local community.

She is calling for anybody with information to get in touch to help them catch the offender.

“Our priorities remain clear – finding the person responsible and securing justice for the woman at the heart of this case,” she said.

“She has been informed of this latest update and continues to be supported by officers.

“Detectives continue to explore all investigative opportunities available to identify the man responsible and bring him to justice.



“We are continuing to do everything we can to identify the suspect, who the victim has been able to describe as a man of a tall and stocky build, who was wearing a dark jumper, black gloves and a black face covering.

“If you believe you have further relevant information or footage which could help us achieve this and further our investigation, then I would urge you to please get in contact with us.”

Anyone with information is urged to get in touch, quoting incident number 550 of 4 November 2026.

News.title: UK weather: Met Office snow warning begins as 100s of homes without power
News.content:
The Met Office has issued a yellow weather warning for snow this morning, while hundreds of homes have been left without power in Greater Manchester

Heavy snow is falling in Yorkshire as a weather warning comes into effect for areas across the UK. The Met Office issued the yellow warning for snow, starting at 12am on Tuesday (November 17).

It is in force until 11am. It covers the Scottish Borders, most of north west England, parts of Yorkshire, and parts of the Midlands. Flurries have been spotted in West Yorkshire, with one video from the village of Kirkburton, near Huddersfield, showing large flakes falling. Hundreds of properties in Greater Manchester have been hit by power cuts.

There have also been reports of snow in Stoke-on-Trent, Staffordshire. Drivers and commuters are being urged to plan ahead for their morning journeys as the roads and railways could be affected by the adverse conditions.

News.title: Dachshund reunited with owner six years after being snatched
News.content:
Dachshund reunited with owner six years after being snatched

Greta the Dachshund vanished in 2020, snatched at midnight but has finally been reunited with her amazed owners, who had lost all hope after year of searching

View 3 Images Greta is happy to be home (Image: Supplied)

A stolen Dachshund called Greta has been found and reunited with her delighted owner — SIX years after she was snatched.

‌



‌



The seven-year-old black-and-tan smooth-haired dachshund finally got to go home after she was picked up as a stray in Widnes, Cheshire.

‌



Keri Arbel, 54, from Shropshire, told The Mirror of her amazement when a dog’s home in Shropshire got in touch last week to say they had found her pet which had been stolen in 2020.

‌



Speaking while Greta sits on her lap, she told how she feared the reunion would never happen but said: “I was so shocked. I was a bit numb really for the first 24 hours. I thought I’d never see her again.

“My biggest fear was if I would have a connection with her and would she have one with me? That was a little bit scary. But as soon as I saw her it all just disappeared straight away."

View 3 Images Keri Arbel was in shock when she was told her missing Dachshund had been found after six years

‌



Terminally ill dying in fuel poverty too scared to turn on heating or lights READ MORE :

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

'It’s marvelous to have her home'

Keri added: “When she saw me she looked really happy and started wagging her tail, the staff said it was the first time she’d wagged her tail. She sat on my lap for an hour and a half and showed me her belly to be tickled.

‌



“It’s marvelous to have her home. She’s a darling, it’s like she’s never been away! “

Four dogs are stolen a day on average according to insurance data, with an estimated 1,626 dogs taken across the UK in 2025. Analysis of police data by Direct Line pet insurance last year found that more than 25,000 dogs in the past 11 years have been stolen - with popular breeds like French Bulldogs, Staffies and Dachshunds the most targeted.

‌



Keri had three of her pet dogs taken in 2020 from a caravan in Keri’s garden where they had been put to settle into their new life after being rescued from Hungary.

She explained how Greta, now seven, Emily-Rose and Nancy were all stolen together just before midnight by thieves in a white builders’ van. Nancy was found four weeks later.

‌



The mum-of-three, who is now a licensed breeder, explained that sadly another of her dog’s called Emily-Rose, also a Dachshund, is still missing.

Keri told how over the years she had been so desperate to find her pets she was scammed by cruel hoaxers demanding up to £2,000 cash. They sent messages via WhatsApp to the number on the missing posters, warning ‘If you don’t pay up you will never see them again.”

‌



View 3 Images Greta and Nancy reunited and now snuggling up together (Image: Supplied)

Keri reveals heartbreaking ordeal

One claimed the dogs were in Ireland and another said to leave £2,000 on a bench and they would leave the dogs tied up. It was like a ransom.” The money was taken but the dogs were not returned.

‌



“Looking back I was so desperate and clinging onto hope, that’s why I paid the money. Police were like they couldn't be bothered ‘it was just dogs!’.”

Gran Keri explained how the search for her pets has been “draining" telling The Mirror: "I went through quite a lot of different emotions, at the beginning I used to cry all the time blaming myself and then I got angry. It completely overtook my life. It was draining, exhausting. But the support I received was immense."

‌



She explained how she had rescued the dogs from Hungary but they had never been in a house before so were 'stressed' by their new environment. The three rescues were kept in a heated caravan while they settled.

“Then one dreaded night about midnight, I was startled by this horrendous scream, and I remember thinking ‘My God what was that? I went out and found the caravan door and it was really warped, when I looked inside they were gone .

‌



“We could see the van pull off and the dogs were just screaming. My husband and daughter’s boyfriend jumped into the car but they just vanished out of sight and the search began. The posters were everywhere but it was like they’d vanished and had been teleported.”

She explained about four weeks later police found Nancy, also in Widnes, at a travellers site, tied up to a shed and they thought ‘she looked out of place’. They’d shaved all her coat off.

‌



“Runcorn police had found Nancy. That was lovely and gave me a boost of hope and thought 'right the other two have to be close'. I knew they would be used for breeding, they were the in-dogs at the time. “

But sadly the years passed and still no sign until last week, while she was at the hairdressers she had several missed calls from unknown numbers. She called one back and Cheshire Dogs home told her they had found Greta wandering the streets outside Manchester.”

‌



'I never understand why they take people’s dogs'

They said a family with a child had been in touch, claiming the dog was called ‘Girly’ and would she consider letting them have her as they had owned her for a year after buying her from drug dealers.

“That was a big red flag but I said I would meet them first. But when I got there and saw she was skin and bone, there was no way I was letting them have her back. Her claws were extremely long too. I said ‘she’s coming home with me’, she was so skinny, you should never see their spine. She’s an old girl now, god knows what she’s been through. She’d been bred from a lot.”

‌



Now Greta spends her days content and snuggled up wtih Nancy on a fluffy donut bed.

“She’s settled in amazingly, but she is a very glutinous eater, so we have to feed on her own but her coat is starting to shine, she’s on raw feed now.

‌



“There’s not an aggressive bone in her. I never understand why they take people’s dogs, they are just sad humans.”

Keri was helped over the years by the Muddypawscrime Facebook group. Co-founder Karen Field, 67, says they currently have 80 missing pets they are appealing for but added: "This has been our longest missing dog case.

‌



“We had a message and it was Keri to say that ‘Greta’ has been found. I was over the moon. We do this day in and day out and we see some terrible things and to actually see one come back after so long it gives others so much hope.

“We do a lot of comfort support with these families because they go through hell.”

“It shows the importance of checking the microchip is up to date and the stolen alert is still on there and your proper name and dress and telephone. If you move house you need to change it. Now we need to find Emily-Rose.”

UK snow forecast as Met Office says wintry weather will soon make way for rain

Snow is set to continue over the mountain tops of Scotland and North Pennines, but Met Office weather forecasters say it should disappear elsewhere as the day progresses

View 3 Images Met Office outlook at 8.45am this morning (Image: Met Office)

The snow is set to melt away today as it turns back to rain.

‌



‌



Parts of England and southern Scotland woke up to a light scattering this morning, with 3cm recorded at RAF Spadeadam, Cumbria. But wintry scenes will quickly wash away this morning as rain sweeps in.

‌



Snow will continue to fall over the mountain tops of Scotland and North Pennines, with 5-10cm expected by the end of play. A Met Office yellow warning for snow remains in place until 11am, and some areas could see some localised disruption.

‌



The Met Office’s Dan Suri said: “Through Tuesday morning the snow will increasingly turn back to rain, with some minor surface-water impacts also possible.

View 3 Images A UK Health Security Agency yellow cold-health alert is in force until Thursday (Image: Owen Humphreys/Press Association)

"Away from higher ground, and so for many people, rain rather than snow will be the main story, although it will continue to feel cold in the north. Temperatures will be closer to average further south, before more settled conditions gradually develop here late this week.”

‌



A UK Health Security Agency yellow cold-health alert is in force for the North West, North East and Yorkshire and the Humber until Thursday morning. Today and Wednesday will remain unsettled.

View 3 Images Rain will dominate for many today (Image: Met Office )

Rain will affect central and northern parts of the UK, while the south will see heavy and blustery showers, with the potential for hail and thunderstorms. Fog is also possible in Northern Ireland on Wednesday morning and across parts of England and Wales on Thursday morning.

Towards the end of the week, drier but colder conditions will gradually extend southwards, with overnight frosts becoming more widespread. Friday night could be the coldest night of the week.

‌



There remains uncertainty over the weekend, with the potential for rain to return from the west. Last night’s snowfall was triggered by a band of rain moving northwards which encountered colder air.

News.title: Three flu symptoms you must not confuse with a cold, pharmacist warns
News.content:
Three flu symptoms you must not confuse with a cold, pharmacist warns

Flu symptoms can appear very similar to a common cold, but a pharmacist warns there are three key differences you should not ignore — here is what to watch for and when to call NHS 111

View 3 Images You should contact NHS 111 if you have flu symptoms (Image: Getty)

There are several telltale signs that suggest a nasty cold is on the way, and with the changing seasons it's probable that you or someone close to you will come down with one.

‌



‌



But your symptoms might actually be indicating something more severe, as the boundaries between flu and a common cold are frequently unclear.

‌



Estimates from the UK Health Security Agency suggest 3,798 deaths in England were attributable to flu during the 2025-26 season, making it crucial to understand the key distinctions.

‌



Omar El-Gohary, Superintendent Pharmacist at iQ Doctor, explains that home remedies need reconsidering when dealing with flu, as there's a risk of taking too much medication.

The difference is that a cold usually develops slowly, with symptoms emerging as a sore throat, sneezing, a runny nose and a cough. In contrast, flu often strikes suddenly, leaving you drained, achy and too poorly to continue with daily activities.

View 3 Images There are some at home remedies (Image: Getty)

‌



Ensure our latest health headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as Preferred Source in your Google search settings

It doesn't need to feel like the 'proper flu' to warrant concern, but it's vital to monitor how you're breathing, whether you're able to drink fluids and if your condition appears to be improving or deteriorating.

‌



The most effective way to tackle aches and fever, the pharmacist advises, is to take paracetamol or ibuprofen, which can relieve discomfort and reduce temperature, while following the packet instructions. For a sore throat or cough, a warm lemon and honey drink can help to ease any discomfort for adults.

When dealing with a blocked nose, saline drops or sprays may provide relief, as can appropriate decongestants, which can offer short-term respite. Bear in mind that NHS guidance does advise against using decongestant nasal sprays and drops for more than five days; prolonged use can actually make congestion worse.

‌



View 3 Images There is a key distinction between the cold and flu (Image: Getty)

If you're feeling exhausted, it's recommended you allow yourself as much time and opportunity for rest and sleep as you can, making sure to keep fluids nearby to maintain hydration.

‌



It's crucial to recognise when it's time to stop managing your symptoms at home and get professional medical help. This becomes especially important if your fever or cough gets better then comes back, or simply deteriorates as your condition becomes more difficult to handle.

It is essential to request an urgent GP appointment or get in touch with NHS 111 if you suspect you have flu symptoms, are struggling with shortness of breath, or haven't noticed any improvement after a week.

Article continues below

The specialist advises dialling 999 for any serious breathing difficulty, sudden chest pain, coughing up blood, or if your lips or skin become blue, grey or extremely pale.

Putin humiliated as crucial Kerch Bridge collapses under huge Ukrainian onslaught

A key bridge connecting Russia and occupied Crimea has been critically damaged following a night of intense strikes by Kyiv

View 2 Images The Kerch Bridge, built by Putin after the occupation of Crimea, has been hit in an overnight strike

Vladimir Putin has been humiliated after Ukraine struck a key bridge linking occupied Crimea and Russia.

‌



‌



A section of the Kerch Bridge, also known as the Crimea Bridge, has been destroyed after Ukrainian Flamingo missiles hit overnight on November 17. This comes amid a night of intense strikes by both Kyiv and Moscow targeting infrastructure.

‌



An ex-adviser to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky shared images claiming to be of the partially bridge partially collapsed into the water below.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 2 Images The Kerch Bridge has been hit by Kyiv in the past (pictured in 2022) (Image: Satellite image ©2026 Vantor/AFP via Getty Images)

The video, shared by Anton Gerashchenko, appears to show footage from a camera on the Flamingo missile as it heads towards the crucial bridge and cuts before impact.

‌



Another video, shared by the former-adviser, appears to be from the bridge and shows a fireball as the missile hits. The images and footage seems to show a support arch from the bridge and a section of the road destroyed.

Ukraine's Presidential Sanctions Commissioner, Vladyslav Vlasiuk, in a X post wrote: "Crimean Bridge. Sanctioned."

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Crimea's Moscow-appointed governor, Sergei Aksyonov, confirmed last night that the bridge was no longer in use. In a Telegram post, he wrote: "The enemy has once again attacked the Crimean Bridge. At the moment, traffic has been suspended."

He added: "We ask residents and visitors in Crimea to refrain from traveling toward the bridge and to take these restrictions into account when planning their routes."

The 19km bridge connects Russia's Krasnodar Krai region to the occupied Crimean peninsula over the Kerch Strait. The bridge was built after the peninsula was taken over by Russia in 2014.

‌



The bridge was personally opened by Putin in 2018 and has been the target of repeated Ukrainian attacks in the war sparked by Russia's illegal invasion.

This comes after Russia forces struck two bridges in Ukraine, over the Dnipro River, overnight. There are eight major bridges across the Dnipro that connect the East and West of Kyiv.

‌



The mayor of the Kyiv, Vitali Klitschko, on Telegram said according to "preliminary information, there have been hits on the north and south bridges in ⁠the capital".

He added that the capital of Ukraine had suffered "damage to critical infrastructure systems" as well as disruptions to water and heating. Officials added that some train services, above ground, were damaged as people were told to take cover in defence shelters.

Ukraine also targeted the Kerch Bridge in a series of drone strikes on Monday. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov, yesterday, insisted the attack caused "insignificant damage".

News.title: Oncologist says persistent hiccups could be 'overlooked' cancer sign
News.content:
Oncologist says persistent hiccups could be 'overlooked' cancer sign

Dr Jiri Kubes has explained other symptoms as well

View 3 Images Hiccups could be an early sign (Image: Miladin Pusicic via Getty Images)

Persistent hiccups could be among the lesser-known symptoms associated with a specifc cancer, a specialist has warned, as a new NHS-backed test brings attention to earlier detection.

The warning follows NICE’s publication of draft guidance recommending a simple ‘sponge on a string’ test, which collects cells from the food pipe to help identify Barrett’s oesophagus, a condition that can increase the risk of developing cancer. Final guidance is expected in February 2027.

The test involves swallowing a small capsule containing a compressed sponge attached to a thin string. Once in the stomach, the capsule dissolves and the sponge expands before being gently withdrawn through the mouth, collecting cells from the oesophagus as it passes. These samples are then analysed for abnormal changes, potentially identifying patients who need further investigation without immediately requiring an invasive endoscopy.

Dr Jiri Kubes, radiation oncologist and medical director at Proton Therapy Center in Prague, said the development was a timely reminder that some symptoms of oesophageal cancer can be surprisingly easy to overlook, as people often mistake them for common digestive complaints.

He said: “People often associate oesophageal cancer with difficulty swallowing, but there are other symptoms that can be less obvious. Persistent digestive problems or unusual changes that don’t go away should not automatically be dismissed.”

View 3 Images Dr Jiri Kubes (Image: Proton Therapy Center)

Five cancer symptoms people should not ignore

Hiccups that won’t go away

Ordinary hiccups are rarely anything to worry about, but persistent hiccups can sometimes occur alongside oesophageal cancer. They are unusual as a standalone symptom, so look out for other changes too.

Heartburn that keeps coming back

Frequent heartburn and acid reflux that do not improve with usual treatment should be investigated. Long-term reflux can also be associated with Barrett’s oesophagus, which increases cancer risk.

Feeling as though food is getting stuck

Difficulty swallowing, known as dysphagia, is an important warning sign. It may initially affect solid foods, with some people experiencing pain or discomfort when swallowing.

Losing weight without trying

Unexplained weight loss can be associated with oesophageal cancer, particularly alongside swallowing difficulties or persistent digestive symptoms.

View 3 Images A doctor has explained what to keep an eye on (Image: nicoletaionescu via Getty Images)

A cough or hoarse voice that won’t clear

A persistent cough or lasting change in voice can sometimes occur with the disease. Although there are many possible causes, symptoms that do not improve deserve medical attention.

Why early detection matters

Dr Kubes said: “The important thing is not to assume that every episode of heartburn or hiccups is a sign of cancer. These symptoms are much more commonly caused by other conditions.

“But people should pay attention to changes that are persistent, unusual for them or getting worse. Difficulty swallowing, in particular, should always be investigated.

“Advances in detection are encouraging, but awareness matters too. We want people to seek advice when something does not feel right, rather than waiting until symptoms become difficult to ignore.”

The NHS advises contacting a GP about difficulty swallowing, unexplained weight loss or heartburn on most days for three weeks or more.

News.title: Wetherspoon brings in policy change affecting customers at all UK and Ireland pubs
News.content:
Wetherspoon brings in policy change affecting customers at all UK and Ireland pubs

Many regulars at their local Wetherspoon may not be aware of the change

View 2 Images Wetherspoon is bringing in a new policy across all its venues (Image: Reach plc)

Pub and hospitality chain Wetherspoon has rolled out a change affecting all its locations in the UK and Ireland. The new policy will affect all the group's venues from 2026 onwards.

‌



‌



The pub giant is bringing in an improvement to its services, but some customers may not even realise the change is coming. The company has decided to step up its washroom provision by rolling out a new urinal treatment across all its venues in the UK and Ireland.

‌



New system in place

After a successful trial at 88 pubs, the URIZAP system is now to be used in the gents at all of the group's locations. The cleaning technology is a microbial formulation that eliminates urinal odours and blockages, providing an eco-friendly alternative to harsh chemical cleaners for uric scale and urinal blockages.

‌



Blind woman told to leave Wetherspoon because she didn't have ID for dog

The product works by digesting uric acid build-up without the need for harsh chemicals or manual intervention, and is suitable for all types of urinals. The pub chain published an article in the winter/spring 2026/27 edition of the Wetherspoon News magazine about the lavatories upgrade.

'Fresher for longer'

The group told customers: "URIZAP is suited to high-footfall environments and cuts significantly the need for the strong-smelling chemical cleaners traditionally used in busy venues. The result is a washroom which stays fresher for longer, with proactive (rather than reactive) maintenance, ensuring clean toilets and cisterns before problems get the chance to arise."

‌



The article states that pubs using URIZAP noticed marked reduction in the need for plumbing maintenance visits to sort out urinals. A key benefit is that urinals "don't have to be shut off" during extremely busy periods avoiding the issues this can cause.

Wetherspoon said: "Urinal issues generally demand attention at the worst-possible moments, pulling staff away from serving customers or other duties to deal with issues. URIZAP's continuous action frees staff to focus on other tasks."

‌



View 2 Images Wetherspoon has changed its policies (Image: Getty)

Eco benefits

Adopting the new solution helps towards Wetherspoon's wider sustainability goals, with fewer single-use plastic containers being used in dealing with urinal issues. Switching to URIZAP also means lower chemical volumes getting into the waste water system and less water overall consumption.

Article continues below

Vince Graham, chief executive of Thrive, said: "Wetherspoon leads the way on washroom standards. We're proud that one of Britain's best-known hospitality businesses has chosen URIZAP to take that standard even further, improving facilities for customers and staff."

Wetherspoon confirmed that the solution has been rolled out estate wide, and this was completed in around July 2026. Staff at the 88 trial locations noted improved odours in the toilets, less frequent maintenance issues and that scale build had been removed from the urinal pipework.

News.title: The young people caught up in Britain's Neets crisis
News.content:
Michael, 19, who lives with his dad in the Wirral, says he dropped out of college and spent a year at home after his social anxiety "got really bad". It is "very easy" to fall out of the system, he says, if there is little support available.

Michael's story is not unique. There has been a large rise in anxiety and mental health problems in young people.

About one in five Neets have a mental health condition, according to 2025 data, external from the Department for Education (DfE) - more than double the rate in 2012.

Having signed up for Universal Credit, Michael was put in touch with the Merseyside Youth Association to help him find a job. He says mentors there have helped him improve his mental health, which led to him dropping out of college during his A-levels. He says that left him trapped inside his bedroom.

He says jobs in his area are scarce and those that do come up tend to go to older people with more experience. Michael says he is trapped in the cycle of not having the experience needed to build more.

"Everything is experience, experience, experience - that's the one thing that I always used to hear when going for jobs on my own without the help," he says.

We followed Michael for a day, meeting him after his 05:00 start for a work experience shift at a local supermarket that the Merseyside Youth Association helped him get.

News.title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women
News.content:
The upskirting image that was sent in March 2024 to a woman we are calling Layla should have led to Arter's arrest.

Bail conditions or custody would have prevented him from taking his wife, Rebekah, to Barbados.

On 28 June, Arter rang Rebekah's relatives from the island to tell them she had died.

Rebekah had been escaping an abusive relationship in 2006 when the Met put then-Det Sgt Warren Arter in charge of investigating her former partner.

Arter pursued Rebekah, they began a relationship and he quickly moved in with her.

Her now-adult son, Elliot, says Arter initially made his mum feel "safer" but that his behaviour soon changed.

"He'd say to her: 'Get in the kitchen, make my dinner you slag. Make me a tea you [expletive] bitch,'" Elliot recalls.

Arter would openly watch pornography on his tablet while he was in the living room with her, Elliot says.

He also collected urine from Elliot, claiming he was testing it at the police lab to help the boy's promising football career - but Elliot now suspects it was an effort to hide Arter's drug use.

Watch Panorama: The Predator in the Police on BBC One at 21:00 on Tuesday 17 November (not in Wales or Northern Ireland) or on iPlayer

The inquest into Rebekah's death heard evidence that use of sedatives had become so routine in the home she shared with Arter, that a daily smart-speaker reminder announced "G o'clock" - a reference to the date-rape drug GHB.

In the years before she died, Arter had filmed and distributed videos of his wife being sexually abused. The BBC has seen some of them.

Many show her unconscious or otherwise incapacitated while Arter insults her.

"You should get raped," he says, in one video.

In another, Arter can be heard speaking to a man behind the camera, asking him to be quiet and saying "they go mad otherwise" - suggesting the video was being made for a wider audience.

His crimes were so brazen that he sent abuse videos of Rebekah unsolicited to at least four women he knew.

Two were women whose cases he had investigated - one of them was Layla.

She had met Arter in 2010 after she reported being raped. His exploitation of her continued for more than a decade, up until she reported the upskirting image - which she had deleted - to staff from the IOPC.

Both Layla, and her adult daughter who was with her when she spoke to the IOPC, say she identified the woman in the photo as Rebekah - whom she recognised from previous videos.

The IOPC says the staff member has no record or recollection of being told the identity of the woman in the photo - and it did not have the authority to investigate as Arter was no longer a police officer.

News.title: Cass report author says she does not support draft conversion practices bill
News.content:
The author of the independent review into gender identity services for young people says she doesn't support the current draft bill banning conversion practices - having previously welcomed it.

Baroness Cass said the current wording of the bill risked "serious unintended consequences" for parents of children suffering gender distress, or medical professionals working in that area.

She was speaking at a parliamentary committee scrutinising the bill, which the government said would protect LGBT people in England and Wales.

A government spokesperson said they welcomed her comments and would take all evidence put forward by the committee seriously as they "want to get this ban right".

Conversion practices are generally described as interventions, treatments or activities designed to change or suppress someone's sexual orientation or gender identity.

This can sometimes happen in religious or family settings and can be very distressing for the person at the centre of it.

There have been long-running campaigns in the UK to outlaw such practices, and in its 2024 manifesto, the Labour party promised to introduce a bill banning them.

When the government introduced its draft legislation, external in June this year, Baroness Cass was quoted in the publicity for it, external.

In it, she said: "I am pleased to see that the government is bringing forward legislation which not only gives a clearer definition of what conversion practices are, compared to previous drafts, but also what they are not".

She went on to say she looked forward to the bill receiving further scrutiny before it became law.

But asked at the Draft Conversion Practices Bill committee if she supported the bill's current form, she said simply "no".

Baroness Cass said the increased "polarisation" used in the debate around gender meant people may use the new law in a way that wasn't intended.

The current wording of the bill requires the victim to suffer "serious harm to the individual's physical or mental health, or serious alarm or distress to the individual which has a substantial adverse effect on their usual day-to-day activities."

But Baroness Cass said she worried this wording left open the possibility of "vexatious" complaints that could put therapists working with young gender-distressed people at risk of prosecution.

"If a young person, for example, has been sexually abused, any discussion about it is going to be incredibly triggering.

"But if you can't therapeutically work through it without any reference to it, and that's the problem," she said.

She said that professionals working at the new NHS Gender Dysphoria Clinics were concerned that even complaints processes that didn't result in a prosecution could be damaging.

Baroness Cass also raised concerns about the possible impact the new law could have on families.

She said that, for instance, if a parent stopped a child's money if they thought they might buy a "breast binder or hormones" that this may also fall within the scope of the bill and result in prosecution.

Asked about her apparent support for the bill when it was first published, Baroness Cass said that she was in favour of the idea but hadn't had the time to read the details before the press release was to be published, but went ahead and gave the quote anyway.

When she published her report on gender identity services for young people in 2024, she described conversion practices as "abhorrent". She says she still feels no LGBT people should be subjected to conversion practices.

She told the committee she wants "a bill that protects the people it's supposed to protect, but doesn't accidentally entrap those who you don't want to [entrap]."

The government said: "We want to get this ban right, which is why we have put this draft bill forward for pre-legislative scrutiny.

"We welcome both Baroness Cass's support for taking action to end abusive conversion practices, and her comments on the need for legislation to avoid adverse consequences.

"We will take all evidence put forward by the committee seriously as we move forward in ending almost a decade of delay for LGBT+ people who should never have to suffer abuse in an effort to change who they are."

The committee hearings continue.

News.title: Failed asylum seekers face removal without five-day notice period
News.content:
The government is to change the law so that it no longer has to give failed asylum seekers notice before they are removed from the country.

Currently, people are given five working days' notice but ministers believe this leads to last-minute appeals which delay the process.

Under the new rules, once an asylum claim fails, the Home Office would have six months in which to remove the applicant without telling them in advance.

The move was criticised by the Refugee Council which said: "Removing people at such short notice will cause unnecessary distress and anxiety to people."

Imran Hussain, the director of the refugee charity, said: "The reality is that voluntary removals are far more effective at removing people than enforced returns.

"If you assist people to return with dignity, many will take that option, at far lower cost to the taxpayer."

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood will make the change by amending the Immigration and Asylum Bill which is currently going through Parliament.

The amendment will scrap the notice requirement for those who have exhausted the asylum appeals process.

Instead, the Home Office will have the power to remove people immediately, a power that will remain in place for up to six months.

The Home Office has not said how many additional people it thinks it will be able to remove but has pointed to Denmark where the number of migrants awaiting removal more than halved over five years to under 1,000 after a similar policy was introduced.

The previous government, led by Sir Keir Starmer, had pledged to clear the asylum backlog.

In June 2026, there were 40,168 people waiting for an initial decision on asylum application claims and a further 90,341 waiting for the outcome of an appeal in the courts.

Between July 2025 and June 2026, 38% of asylum decisions led to the applicant being granted refugee status.

Forty percent of all asylum claims come from people who arrived in the UK by small boat.

The remaining 60% of claims are made by people who arrived in the country by other illegal means or who came to the UK legally and subsequently applied for asylum.

Anna Turley, minister for border security and asylum, said: "We are ensuring those migrants who have exhausted their right to appeal can be removed promptly, rather than being given an opportunity to frustrate their legitimate removal from this country.

"This bill will restore order and control to the system, ensuring it is swift and fair."
