News.title: Vance says he will decide 'sometime next year' about 2028 US presidential run
News.content:
US Vice-President JD Vance has said he will make a decision "sometime next year" about whether or not he will run for president in 2028.

In an interview with Fox News, Vance would not provide a timeline on making a determination, but signaled he is not in a hurry to make up his mind.

"I haven't made a decision. We'll figure it out sometime next year," Vance said. When pressed by host Laura Ingraham, he added: "When I make a decision, I'll be all in on whatever that decision is."

The comments came amid growing interest in Vance's next moves in the weeks since voters handed both President Donald Trump and Republicans a resounding defeat in the midterm elections.

People in Vance's orbit who have spoken to the BBC said the November elections did not change the timeline around his decision-making process for 2028. He is expected to run but allies believe he could wait several months to make a final decision.

Speculation about Vance's White House aspirations began the moment President Trump selected him as his 2024 running mate. The pick positioned Vance, who entered the White House as one of the youngest vice-presidents in US history, as the most likely heir to Trump's Make America Great Again (Maga) movement.

But while serving in office, Vance has carefully avoided discussing his own political ambitions.

He kept that up during the midterms, when supporters frequently interrupted his campaign speeches to urge him to run in 2028. Vance's stock response was that Republicans needed to focus on the election at hand in November.

But with the midterms in the rearview mirror, and Republicans eager to move on from their 2026 drubbing, the next election at hand is now the 2028 presidential race.

News.title: UK lost more than it gained from Brexit, Burnham says ahead of EU summit
News.content:
The prime minister has argued the UK has lost more than it has gained from leaving the European Union in a speech ahead of a UK-EU summit later this week.

Speaking at the Lord Mayor's Banquet on Monday, Andy Burnham compared the UK's Brexit deal to the "emperor's new clothes" - saying "a needlessly hard Brexit" created barriers for businesses and the promise to "take back control" was not delivered.

He is due to sign new agreements on food, energy and youth mobility with the bloc at Friday's summit, after the substance of those deals was set by his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer.

The Conservatives have said Labour are "dragging us into the European Union via the back door".

In his first major speech on foreign policy, the prime minister said that following the summit he would begin new discussions with the EU about options for "our long-term relationship".

However, he warned it would take time and insisted that "at every stage the British people will be the boss".

Burnham has ruled out major changes before the next general election.

On the UK's current relationship with EU, Burnham said: "It's like the emperor's new clothes â where no-one is prepared to say the obvious truth. Well, I say it as I see it. And to be frank, the emperor has nothing on.

"The Brexit we were given has not worked. We have lost more than we have gained."

Ahead of Friday's UK-EU summit, Burnham set out three tests for any agreement.

Firstly, that it must be consistent with Labour's 2024 general election manifesto pledge that there would be "no return to the single market, the customs union, or freedom of movement".

He also said it must improve the original Brexit deal and bring it closer to what people thought they were voting for in 2016.

Finally, he said any deal must pass the "Makerfield test" of providing tangible improvements to people's everyday lives - a reference to voters in Burnham's Greater Manchester constituency.

He also said the prospect of a new deal is a "win-win" and illustrates a "new approach".

"Not adversarial. No longer burning bridges. But being constructive and positive - showing that we can come together to confront shared challenges."

Burnham said "Britain was back in the game in a big way" and would be a country that "leads with its values".

News.title: Russell Brand prison message 'appalling' and being investigated, No 10 says
News.content:
A message by Russell Brand to his followers in which he claimed innocence for his sexual offences was "clearly appalling" and is being urgently investigated, Downing Street has said.

The comedian is currently serving a 10-and-half-year prison sentence after being convicted of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

His wife Laura read out a message from him on their Sunday Service show on YouTube, in which the convicted rapist claimed: "I am not guilty of the offences I have been jailed for."

No 10 said it expects action to be taken if Brand is found to have broken prison rules.

Justice Secretary Alex Norris said the broadcast of a statement from Russell Brand is "completely unacceptable".

In a post on X, Norris wrote: "Prisoners are rightly banned from making statements that cause distress to victims.

"This is being urgently investigated, and I expect action to be taken if he is found to have broken the rules."

In the couple's podcast, released on Sunday, Laura Brand can be seen sitting on a sofa and is holding a Bible with a candle burning in front of her.

Relaying the message from her husband, Laura Brand said the comedian - who is currently being held at HMP Littlehey in Cambridgeshire - called prison staff "strong", "kind" and "dedicated", and asked people to support his "treasured wife and family".

She said she had been speaking to him and he "is OK and is praying".

Brand has positioned himself as a Christian influencer, and has a large following among believers, including in the US.

Asked about the message, the prime minister's official spokesman said: "Prisoners are strictly banned from making statements that cause distress to victims and speaking to the media is only permitted in exceptional circumstances.

"Prisoners cannot get around these rules by having someone else publish their comments."

Speaking earlier, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband told Sky News: "His crimes are heinous and awful. I think it's revolting, by the way, that he shows no remorse today in his comments."

"No remorse, no sympathy for the victims. Just disgusting comments," he added.

Victims' commissioner for London Andrea Simon said the claims will "certainly retraumatise his victims and other survivors of rape who have to hear it".

Speaking on BBC Radio 4's Today programme, she added: "The victims during the sentencing hearing highlighted how his denials and ongoing media fame over two decades had added to their pain and trauma.

"The fact survivors are still having to hear this now is really problematic and very concerning that we can't do more to protect them from it."

While freedom of expression allows convicted sex offenders such as Brand to profess their innocence, Simon said terms of service of media platforms should regulate "the way in which they get their message out".

She added that prison rules should also be reviewed to "bar those convicted of sending messages to be broadcast" unless permission is granted by the prison governor.

If Brand is found to have broken prison rules, possible punishments enforceable by prison governors can result in restrictions on social visits or loss of privileges such as access to additional time in the gym or loss of TV.

Governors can also impose proportionate restrictions on communications where justified.

This could include blocking specific phone numbers, increased monitoring of calls or restricting contact with individuals where necessary to protect victims or maintain prison security.

News.title: Emma Barnett to leave Radio 4's Today for new BBC show
News.content:
Radio 4 presenter Emma Barnett is set to leave the Today programme this week for a multiplatform new BBC show in the New Year.

Former Woman's Hour host Barnett has developed a "bold" new show, she says, which will launch in 2027 across BBC Sounds, BBC iPlayer and YouTube.

Her final day presenting Radio 4's flagship morning news and current affairs show will be on Wednesday 18 November.

"For the last nearly six years - it's been incredible to talk to the mighty Radio 4 listeners," she said in a statement. "Having proudly hosted Woman's Hour and now the Today Programme - I've had the rare pleasure of hosting nearly every hour of the morning on this truly unique and special radio network."

She added: "But it's not goodbye to the BBC audience I value so greatly because I have something else for them that I hope will add something meaningful and entertaining to their lives."

Posting on Instagram, external, she said there would be more information on what her new show would be about soon.

"Watch this space and look ready. I amâ¦ More soon."

Barnett joined Today in May 2024, taking over from Martha Kearney to work alongside fellow presenters Anna Foster, Nick Robinson and Justin Webb, as well as Mishal Husain and Amol Rajan who have also since left.

Today programme editor Rebecca Keating said Barnett had brought "enormous energy" to Today, with "a keen focus" on listeners.

She noted how Barnett had a proven "track record of telling stories of personal hardship that influence public debate" but how she was "also equally at home interviewing British icons like Dame Judi Dench.

"We will miss her generous tea making and wish her every success in her new venture."

In August, Barnett, 41, revealed she had had a hysterectomy and surgery for endometriosis, days before a documentary she made about the condition was broadcast.

She returned to the Today programme explaining she had been absent in recent weeks because she was in hospital "in a case of life imitating work".

Speaking on her BBC podcast, Ready to Talk with Emma Barnett, last year, she told listeners that finding out she was going through perimenopause at the age of 38 felt like she had been "mugged, robbed".

The broadcaster said it was the "first time in my life I haven't really wanted to be a woman - it's the first time I've thought, I'd really quite like to be a bloke".

Radio 4 controller Mohit Bakaya said he was "delighted she's staying with the BBC" and would "look forward to her new show."

News.title: Barristers must stop using rape myths in trials, justice secretary says
News.content:
Brand was sentenced to 10-and-a-half years in prison for one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

Winter said to the court "not one of them [Brand's accusers] resisted or screamed or even tried to leave".

Winter also asked the jury if they could be sure that out of the "many, many women" Brand had had sex with over a decade, "he raped just three of them".

Norris wrote in his letter to the BSB: "[The board] must send a strong signal to the profession on the harm arising from rape myths, and that the perpetuation of such myths within a court room is unacceptable, just as they are unacceptable in our society at large."

The charity Rape Crisis says it is "really common for people who experience rape, sexual assault, sexual abuse or other types of sexual violence to find they can't move or speak".

The judge presiding over Brand's case was praised by the Criminal Bar Association and campaign groups for comments he made during his sentencing remarks to dispel rape myths.

Mr Justice Bennathan told Southwark Crown Court: "Whatever women wear, wherever they go, indeed whatever they drink, they retain the right to say no and to demand justice from the criminal courts when sexual predators like you, Russell Brand, act without their consent."

A spokesperson for the BSB said such cases "must be decided on the basis of the evidence and not prejudice", adding: "Any other approach may discourage others from coming forward and adversely affect public confidence in the criminal justice system more widely."

Kirsty Brimelow KC, chair of the Bar Council of England and Wales which is part of the group examining the need for further training, said it was important for the BSB to remain "independent of the government".

She told BBC Radio 4's Woman's Hour that a "regulatory gap" had not been made clear to her and there were already powers to discipline barristers if breaches of the code of conduct happen.

She said training for "vulnerable witnesses" was already undertaken but it could be "problematic" if it was made mandatory.

Brimelow said there were currently a lack of barristers defending cases of rape and sexual assault and the possibility of further compulsory training could see more pushed out.

"What I wouldn't like to see is publicity around one case to take a life of its own rather than looking at what we already do," she told the BBC.

A spokesperson for the Ministry of Justice said the justice secretary was "determined to make protections for victims as strong as possible".

"Rape myths have absolutely no place in our courts, giving evidence in cases of this nature is a brave act and can be traumatic for victims: they must never feel as though they are the ones on trial," the spokesperson said.

"Independent judges are already able to, and do, give directions to counter rape myths but we always want to keep looking at ways we can improve how the entire justice system treats victims of sexual violence."

News.title: Women's criminal records wiped for abortion offences
News.content:
Ms Packer, who was 41 at the time, took pills called mifepristone and misoprostol, which were prescribed over the phone due to Covid restrictions, to end a pregnancy in 2020.

Prosecutors alleged that she knew she had been pregnant for more than 10 weeks, which she denied.

Jurors deliberated for more than six hours to reach their unanimous verdict, clearing her name.

Speaking with the BBC and Nicola's consent, her friend Ms Tumbridge said the whole incident was "incredibly traumatic".

"Nicky had what's known as a cryptic pregnancy - that's when you don't have any sign of a pregnancy, no baby bump, no other symptoms.

"She thought she was just a few weeks pregnant and she sought an abortion and was prescribed that by the NHS. Unfortunately, she was a lot more far gone."

Nicola experienced a stillbirth and went to hospital. The staff there called the police.

"She was arrested. She spent a time in her hospital room recovering with two police officers present, one was a man. She was treated appallingly. She was made to use the toilet with the door open in front of the police officers."

It took five years of investigations for a trial to eventually find her not guilty.

"Of course, by that point the damage had been done," says Tumbridge, "and she'll live with that trauma for the rest of her life."

At the time, The Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists said Nicola's trial demonstrated "just how outdated and harmful" that law was.

It is now no longer a criminal offence for a pregnant woman to terminate her own pregnancy at any stage.

News.title: Mystery of 2,000-year-old bog body solved in 'first of its kind' investigation
News.content:
For more than 2,000 years, the remains of an Iron Age woman laid undiscovered in bogland - her story unlikely to ever be told.

But when archaeologists unearthed human bones in 2023, it led to an unprecedented effort in Northern Ireland to find out who they belonged to - and what had happened to that person.

Now a coroner's investigation has been held at the Ulster Museum in Belfast to establish the truth behind the Ballymacombs More Woman.

It has establish that she was between 15 to 22 years old when she died - and that she suffered a deliberate decapitation, most likely inflicted from behind with a bladed weapon.

The discovery of her remains near Bellaghy, County Londonderry, marked an important moment, according to Hannah Crowdy, head of curatorial at National Museums NI (NMNI).

"Finds like this that are women are incredibly rare," she told BBC News NI. "She's the first of her kind in Northern Ireland at all.

News.title: UK budget leaves NI underfunded, O'Dowd says
News.content:
Northern Ireland's public funding has worsened relative to the rest of the UK as a result of the Westminster budget, Stormont's finance minister has claimed.

John O'Dowd said the Treasury's figures show that NI will now be funded below its objective "level of need" next year and the year after.

Needs-based funding recognises that it costs more to deliver public services in some parts of the UK compared to others.

The Secretary of State Sir Chris Bryant has offered Â£1.5bn over the next three years and said if Stormont ministers accept this, that will take funding comfortably above the level of need.

O'Dowd said: "Treasury's own assessment shows that we are underfunded, relative to our current estimate of need, in 2027/28 and 2028/29.

"My officials' analysis also indicates that we are underfunded this year, and therefore in each year of the Spending Review."

It is understood O'Dowd believes that in cash terms this means public services will be underfunded by around Â£450m over the next three years.

It comes as executive ministers held further talks about the budget deadlock on Monday afternoon at Stormont Castle.

News.title: Police officers lied about searches connected to fatal crash, hearing told
News.content:
By the evening of Saturday, 3 March, the families of the three young women "were so worried that they decided to report them missing to Gwent Police", having been unable to contact them for hours and noting their lack of presence on social media

Ross's mother, Claire Ross, and Russon's father, Nathan Russon, went to Newport central police station to report their children missing.

The panel was told logs were created at this time which would help with subsequent enquiries.

During this time, Smith's mother, Emma Borg, had gone to the caravan the young people had travelled to and found her daughter's handbag there but no sign of the group.

Morley told the hearing that the "people in the caravan weren't particularly helpful", making Smith's mother realise that "something was very wrong".

Smith was eventually reported missing by her sister Lauren Doyle a couple of hours later, which included "sensitive information" adding overall to what was described as a "very worrying set of circumstances".

He added that the force also received "some concerning information about the men that was added to the system" which he said he would not read out in public.

The hearing was told that PC Hardwick and PC Livingstone were on a 16:00 to 03:00 shift and were given the "straightforward task of attending two home addresses to take any details from family members and to search".

Morley said this was something that "should always happen" during a missing person's enquiry and was "common sense" - allowing officers to assess whether the missing person might actually be at home, might have left something of importance behind like a note or might have taken something of importance.

The panel heard PC Livingstone had been assigned the search of Smith's house and PC Hardwick that of Russon's, but the two officers went to both addresses together and when they returned filled in the relevant paperwork.

PC Livingstone said she had first spoken to Smith's brother and then her mother.

In relation to the search, the following was written down: "Nothing missing out of the usual.

"Mum and Dad was concerned and Mum believed she went out in the same clothes and has not taken any new clothes with her."

That, the panel were told, was a "dishonest and misleading entry".

News.title: Doubles star Henry Patten calls out ATP chairman for not attending world No 1 ceremony
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

British doubles star Henry Patten has criticised the ATP Tour leadership for failing to attend a trophy ceremony at the season-ending ATP Finals, amid a long-running dispute over the future of the sport.

Patten and his partner Harri Heliovaara were presented with a trophy for finishing the year as doubles world No 1 by chief tour officer Andre Silva, but ATP chairman Andrea Gaudenzi and chief executive Eno Polo were conspicuously absent. Gaudenzi later attended a separate ceremony to hand year-end singles No 1 Alexander Zverev his trophy.

Patten said: “For us, it's a really big deal. It's a real shame that the ATP chairman and CEO don't think the same.

“It would have been nice to have them on court with us today, but here we are by ourselves.”

Patten and Heliovaara rose to the No 1 ranking for the first time during the Paris Masters after an excellent year in which they claimed a second Wimbledon title, their third grand slam together, as well the ATP 1000 tournament in Madrid and titles in Adelaide, Doha, and Dubai.

They are also aiming to defend their ATP Finals title, making a winning start to the round robin in Turin after beating Orlando Luz and Rafael Matos in a match tie-break on Sunday.

Patten has previously been vocal in his criticism of how doubles players are treated by the Tour, including over controversial proposals to reduce their prize money, reallocating around £15m to singles players, and slim down doubles draws in 2028.

The 31-year-old said at Wimbledon this year, amid a spat with the Tour over its lack of promotion on social media of its doubles stars: “The reality is you need to win a slam or be in the final of a slam to be anywhere near their Instagram page. I don’t see why they couldn’t promote eight guys [in the semi-finals].

“They have these odd narratives like, ‘no one watches doubles,’ but Wimbledon have done a pretty good job of selling out crowds for doubles this week on every court."

“You should be aiming for your tournaments to be as successful as these, so I would love to see them change their mindset with the doubles. I would love them to see it as an opportunity for growth alongside the singles, but we’ll see.”

Of the proposals, which were presented at an ATP Council meeting in July, Patten said: “We need to get in front of board members, the CEO and the chairman. We need to sit down and talk to them. We’re tired of the discussions going on behind closed doors and the players having to react to that. It is not good enough.”

Patten and former Wimbledon mixed doubles champion Sam Verbeek were instrumental in writing an open letter to the Tour, which was signed by more than a hundred players including Heliovaara, calling for the plans to be scrapped.

News.title: Some UK investment projects ‘abandoned’ amid high business costs, Ikea says
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Ikea has said it “abandoned” some UK investment plans due to the business environment and higher costs in the country.

The company also said it came under pressure from a “challenging” environment and “weakened” consumer confidence over the past year.

UK boss David McCabe told the Press Association that the furniture and homeware giant has been continuing to invest in the UK but has faced higher costs following recent budgets.

He said: “Companies like Ikea are looking at incredibly high costs and an increasingly complex operating environment.

“We believe the UK is definitely a market for investment and have recently invested in eight new units in the UK.

“But there are higher costs and complexities here, and it has meant that we have had investment projects in the UK that we have had to abandon, and that is a shame.”

Ikea said that “structural cost pressures” in the region would weigh on investment opportunities and competitiveness in the wide retail sector.

The boss stressed that Andy Burnham’s Government “missed an opportunity to back retailers” at the latest autumn Budget last month.

It came as Ikea reported that UK retail edged 0.5% higher to £2.26 billion for the year to August 2026.

The company had seen revenues rise 4.7% over the first four months of the financial year but saw sales dip in the second half of the year.

The company highlighted that “sustained pressure on household budgets” led to weak sentiment among consumers, knocking demand for big ticket items and more expensive product lines.

Mr McCabe added: “There’s no doubt it continues to be a challenging period for people and a challenging retail environment.

“But we are optimistic – we are seeing people coming into our stores and enthusiastic for the festive period.”

The company invested £54 million in August to help reduce prices, focusing on affordability to help support sales in the face of the tough consumer backdrop.

Ikea has also benefited from its continued expansion across UK, opening sites in London Oxford Street, Brighton, Norwich and York last year, followed a small-format store in Chester.

It also opened a plan and order site in Dundee, as well as one in Aberdeen last month.

News.title: Imran Khan appeals to Pakistan’s top judges for urgent medical care: ‘Give me justice before it is too late’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Jailed former prime minister Imran Khan has made an urgent appeal seeking medical treatment for himself and his wife, telling Pakistan’s top judges that “the system has stopped giving me justice”.

In an open letter delivered by his legal team, Mr Khan said his blood pressure had spiked dramatically, with medical professionals warning he faced the danger of cardiac arrest or a brain haemorrhage. Yet, he claimed, authorities hadn’t complied with a previous court ruling directing his transfer to a hospital in Islamabad.

“I will only remain able to prove my innocence if I stay alive,” he said.

The letter, addressed to judges of the country’s top courts and released by Mr Khan’s lawyer Salman Safdar and his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party, stated that his wife, Bushra Bibi, required further eye surgery to prevent permanent loss of sight.

The former premier has been jailed since 2023 following a corruption conviction. He was ousted from power through an April 2022 parliamentary vote of no confidence that he later accused the country’s powerful military of orchestrating at the behest of the US.

His wife is likewise serving a prison sentence on corruption charges.

In spite of his legal troubles, Mr Khan remains a prominent political figure. The PTI says the charges against Mr Khan and his wife are politically motivated and the party is actively campaigning for their freedom.

open image in gallery Supporters of Imran Khan's party take part in a protest marches ( Reuters )

In his letter from jail, Mr Khan said he did not face a criminal case for 70 years while he served “the nation on the cricket field, in social work and philanthropy and as its 22nd prime minister”. But then came an “unprecedented and ruthless campaign of political victimisation: countless prosecutions, more than a hundred appearances before the courts, pre-arrest bail sought again and again, an assassination attempt”.

Through it all, he said, he chose the path of law, with every relief reinforcing his faith “that justice would prevail”. Later, he said, “that relief became narrow, and then it closed off”.

“It grieves me deeply to say that, when I needed it most, the system I had placed my trust in did not come to my aid.”

open image in gallery Imran Khan’s sisters Aleema Khanum, Uzma Khanum and Noreen Niazi walk with supporters during a protest over concerns about their brother's health ( Reuters )

Earlier this year, Mr Safdar told the Supreme Court that Mr Khan had lost almost 85 per cent of vision in his right eye. Government officials denied the claim at the time.

One of Mr Khan’s sisters later noted his eyesight had significantly improved following treatment.

In his letter, the former leader accused the jail administration of “acting vindictively” and isolating him. He claimed he had been allowed to meet his counsel only four times, and his wife just once, in violation of laws, leaving them “unable to defend” themselves in the cases they were fighting.

Being held in “prolonged solitary confinement” had taken a toll on his mental health, Mr Khan said, with a medical board recording anxiety, and advising him “frequent contact with my wife and family, reading material, and television”.

The advice, he claimed, had not been followed. The purpose of his prolonged isolation, he said, was to “make me ill and to break my will”.

Raising concerns about his wife’s well-being, he said that after a complicated eye surgery that was done in secrecy in April, she was sent back to solitary confinement.

When he met her this month, “she could neither bear the light nor open her eyes, and without another surgery she may lose her sight permanently”.

“This unrelenting state is taking me to a place from which I may not return alive,” Mr Khan wrote.

“I have fought impossible legal battles in countless cases and I have not stopped. But the system has stopped giving me justice,” he rued, adding that his constitutional rights were brazenly and blatantly violated.

open image in gallery Supporters of Imran Khan take part in a protest march in Lakki Marwat of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on 4 October 2026 ( AFP/Getty )

Federal minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry rejected Mr Khan’s assertions, maintaining that he was receiving regular medical care.

Posting on X, Mr Chaudhry stated that Mr Khan had been taken to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences in Islamabad on eight separate occasions for examinations, with tests showing satisfactory health and blood pressure.

Mr Chaudhry added that the jailed leader received meals of his choice as well as access to books and television and that the state was fulfilling its legal duties regarding prisoner welfare and medical care for every inmate.

Mr Khan’s letter came days after prison authorities allowed a visit by his legal representatives. "Today, I ask only that my wife and I be treated," he said in the letter to the judges. "I appeal to Your Lordships, on the most basic grounds of human compassion: give me justice before it is too late.”

The government of prime minister Shehbaz Sharif has maintained that Mr Khan isn’t held under executive orders, but as a "convicted prisoner". It has also denied that he is held in solitary confinement or denied contact with relatives, claiming that he has received more than 900 visits since 2023.

Speaking about Mr Khan’s letter, a close aide said the jailed leader’s were “not simply requests for special treatment”.

“They concern basic medical care, access to family and legal counsel, and compliance with judicial orders,” Zulfikar Bukhari said.

“Political disagreements and criminal proceedings cannot diminish a prisoner’s right to medical treatment, humane conditions and due process.”

News.title: UK unemployment rate unexpectedly drops as job vacancies fall further
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The UK's unemployment rate has unexpectedly dropped to its lowest point in over a year, despite a continued steep reduction in available job vacancies.

Data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) indicates that the jobless rate decreased to 4.6 per cent for the three months through to September, down from 4.7 per cent recorded in the preceding three-month period.

This represents the lowest level since April 2025, defying widespread forecasts among economists who had expected the rate to hold steady.

Nonetheless, vacancies fell by 22,000 over the quarter down to 690,000, marking the largest quarterly drop recorded since June 2025.

Payroll employee numbers also experienced a steep reduction, falling by 34,000 in October to 30.2 million, though these provisional figures remain subject to revision.

The ONS reported that growth in regular earnings slowed to 3.5 per cent in the three months to September, down from 3.7 per cent previously, though it continued to be outstripped by Consumer Prices Index (CPI) inflation, up 0.4 per cent in real terms.

The release of the data arrives as a long-anticipated report on youth unemployment by former Labour health secretary Alan Milburn is published on Tuesday, setting out significant reforms to address the expanding numbers of young people across the UK not in education, employment or training – referred to as Neets.

open image in gallery How the UK employment rate has changed in recent years

The ONS figures showed unemployment among 16-24 year-olds eased back to 15.1 per cent in the latest three months, but that the inactivity rate for those not in work or full-time education remained high at 20.8 per cent.

Liz McKeown, ONS director of economic statistics, said it was a “mixed picture overall”.

She added the drop in vacancies was “concentrated in smaller businesses, which report that increased labour and operating costs are affecting their hiring decisions”.

“Meanwhile, regular wage growth slowed, driven by a fall in public sector wage growth, as the recent impact from the timing of pay awards has started to drop out of the numbers,” she said.

Martin Beck, chief economist at WPI Strategy, said the numbers showed that outside of the pandemic years, vacancies were now at their lowest level since 2014.

He said: “The problem isn’t that businesses are firing workers. It’s that they’re increasingly reluctant to hire them.”

open image in gallery The data comes as a long-awaited report into youth unemployment by former Labour health secretary Alan Milburn is being published ( PA )

He said this “raises further questions about the wisdom of government policies that have made employing people more expensive and potentially more burdensome, notably higher employer National Insurance contributions and expanded employment rights”.

He also warned against the Bank of England raising interest rates further after this month’s hike from 3.75 per cent to 4 per cent, which he said could badly impact the jobs market.

He said: “The danger now is that policymakers become so preoccupied with preventing another inflation shock that they overlook the damage being done to employment and growth.

“With hiring weak, wage pressures easing and energy prices retreating, another rate rise would risk turning a prolonged jobs market slowdown into something altogether more serious.”

News.title: ‘The God Father’ of Mexican drug trafficking: Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo dies aged 80
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Notorious Mexican drug lord Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo has died in a hospital in the western city of Guadalajara aged 80.

Known as ‘The Godfather’ and the ‘Boss of Bosses’, Félix Gallardo was one of the founders of the Guadalajara cartel, and is considered to be one of the biggest drug smugglers in history.

The Jalisco state security department said in a statement that he died on Sunday at 2 pm local time due to multiple organ failure.

open image in gallery Félix Gallardo had been in hospital since Friday ( Reuters )

The 80-year-old kingpin had been hospitalised since Friday, when he was rushed from Puente Grande, a maximum-security prison complex.

He had been held at the prison since 1989, and was serving a combined 77-year prison sentence for drug trafficking offenses and for the 1985 killing of US Drug Enforcement Administration agent Enrique “Kiki” Camarena.

Together with Rafael Caro Quintero and Ernesto Fonseca Carrillo, Félix Gallardo founded the Guadalajara cartel, also known as The Federation, in the late 1970s.

The cartel dominated drug trafficking in Mexico during the 1980s cocaine boom, entering into partnership with the Colombian cartels like Escobar’s Medellín Cartel to pool production in the Andes with Mexican transportation across the border into the US.

It is reported that at one point, an estimated 80 per cent of all cocaine that entered the US came from the Medellín Cartel.

open image in gallery Félix Gallardo was serving a combined 77-year prison sentence ( Reuters )

However, the Guadalajara cartel eventually splintered into several criminal organisations in the country’s north, including the Sinaloa cartel.

All three founders were convicted in Mexico in connection with Camarena’s killing.

The DEA agent was kidnapped and tortured before his body was found in 1985.

Caro Quintero was released on procedural grounds in 2013, but was recaptured in July 2022.

In February 2025 he was extradited to the United States along with 28 other prisoners wanted by US authorities on drug-related charges.

Félix Gallardo had sought house arrest since 2019, citing his advanced age and deteriorating health.

While courts initially rejected his requests, in September 2022, a judge granted him house arrest, but the order was never carried out because of legal challenges by Mexico’s federal attorney general’s office.

News.title: Gerwyn Price clarifies controversial checkout in Grand Slam of Darts win: ‘I didn’t know’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Gerwyn Price maintains he had no idea he won a leg at the Grand Slam of Darts after a controversial checkout in which he went bust.

The Welshman beat Sebastian Bialecki 5-2 to book his place in the knockout stage on Monday night in Wolverhampton. But controversy emerged in the Group E match when Price hit a 145 checkout, though the problem was he had 135 remaining in the fourth leg of the match.

‘The Iceman' was unsure what his actual number left with two darts in hand, clarifying with referee Charlie Corstophine, who told him he only needed 88, though in fact he needed 78.

Price would hit T16 and D20 to, in his mind, check out and win the leg, but after later setting up a last 16 clash with Ryan Searle, the 41-year-old insisted the miscount was a complete accident.

"I didn't know until I just walked in,” Price said.

“I hit the first treble and I asked what I'd got left and he said 88. So I went treble 16 double top and he said game shot.

“I did ask him in the throw what I had next. I swear to god I didn't know until I cam back here! I'm glad I didn't know, because it probably would have played on my mind.”

Price also confirmed he is not a fan of the new format, which has seen only group winners advance and surprise early exits for Ross Smith, Jonny Clayton and Luke Woodhouse.

"I prefer the old one [format], obviously. I've had some good memories here. You can slip up once, but in this one you can't,” Price said.

"As you can see, a couple of good boys have gone, and they probably thought they'd have a second chance. But once you lose a game, that's it; you're gone."

News.title: Pope forgives person who nailed him in the eye with a rosary in Peru
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Pope Leo XIV has forgiven the person who threw a rosary at him before his final Mass in Peru and nailed him in the eye, saying it was merely a sign of the person’s profound faith.

Leo got hit during a popemobile ride Monday through the estimated 1.5 million people who had flooded a Lima air base for the service. Leo grimaced and touched his eye but proceeded as if nothing had happened.

During an in-flight press conference en route home, a Peruvian reporter apologized for the incident. Leo, who lived in Peru for two decades and has Peruvian citizenship, brushed it off as merely someone trying to get close to the pope.

And he also joked about it.

“The nice thing about Peruvians, including the person who with a lot of faith simply wanted to offer me a rosary, are things you carry in your heart – or maybe in your eye – but that mark the life of someone,” he said.

“It tells you that here truly there is enthusiasm. Here there is profound faith. Here there is a desire to receive the blessing of the Lord,” he said.

People often toss rosaries, stuffed animals, sports jerseys and other items toward the pope when he is in the popemobile and he has often wowed crowds with his quick reflexes and ability to catch them. His bodyguards, however, say these tossed items are some of their biggest security concerns when he’s out in public.

News.title: Wall Street slides as Nvidia casts shadow over tech stocks
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. Asian stocks fell sharply at the start of a huge week for AI following the shock exit of Nvidia boss Jensen Huang over a string of extramarital affairs.

South Korea’s tech-heavy Kospi fell 3.6pc and Japan’s Nikkei 225 dropped 2.4pc after another night of drama for the $4tn (£3tn) chip giant.

Just hours after Scott Bessent, the US treasury secretary, called for a “dramatic shake-up” at Nvidia , it emerged Mr Huang was considering a possible comeback.

Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, the boss of Epic Games, were among prominent figures to sign a public letter demanding that Nvidia “bring Jensen back”.

Meanwhile, several unnamed tech executives set up a “war room” to coordinate a “Stand With Jensen” campaign, according to The Financial Times.

The Wall Street Journal also reported overnight that Nvidia could be looking to scale back some of the aggressive financing it has deployed to prop up other AI companies.

Mohit Kumar, an economist at Jefferies said: “These concerns are more real and are likely to have an impact on a number of companies in the supply chain.”

Taiwan’s Taiex, a beneficiary of the global AI frenzy, sank 6pc, with shares of its leading chipmaker TSMC down 5.7pc.

Allies in Silicon Valley, including Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, the boss of Epic Games, have pushed for Mr Huang’s reinstatement at Nvidia despite an ongoing investigation into his conduct by the company’s board.

The chip giant will unveil its latest quarterly results on Tuesday after triggering a wave of turmoil for the tech sector.

AI giant Anthropic is expected to list in New York this week with a valuation of $1.4tn, doing so at a time when valuations are coming under pressure.

By Monday morning, several major AI supplies had suffered a drop in their share price, with chipmakers SK Hynix and Samsung down 4.3pc and 4.5pc, respectively.

OpenAI investor SoftBank Group also slipped 3.7pc, while memory maker Kioxia dropped 7.7pc. Chip equipment maker Tokyo Electron was also down 7.1pc.

Jim Reid, an analyst at Deutsche Bank, said: “Nvidia’s results tomorrow may outweigh everything and will largely put a bow on a bumper earnings season in what has been a bumpy period for markets.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

What happened overnight

Asian stocks mostly fell Monday as the tech sector struggled to recover from the crisis at Nvidia after boss Jensen Huang stepped down.

Mr Huang, a pivotal figure in the artificial intelligence boom, resigned Thursday following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

The 63-year-old’s departure raised concerns about the chip titan, which is at the centre of a build-out that has helped propel global markets to record highs and boosted economic growth around the world.

Reports that Mr Huang was in talks for a spectacular return to the hotseat, did not appear to be having much of an impact in Asia, with Taiwan’s Taiex index plunging 6pc as chip giants TSMC and MediaTek were hammered.

South Korea’s Kospi sank more than 3pc owing to steep losses in SK hynix and Samsung, while Japan’s Nikkei lost more than 2pc with Advantest plunging 11.1pc and Kioxia 7.7pc.

There were also losses in Shanghai, Sydney, Singapore, Bangkok, Manila and Jakarta, though Hong Kong, Mumbai and Wellington rose.

News.title: How an NHS midwife overhauled maternity care in the world’s most dangerous place to give birth
News.content:
In her nearly 20-year career as an NHS midwife, Isata Dumbuya saw only one woman die. But in her first week working in a government maternity hospital in rural Sierra Leone, she witnessed the deaths of four mothers.

Her Sierra Leonean colleagues seemed resigned to such tragedies. Yet for her, these avoidable deaths were a huge shock: they brought home the enormity of her career change, and the challenges she now faced.

She had returned to Sierra Leone to pass on her NHS experience and training, but she had never seen anything like this.

“I did not know what to do – in all my experience,” she recalls. “There were [medical] conditions that I was seeing there that I had never seen in my life because they would not be allowed to happen in the UK.”

After a long and successful career in the UK, the mother-of-five had been inspired to return to her birthplace after seeing reports of the appallingly high mortality rates faced by mothers.

At the time women in Sierra Leone had a one-in-17 lifetime chance of dying during pregnancy, delivery or its aftermath. Today the lifetime risk is one in 52.

She found the government hospital in Kono overwhelmed, short-staffed and poorly organised.

Her new colleagues were exhausted and fatalistic from the relentless deaths.

“In this time, the only thing I was useful for was crying.

“I [had a lot of doubt] because I’m like ‘I can’t do this’. I really don’t know how.

“And also, when you are looking at the people around, they are so fine with it, because they had to do some serious level of emotional shutdown to cope with all this.”

News.title: England stun world champions Spain in one of their greatest victories
News.content:
There was so much to admire. England began the night testing Spain’s first-phase passing to breaking point. They began the second half counter-attacking Spain for two goals from Ezri Konsa and White. Then after Elliot Anderson’s red card, this was a different England. With Trafford in inspired form, they held off the relentless Spain for long enough.

Harry Kane scored his 93rd England goal from the spot and was replaced before the end so that Myles Lewis-Skelly’s energy could give the midfield one more lease of life. By the end, the excitement meant that Kane was unable to take his seat on the bench, and he stood alongside Tuchel in the technical area, cajoling and advising.

England have beaten Spain on Spanish territory in recent times, but it was the nature of this performance, its many qualities when the moment required them, that made it so significant. This was the end of a 43-game unbeaten streak for the European and world champions, and it was ended by an England team in their best form in recent years.

Only three who started this game – Kane, Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice – started the final of Euro 2024, lost to Spain. Tuchel’s pool of talent is deeper than it was for his predecessor but there is also a greater maturity to the way they play. The England manager called it the greatest performance of almost two years in charge “given the circumstances… who we play, where we play” and as ever for England just slightly too late.

The defeat by Argentina in the semi-final in Atlanta just stings that little bit more when one considers the craft and resilience England showed on this night. They were under the hammer after Anderson threw an arm over the shoulder of Lamine Yamal and was dismissed before Mikel Oyarzabal converted the penalty that followed. “Thirty minutes against Spain in Spain feels like three hours,” Tuchel said, although Spain had a long way back after the blitzing they took at times in the first hour.

News.title: Scotland’s ugly win seals weekend of domination for northern hemisphere
News.content:
This was far from pretty. In fact it was downright ugly. If Wales’s historic win over New Zealand on Saturday will be spoken of for generations, this turgid 15-12 victory for Scotland over Australia had probably been forgotten, even by the 65,095 who witnessed it, by the time they caught the tram home. But it capped a spectacular weekend for northern hemisphere rugby.

One should never read too much into results one year out from a World Cup; different conditions, home advantage, different stages in teams’ development cycles, and so on. But it was difficult not to feel at least some encouragement from a weekend in which France ended a five-match losing streak against world champions South Africa in one of the most thrilling Test matches of recent times, Wales ended their All Blacks hoodoo with an epic display of defensive resolve, and Scotland won a grim arm-wrestle against Australia. With England and Ireland thrashing Japan and Fiji respectively, only Italy’s loss in a tight one against Argentina prevented a clean sweep.

It will be interesting to see how the southern hemisphere responds over the next couple of weekends, but you have to say, this new Nations Championship format has breathed a bit of life into the global game. Even if it was in very short supply at Murrayfield on Sunday.

After the barnstorming games in Paris and Cardiff, expectations were high heading into the match, but it proved to be a messy, attritional affair, not helped by a greasy pitch and two teams absolutely desperate for a win. First-half tries from Matt Fagerson and Jack Dempsey put Scotland 12-5 up at half-time, with Harry Potter having replied for the visitors.

News.title: Record-breaking England hammer Australia to force series decider
News.content:
Good morning from Adelaide Oval. For England fans waking up back home, things are a going a little better now than they were in Perth 48 hours ago.

Having been asked to bat first again, they are 102 for one after 18 overs, and going nicely. Tom Banton has made a fine fifty, while Joe Root is doing what he does. You know the drill: look up and he’s on 30, and so on.

The man to go was Ben Duckett, whose tough times in Australia continued, when he picked out a fielder in the offside ring for nine. The ball was short and wide, and the stroke pretty ugly. Anyway, without him, England have managed to build a bit of a platform. The pitch is classic Adelaide, lacking the pace and bounce of Friday in Perth, and it helps that Australia have left out their new find, Mahli Beardman, who is being “managed”.

Naturally, there is also still a lot of chat about sandpaper. David Warner was supposed to be here for Fox but is not, having attended to a family commitment in Sydney last night, according to the station.

More significant, though, was the intervention of Chadd Sayers, a one-cap seamer who was on the sandpaper tour. He is commentating for SEN and has backed Khawaja up strongly. He believes all players knew that sandpaper was being used in two Tests and says there was a 60-90 minute meeting involving all players about taking collective responsibility. Cummins said the opposite.

News.title: Ireland stay in hunt for final place despite complacent display
News.content:
Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of this Nations Championship fifth-round Test between Ireland and Fiji at Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

Ireland are third in the Northern Hemisphere standings, having played a game less than England and France above them, but a point bonus victory this evening would put Andy Farrell’s side level with Steve Borthwick’s men and keep them in the mix for top spot. Meanwhile, Fiji are rock bottom of the South Hemisphere table, with a miserable points difference of -133, and lost 54-17 to France last time out.

Tadhg Beirne, who is poised to captain his country for the first time on home soil this evening, said Ireland are aiming to carry on the positive momentum following their 42-12 win over Argentina eight days ago, but feels his side can still improve. “The big focus for us is to continue building on our performance, particularly from last week,” he remarked.

“We laid down a foundation of how we want to play, but we’re certainly not satisfied with that. I think there were patches of us playing really well there, but there were also patches where we weren’t to the standard that we’re going to hold ourselves to.”

News.title: Botham’s grandson inspires Wales to historic win over All Blacks
News.content:
The second half of Wales’ Nations Championship started with a hard-fought 28-21 bonus point victory over Japan last Saturday. Steve Tandy’s side sit fifth in the Northern Hemisphere table, but just five points separate them from second-place England, and they still have a tonne of pride to play for as they aim to finish as high as possible in the group.

Speaking ahead of the encounter, Tandy said: “We’re excited for the opportunity we have against New Zealand. It was good to get the win last Saturday, but some elements of our execution weren’t where we wanted.

“We have to go up another level this weekend and be more ruthless. We have one of the best teams in the world coming. We want to be better and put in an 80-minute performance.”

Meanwhile, New Zealand arrive in the Welsh capital in imperious form, having won their opening four Nations Championship matches and boasting a +73 points difference. South Africa’s defeat has opened the door for the resurgent All Blacks to pounce, and they’ll be brimming with confidence following their eye-catching 43-21 triumph against Scotland at Murrayfield a week ago.

As for the team news, Tandy has made four alterations to the starting XV that overcame Japan. Taine Basham is poised for his first international appearance since the 2024 Six Nations, while James Botham, Gabriel Hamer-Webb and Adam Beard also begin the contest. The influential Aaron Wainwright is out with a minor calf problem.

All Blacks Head Coach has ordered 10 changes to the 23-man squad that brushed Scotland aside. Forwards including George Bower, Asafo Aumua, Josh Lord, Anton Segner and backs such as Richie Mo’unga, Anton Lienert-Brown and Fehi Fineanganofo all start for the heavily rotated visitors. Full-back Beauden Barrett will captain New Zealand for the first time, in his 149th Test, while Will Jordan is unavailable because of a hamstring issue.

Kick-off is at 14:10, with team news following now.

News.title: Joseph a star in the making as England revel in role of bullies
News.content:
England have made wholesale changes, with only five members from the starting XV against Australia remaining. Henry Pollock starts at eight, Will Joseph earns just his second cap on the wing and Archie McParland is set for his international debut off the bench.

“Japan are a very well-coached side who will challenge us in different ways, and we know we will need to bring intensity throughout the game,” said Borthwick. “The atmosphere at Allianz Stadium last week was incredible. The players really fed off the energy in the stadium, and we are really looking forward to being back on Saturday [today].”

Japan’s first game of this month’s fixtures ended in defeat as they lost 28-21 against Wales in Cardiff last weekend. That defeat means they have just one win from their first four games of the Nations Championship, which came against Italy in the opening game, and they sit second bottom in the southern hemisphere standings.

“We have had really good training to prepare us for the game we are expecting against England,” Jones said. “We had two days of very settled and pretty training but Wednesday was quite dirty. We had to adapt to certain situations and in the end we did it really well. I was really pleased with the players, really pleased with their effort, really pleased with the way they adapted to the situations. I am looking forward to going to Twickenham with this young Japanese team that is going to play the house down.”

Kick-off from Allianz Stadium is at 4.40pm.

Sports.title: Tottenham ‘turned down chance to sign James Trafford in cut-price transfer’ despite ‘loving’ England goalkeeper
Sports.content:
Next

TOTTENHAM rejected the chance to sign James Trafford in 2023 because of his lack of experience.

England‘s new goalkeeping hero joined Burnley in a £19million deal instead, according to former Clarets assistant Craig Bellamy.



Trafford, now 24, starred for the Three Lions in Sunday’s stunning 3-2 Nations League win over world champions Spain and made a superb double late save in Madrid.

Bellamy, who was Vincent Kompany‘s No2 at Turf Moor before he took the Wales job in 2024, revealed: “Traffs had really good loans with Bolton and then he came to us.



“Spurs loved him but they couldn’t buy him to play in the Premier League yet. There’s a difference. You’ve got to earn your stripes.

“They said, “We think you are bold for what you have done.”

“They were right because maybe we wouldn’t have got the goalkeeper.

“We paid a lot of money for him but if we didn’t do it now, we were going to miss him.

“Then you look, were we producing him for someone else because we gave him game time and his exposure?”

Trafford has been an England hero before – at youth level.

Next

MAX DOWMAN was the Young Lions’ late hero as Lee Carsley’s side proved their worth in a HALF-A-BILLION-POUND bout in the South West.

There was nearly £600MILLION worth of talent in both the England and France Under-21 squads on Monday night at Aston Gate, more than THREE times the estimated value of usual occupants Bristol City.



And Arsenal talent Dowman, 16, the man with the biggest reputation, proved England have the best bang for the buck as he won the game on his first ever start for the U21s.

Dowman’s 89th-minute winner added to first-half goals from Mikey Moore and Divin Mubama to outweigh a second-half double from France substitute Giovani Vesini.



France didn’t lose a single match during their Euros qualification process, averaging over three goals per game as they cruised to qualification.

Carsley’s outfit proved too strong in the opening 45 minutes and it took Moore, 19, who was making his first ever start for the U21s, just six minutes to put England ahead.

The Tottenham ace, currently on loan at Koln, was played in by Ethan Nwaneri before he tucked a curling effort into the bottom corner.

Arsenal loanee Nwaneri – currently at Borussia Dortmund – was involved again for the second, delivering a pin-point floated cross to the back post to find Mubama, 22, on the half-hour mark.

Manchester City loanee Mubama – currently at Southampton – judged the flight of the ball perfectly, nodding it back across goal and into the opposite corner to double England’s lead.

But France hit back with 10 minutes to play when Versini’s shot slipped through Tommy Setford’s gloves and into the back of the net as the rain hammered down.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Versini added a second just five minutes later when he curled in a stunning effort from 25 yards out.

But just when it looked like England’s night had been spoiled, up stepped superstar Dowman to save the Young Lions.

The playmaker, who became England U21’s youngest-ever player when he made his debut last week, tapped home a pass from Harrison Armstrong with just over a minute left to play.



Carsley knew that his side had not been tested during their qualification campaign for the Euros, beating the likes of Kazakhstan and Andorra on their way.

But this performance against comparable opposition showed that England might just have the quality to pull off a historic three-peat in the summer when they bid to win their third European Championship in a row, having lifted the title under Carsley in both 2023 and 2025.

On getting the better of France, Carsley said: “What I would say about this squad is, I have got a lot of expectation for them. I think they can really achieve something special.

“France are one of the best teams I have seen so far. I have watched a lot of Germany, Spain and France ahead of the next six months. France are definitely up there with the best teams that I have seen.”

Speaking about Dowman, Moore said: “He is a top kid. You forget how old he is. I was saying on the bench that my little brother is 17, and he feels older to me than my little brother.



“It is weird seeing how well he is doing at such a young age. I think he has been top and everywhere he goes he is taking the next step and he just needs to keep going and keep pushing.”

Sports.title: Man Utd star suffers knee injury days before Mauricio Pochettino set to take charge as manager
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED keeper Karl Darlow has suffered an injury setback ahead of Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival at Old Trafford.

The Wales stopper, 36, skipped training on international duty and is set to miss the Nations League match with Portugal in Cardiff on Tuesday.



Darlow, a summer signing from Leeds on a free transfer, has been back-up to United No1 Senne Lammens this season and made his debut in the Carabao Cup 3-2 loss to Brighton.

Wales boss Craig Bellamy, who started Darlow in a 3-1 defeat to Norway on Saturday, said: “We’ll check on Karl.



“His knee just flared up a little bit.

“He has not been playing on a regular basis so we were aware of that before it.



“We’ve given him as much time to recover.”

Darlow missed the majority of pre-season as well as the last international break which spanned four matches due to the same knee problem.

New United boss Pochettino, who replaces the sacked Michael Carrick, arrives in the UK later this week after USA‘s clash with Haiti in the early hours of Wednesday.

He has already sent some off his staff ahead to get cracking.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Long-time assistants, Jesus Perez and Toni Jimenez, as well as his son, Sebastiano, jetted into Manchester on Sunday.

Assistant coach Miguel D’Agostino and physical trainer Silvia Tuya have remained with the US and will head across the Pond after the game with Haiti.

Pochettino hinted that some of his USA players may wind up joining him at Old Trafford.

He said: “I know that you asked the players before. All good players always have dreams.

“To reach the last level – and I see United is one of the teams that is in the last level – it’s a dream for many of the players.



“But now I see they need to be focusing in today, in tomorrow’s game, in their day clubs.

“I know really well for more than two years every single player and I see they are all players with an unbelievable talent.

“And of course, in the future when that happens, we are going to pay attention.”

Sports.title: Meet forgotten ex-Chelsea star, 51, central to England’s decision to axe Jordan Pickford for James Trafford
Sports.content:

ENGLAND boss Thomas Tuchel has hinted he is planning to change his No1 with James Trafford making a strong case for Jordan Pickford’s place.

But Tuchel, 53, can’t be the only one credited with that decision as he holds the Three Lions’s goalkeeping coach Henrique Hilario‘s opinion in very high regard after their many years working together.



Hilario, 51, spent two years as part of the German tactician’s coaching staff at Chelsea.

And the Portuguese coach followed the ex-Bayern Munich boss at Wembley last year when the latter replaced Gareth Southgate at the helm.



Following the former Paris Saint-Germain boss’ arrival, Pickford, 32, remained England’s undisputed starting goalkeeper all the way until last summer’s World Cup.

But it seems like Hilario has seen something special in Trafford, 24.



The former Borussia Dortmund boss and his goalie coach were impressed with the Leeds star’s shot-stopping abilities but also agreed he is better with the ball at his feet than his Everton counterpart.

That led to the England boss splitting game time with each keeper making three starts in the last six Nations League matches.

However, Trafford appeared to have made a stronger case for the position after a stunning display on Sunday’s historic 3-2 victory against world champions Spain in Madrid.

The ex-Manchester City ace sealed the Furia Roja’s first defeat in two years after a heroic last-gasp double save to deny Fermin Lopez and Aymeric Laporte.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

It seems like Hilario’s instinct has paid off and showed why Tuchel extended their cooperation after a successful stint at Chelsea that saw them winning the Champions League in 2021.

The former goalie signed for the Blues in 2006 from Nacional as third-choice behind Petr Cech and Carlo Cudicini.

And the ex-Portugal international spent almost a decade providing back-up before retiring in 2014 after being part of two FA Cup victories and another two League Cup trophy wins.



Two years after hanging up his gloves, the Porto academy graduate returned to Stamford Bridge under then manager Antonio Conte as assistant goalkeeping coach.

Hilario was then promoted two years later by Maurizio Sarri and remained in that role under Tuchel too.

Sports.title: Man Utd must go all out for stunning £130m Cole Palmer transfer – and axe £300k-a-week Bruno Fernandes to pay for it
Sports.content:
Next

THE new Generalissimo is heading for Old Trafford.

However, no army chief can be assured of success unless his troops truly believe in themselves — and the battle plan.



And in London, the Manchester-born player who has worn two shades of blue is exactly what Mauricio Pochettino needs in his red battalion.

For Pochettino, the key to getting it right will be ridding his dressing room of symbols of the old guard and replacing them with acolytes ready to follow his orders.



That means Ineos, Omar Berrada, Jason Wilcox and the United board giving Poch the tools to do the job, whatever the impact on the “bottom line”.

On making big calls that the merchandising arm of the club might not like…

While getting him out of Chelsea will surely take a British-record fee in excess of £130million, Cole Palmer fits both the Poch playbook and the United DNA.

Apart from anything, he’s a Wythenshawe lad who grew up supporting the Red Devils and idolising Wayne Rooney.

That means a sacrifice — cutting through the noise and the game of contract bluff and telling Bruno Fernandes it is better for all sides for the Portuguese to move on.

Before that, though, new manager Poch and the Old Trafford hierarchy must make it clear to Chelsea’s top brass that they are willing to pay whatever it takes to bring Palmer, 24, back to his home city.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

More of the same will not do for United. It’s what got them in this huge mess in the first place.

When he walks into Carrington on Thursday, Pochettino will inherit a dressing room compiled under SIX different managers.

Luke Shaw, Poch’s one-time teenage “son” at Southampton, was signed by Louis van Gaal, who also gave Marcus Rashford his debut.

Jose Mourinho added Diogo Dalot, while successor Ole Gunnar Solskjaer brought in Harry Maguire and Amad Diallo, as well as Fernandes.

And then it was Erik ten Hag, who landed Mason Mount — Poch let him go as Chelsea chief — Leny Yoro, Matthijs de Ligt, Joshua Zirkzee and Noussair Mazraoui.



That came before a summer splurge in 2025 under Ruben Amorim that saw Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Benjamin Sesko move in.

This summer, with Carrick at the wheel, no left-backs or strikers joined — but Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos arrived in midfield.

All adding up to a side that will travel to Anfield on Sunday in the relegation zone… and potentially rock bottom of the pile.

Radical change, both in personnel and mindset, is required. Tough choices. Big calls.



Fernandes, 32, has been an outstanding player for United since his arrival in 2020 from Sporting.

In addition to 341 appearances and 113 goals, he was part of the sides that won the FA Cup and Carabao Cup.

Fernandes ended last term as Football Writers’ Association Footballer of the Year and winner of the PFA award, too.

Yet the public row with Carrick and last week’s floating of the contract issues were a signal that a parting of the ways would be mutually beneficial.

Especially if United can line up Palmer, who knows exactly what Pochettino demands.



It was the Argentine who gave Palmer his big break, bringing him from an irregular role at Manchester City to a starting one at Stamford Bridge.

In his three-and-a-bit seasons in Pep Guardiola’s squad — learning from a master — Palmer made 37 appearances, just 13 of them starts.

But the attacker signed off with City’s goal in the 2023 Uefa Super Cup shootout win over Sevilla.



His first Chelsea term — working with Poch — brought 40 starts, five games off the bench, 25 club goals and an England debut. The season ended with his strike against Spain in the Euro 2024 final in Berlin.

Pochettino took a gem and honed it, giving Palmer the responsibility and freedom he craved, those hours of running on the training ground at Cobham rewarded.

Those hints and suggestions that Palmer has a hankering for home will not go away.

He can’t go back to City but if United can prise him out of SW6, it would supercharge the atmosphere in and around the club.

Poch would add a world-class talent with a willingness to put in the hard yards.



And he could be a dressing-room disciple — able to articulate the manager’s message, pass it on and explain why it works for everyone.

Chelsea, of course, will not want to lose him.

But they didn’t want to lose Enzo Fernandez, either. And a huge offer on the table might soften that resolve. Money talks.

SPOT ON, TOMMY

IF YOU had been asked to name England’s first-choice back five in the summer, it probably wouldn’t have been: James Trafford, Ben White, Ezri Konsa, Marc Guehi and Lewis Hall.



Things move quickly in football.

Thomas Tuchel’s September promises over what he wants his side to be have been made good.

Watching England hustle, harry and monster Spain for more than an hour on Sunday night was what feel-good football is supposed to be.



Tuchel will never completely shift the shadow of Argentina in Atlanta until he proves he can handle the pressure-cooker situations at Euro 2028.

But something significant is being built. Something substantial. The FA’s faith in Tuchel looks more than justifiable.

HOPE FOR DELE

AT WEMBLEY on Thursday, Harry Kane was rightly feted for his feats for his country.



But just 24 hours earlier, a few miles away, one of the players who emerged alongside the England captain was ploughing a lonely furrow on a field in Chiswick.

Working with a personal coach, Dele Alli found himself surrounded by school matches, rather than the international stage he once strutted.

The hope, a devout one, is that there could yet be a way back for Dele, even if, at 30, it may not be at the very highest level.

He is certainly giving himself the chance.

WEN? NEVER

SO, IN THE END, Arsene Wenger decided he did not want to be football’s standard bearer against Gianni Infantino.



The ex-Arsenal boss considered the idea of running for the Fifa presidency for more than a week before passing on the option, with French FA head Philippe Diallo instead nominated by Uefa ahead of Wednesday’s deadline.

Yet if anyone is going to bring Infantino down, you suspect it will be a US politician, rather than any of football’s movers and shakers.

Democrat Congressman Jamie Raskin has Infantino — and, of course, Donald Trump — in his sights at his expected role as the new head of the House Judicial Committee, with the power to subpoena witnesses to give evidence under oath.



It was the FBI-led raid on Zurich that eventually ended Sepp Blatter’s Fifa reign.

And Raskin could be the weapon Uefa lacks the wherewithal to wield.

GREAT DANE

IT DIDN’T work for Thomas Frank at Tottenham.

A marriage of inconvenience, leading to one of the biggest Danish tragedies since Hamlet.

Spurs fans will be preparing the fusillade they are sure to aim at Frank when they visit Crystal Palace at the end of January.



New Selhurst boss Frank, though, remains a thoroughly decent man and a good manager.

He will show that — and get the Eagles flying again.

PAPER THIN

THE MORE that Cricket Australia attempts to close the Sandpaper-gate scandal down, the worse the cover-up looks.



Pat Cummins denied he had knowledge of the ball-tampering plan after admissions by Usman Khawaja and David Warner.

But those denials were then blown apart by Cape Town 12th man Chadd Sayers.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Trent Bridge for the first Ashes Test in June is going to be a bear-pit.

It could be a summer of hell for the Baggy Greens.

Sports.title: Irish boxer Reeves dies aged 31 following three months in coma
Sports.content:
Lee Reeves underwent surgery after he was knocked out by Gary Cully in August; Limerick native was in medically induced coma until his death following infection; 'Everyone is devastated to learn of the passing of Lee Reeves,’ said promoter Queensberry

Irish boxer Lee Reeves dies aged 31 three months after suffering serious injuries in fight

Lee Reeves (left) has died aged 31, following three months in a coma since suffering injuries in a knockout defeat to Gary Cully

Irish boxer Lee Reeves has died ‌at the age of 31, three months after suffering ‌serious injuries during a fight.

Local media reports in Reeves' hometown of Limerick ​said he underwent surgery ‌after his knockout loss to Gary Cully in ​a junior welterweight bout in August in Dublin and had been in a ​medically induced coma since.

The ⁠reports added that ⁠he had contracted an infection over the weekend which ‌led to his death on Monday.

"Everyone at Queensberry is devastated to learn ‌of the passing of Lee Reeves," the promoters said in a statement. "Lee was an immensely talented boxer, as well ⁠as a true role model ​and inspiration to his community."

Cully ​described Reeves as "a character and ​a gent".

"It's never been nothing love ⁠between us champ, can't really believe I'm writing this but RIP brother," ⁠he wrote on social ​media.

Reeves won 16 of his 18 ​professional bouts, including 11 by knockout.

Jonathan O'Brien, a former coach of Reeves, posted on social media: "Goodbye son, sleep tight, you fought so hard until the end. We love you so much."

Reeves' sister Jessie also paid tribute: "I'll see you on the other side my brother. I've no words for this. I love you endlessly El Champo."

Sports.title: Ravens' season on the brink after loss to struggling Chargers
Sports.content:
Justin Herbert and Omarion Hampton ran for first-half touchdowns as the Los Angeles Chargers earned their first win of the season, manhandling Baltimore at the line of scrimmage in a 23-20 victory over the Ravens on Monday night.

Derrick Henry was held to 10 yards on 10 carries, although he did score two touchdowns as Baltimore (4-6) skidded to its fifth straight loss and by far the most demoralising.

The Chargers (1-8) had lost 11 in a row dating back to last season but they outrushed the Ravens 160-16.

The combined 15 straight losses by the Chargers and Ravens entering the game was a record for a Monday night game.

What is the WTGL?

The WTGL follows on from the success of the Tomorrow's Golf League (TGL), founded by Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy's TMRW Sports, in partnership with the PGA Tour.

The women's edition of the tech-infused golf league will see LPGA Tour stars feature in a unique team format, with five teams (representing five different cities) of five-player rosters confirmed for the inaugural season.

The season-long competition takes place across November and December at the SoFi Center in Florida, a purpose-built indoor venue, with every shot live and all the players mic'd up for the made-for-TV format.

How can I watch the WTGL on Sky Sports?

Both the 2026 and 2027 editions of WTGL will be broadcast exclusively on Sky Sports as part of an expansion of its golf rights, which also includes a further two years of TGL presented by SoFi.

Every match will be exclusively live on Sky Sports Golf, Sky Sports+ or Sky Sports Mix, while repeats will be available the following day on Sky Sports Golf. You can also download the Sky Sports App for news, highlights, scores and reports.
