Sports.title: Matchroom’s Teremoana Title Timetable Starts With Ahio
Sports.content:
Matchroom wants Teremoana Teremoana in a world title shot within 18 months, yet they are still praying Hemi Ahio survives long enough on Wednesday in Melbourne to give their prospect some actual work. You cannot have both without throwing him in against live heavyweights who can hit back.

“Probably coming earlier in his career than we maybe thought,” said Matchroom CEO Frank Smith on the Punch Podcast, discussing the step up against Ahio. “I would say within the next 12 to 18 months, he’s going to be in a position to challenge for a world title. If he carries on on a trajectory he’s going on.”

Going into Wednesday’s 10-rounder for the vacant IBF Intercontinental title, Teremoana already sits at number 15 in the IBF rankings. Winning that regional strap will push him straight toward the top 10, which sounds great on a press release until you look at who he has actually beaten.

His last five opponents lasted an average of 1.2 rounds. On Tuesday, Teremoana tipped the scales 16.7 kilograms heavier than the 36-year-old Ahio while holding a six-inch height advantage. Even though Ahio brings a 25-1 record into Pullman Melbourne Albert Park, oddsmakers have Teremoana as a -1000 favorite to score another stoppage.

If Teremoana blasts Ahio out inside two rounds like everyone expects, Matchroom learns nothing. Nobody finds out if his gas tank holds up past round five, whether his jab stays sharp when he gets tired, or how he reacts when a contender takes his best right hand and fires back.

Climbing the IBF ladder with quick knockouts over regional opposition is easy. Being ready for a real world champion by early 2028 is a completely different story. If Smith is serious about that 18-month clock, Matchroom has to stop protecting his undefeated record and put him in with a top-15 heavyweight who can actually win rounds off him next.

Sports.title: Vito Mielnicki Jr. Passes on Hernández, Targets Zayas
Sports.content:
Vito Mielnicki Jr. wants no part of dangerous Cuban middleweight Yoenli Hernandez right now, and Matchroom Boxing is helping him steer straight toward a much safer commercial target in Xander Zayas instead.

Matchroom CEO Frank Smith confirmed that Mielnicki passed on fighting Hernandez and is already lined up for the undercard of the Jaron Ennis vs. Josh Kelly three-belt unification on February 27 in Atlanta. The plan from there is to match Mielnicki against Zayas next summer.

“He wants to fight Xander Zayas next summer. That’s a fight that we’ve been working on. He was already lined up to have a fight on our undercard of the Boots-Kelly show. That was already planned. And then his focus is to fight Xander next summer,” said Smith on the Punch Podcast.

It is easy to see the business logic behind the move, even if hardcore fans are not going to like it. Hernandez is a big, heavy-handed 160-pounder who has been tearing through opponents and is now negotiating to fight Michael Zerafa for a WBO middleweight title. Mielnicki is ranked No. 2 by the WBO at 160 after beating Austin Williams in September, so the path to Hernandez was wide open if he actually wanted the smoke.

Instead, Mielnicki is pivoting toward Zayas, who just confirmed he is moving up to 160 pounds in early 2027 after getting stopped by Ennis in their junior middleweight unification back in September. Notice the subtle detail in Smith’s pitch. Zayas is no longer a 154-pounder, meaning any summer fight between them will happen at middleweight, where both guys are trying to rebuild or cash in without touching the division’s biggest punchers.

Zayas brings a recognizable name and a built-in New York and New Jersey ticket-selling angle against Mielnicki without carrying anywhere near the physical threat of Hernandez. That is smart matchmaking by Eddie Hearn and Smith, though it tells you plenty about where Mielnicki’s team thinks his ceiling is at 160.

Everything now comes down to who Matchroom puts across from Mielnicki on February 27 at State Farm Arena. If they feed him a soft touch just to keep him busy until summer, fans will see right through the Zayas buildup before the ink is even dry.

Sports.title: Hearn Expects WBA to Enforce Jack Catterall Mandatory
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn sounded like a promoter ready to go to war when he told the WBA they need to do what is right regarding Jack Catterall. That was not polite promoter talk, and Hearn has already warned that he will sue the sanctioning body immediately if they try to let Teofimo Lopez bypass Catterall for a Ryan Garcia fight.

Matchroom has the bankroll to hire top-tier sports litigators, and sanctioning bodies hate getting dragged into courtrooms where internal emails and fee arrangements get exposed. That financial muscle gives Hearn real leverage, especially since Matchroom already holds a written WBA resolution guaranteeing the Catterall and Shakhram Giyasov winner a title shot within 180 days.

The real trouble started because the WBA allowed this situation to drag out instead of putting their foot down from day one. When Lopez captured the WBA welterweight strap, he inherited the mandatory obligations attached to that belt. By stalling and leaving unification loopholes dangling, the organization gave Lopez false hope that he could swerve Catterall and walk straight into a big payday with Garcia.

Hearn knows how fast sanctioning bodies bend when big American money fights are sitting on the table. That is why his warning sounded so pointed, especially after watching Catterall get burned on the scorecards against Josh Taylor in 2022 and see previous mandatory spots vanish into thin air.

“The WBA really need to do what’s right here, and I believe they will,” Hearn said to Mr. Verzace. Coming from a promoter who has already been firing legal notices at the organization since September, that reads like a final notice to enforce the rulebook or face a courtroom battle.

Catterall earned his position the hard way by beating Giyasov in May for the WBA regular belt. If Lopez refuses to take the risk against a tricky southpaw and insists on chasing Garcia next, Hearn is making sure the WBA strips the title immediately rather than letting their champion dodge his mandatory obligation.

Sports.title: Bam Rodriguez Risks Losing Inoue by Fighting Medina
Sports.content:
Trainer Robert Garcia wants Jesse “Bam” Rodriguez to fight WBO bantamweight champion Christian Medina first before facing Naoya Inoue, and that could lead to him losing out on his biggest payday.

Promoter Eddie Hearn already laid out the ultimatum from Inoue’s camp. Inoue wants Rodriguez in Japan in February or March, or he is moving up to featherweight. Once Inoue begins campaigning at 126, he won’t come back down to 122 to fit Bam’s timetable.

Garcia’s logic makes sense on paper if you ignore the calendar. Rodriguez has only had one title fight at 118, and grabbing Medina’s WBO belt would let him unify while getting used to heavier punchers before jumping another four pounds to face the undisputed junior featherweight king.

The problem is that boxing does not wait around for a fighter to take detours. If Rodriguez fights Medina at bantamweight, Inoue will already be settled at featherweight chasing belts against bigger men. Sitting at 118 with two straps means nothing if the superstar you actually want to beat is two divisions above you.

Fans have seen this move too many times when trainers try to overprotect their fighters. Rodriguez (24-0, 17 KOs) is in his prime. Taking one extra fight against Medina will not magically prepare him for the kind of power Inoue brings to the ring at 122.

Hearn knows the window is closing fast and believes Rodriguez wants the smoke immediately. If Garcia insists on Bam playing it safe at bantamweight, he might end up costing his fighter a legacy-defining fight against the pound-for-pound best in the sport.

If Bam loses out on this fight, the backlash from boxing fans and media would be ruthless. And almost all of that heat would land squarely on Robert Garcia’s shoulders. Fans already have zero patience when trainers or promoters let a superstar walk away over a belt unification fight that nobody outside hardcore circles is demanding.

Right now, Inoue is handing Rodriguez a golden ticket directly to an undisputed championship fight and a massive payday in Japan without making him fight a single contender at 122 first. If Garcia passes that up for Medina and Inoue moves to 126, the narrative will immediately turn into Garcia protecting his fighter and costing him a career-defining opportunity.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Sells Fury vs Joshua As Biggest Fight Ever
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn is out there calling Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua on December 11 in Cardiff the biggest fight in British boxing history, and nobody is buying it. Unlike Chris Eubank vs Nigel Benn or Carl Froch vs George Groves II, fans are barely talking about what happens inside the ring.

Instead of breaking down styles, boxing fans are stuck listening to Hearn complain about Dana White being involved and gripe about how terrible the main card undercard looks. Hearn even admitted he has nothing to do with the three main card support bouts and trashed putting unknown heavyweights like Da’Mazion Vanhouter ahead of Welsh two-time world champion Joe Cordina. That tells you everything about where the buzz actually is.

“When we talk about the biggest fight in British boxing history, Rick, it’s not even close,” said Hearn on Rick Reeno’s Mr. Versace podcast.

The energy is missing for a simple reason. This fight needed to happen between 2015 and 2018, or at the latest, when both men held all the heavyweight belts. Back then, fans wanted to see who was truly the top heavyweight in the world.

Since that window closed, both guys took heavy damage. Joshua got stopped by Andy Ruiz Jr. in 2019, lost twice to Oleksandr Usyk, and got blown away by Daniel Dubois. Even in his July comeback against Kristian Prenga in Jeddah, Joshua hit the canvas twice in the first round before pulling out a second-round knockout.

Fury doesn’t look much fresher at 38. After losing back-to-back fights to Usyk, Fury came back in April after more than a year out of the ring and looked old and slow, grinding out a decision over Arslanbek Makhmudov.

Eubank and Benn brought real hatred to the ring, and Froch vs Groves II had fans desperate for answers after a disputed first stoppage. Hearn can count casual Netflix viewers all he wants, yet hardcore fans know this matchup waited way too long.

Sports.title: A Determined Darius Fulghum Defeats Diego Pacheco
Sports.content:
Carson, California – Darius Fulghum had told Matchroom promoter Eddie Hearn and Diego Pacheco that they had made a mistake in choosing him as an opponent, and Saturday night he proved why. Fulghum controlled the inside with his jab and overpowered Pacheco in the clinches. Darius (16-1-1, 13 KOs) used his previous experience as a wrestler to maneuver and control the exchanges during the inside clinches.

At the post-fight press conference, he made note of everyone highlighting how great Diego’s jab was but no one speaking on his jab, saying, “I have a pretty good jab too.” Fulghum outlanded Pacheco in total punches, 197 to 147, landing an efficient 34.3 percent (Compubox).

Diego (26-1, 19 KOs) struggled offensively, being unable to land consistently, only landing a few big shots throughout the fight. He was unable to establish his jab consistently, despite having a four-inch reach advantage. Darius was a man on a mission, determined to redeem himself for his poor showing last November against David Stevens. He was grateful to Golden Boy for giving him a second opportunity at a big fight, saying, “You know the big thing going into the fight tonight, you know, like I said, this exact time last year. November of last year was one of the low points in my life. People wrote me off, you know. Saying he ain’t this and that. He ain’t that good, and I felt it, you know, and I was lost, man. It took those moments to really lock me back into the sport and really prove who I say I am. I’m “DFG,” the greatest. It was my mission to go out there and do my thing. Put my heart on the line. Give every ounce of me in the ring to come out victorious.”

It showed in the ring. Fulghum wanted it more; he was hungry and determined to win and go out on his shield.

All three judges scored it in Darius’ favor: Fernando Villareal and Jack Reiss both had it 115 to 112, and Pam Hayashi scored it 114-113. Hearn agreed with the judges’ scorecards and believes sometimes a loss like this is needed to regroup and become better. He stated that there is a rematch clause, and he believes Diego should exercise his right to it. After the fight, Pacheco said, “It wasn’t my night tonight. I didn’t feel like myself at the beginning, but I guess you get nights like that in boxing. Congratulations to Darius; he did what he had to do, but I would definitely love to run it back.”

Diego now finds himself in the situation Fulghum did last November; a poor performance will bring criticism and naysayers doubting his boxing skills.

How he responds remains to be seen. Darius had a strong showing against Bektemir Melikuziev, outlanding him by a punch 170 to 169 while boxing him on the inside and giving him a bloody nose. After defeating Pacheco, he has to be considered among the best in the division. Oscar De La Hoya posted via Instagram that a world title is next for Darius.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Sees Boots Ennis Fighting Canelo at 168
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn is already trying to cash Jaron Ennis out in a 168-pound fight against Canelo Alvarez before his fighter has even proven himself at 154. Hearn went on Rick Reeno’s Mr. Versace podcast and claimed Ennis would jump straight over the middleweight division if he becomes undisputed at junior middleweight.

“We have a plan with Boots, and we always had that he would go 47, 54, 60, and 68,” Hearn said to Ring Magazine. “So, I know that if Boots became undisputed at 54 and you said to him, ‘Canelo Alvarez for the championship at 68,’ this guy’s a pure competitor. I think he’d be jumping around all over the divisions to be in fights like that.”

That is classic promoter hype designed to rush Ennis into a massive payday without making him fight dangerous guys at 160 first.

Ennis still has to beat Josh Kelly on February 27 in Atlanta with three belts on the line, and Kelly is not exactly a killer. Hearn claims DAZN and PBC will magically have a deal done by fight night so the winner faces Sebastian Fundora for the final strap. Anyone who follows boxing knows how easily deals between rival networks fall apart. Even if Ennis beats Kelly and Fundora, neither guy prepares him for real super middleweights.

Jumping 14 pounds is a massive gamble, even after Terence Crawford pulled it off against Canelo. Ennis looked good beating up Xander Zayas at 154, where he can punish smaller guys for walking in. Doing that against Canelo is a totally different story because Canelo has spent years taking punches from full-sized 168-pounders and light heavyweights. Ennis would be giving up way too much natural size and strength just to chase a big check.

Hearn admitted he still wants to see Ennis fight Vergil Ortiz Jr. at 160 if Ortiz wins a title there. That is the fight fans actually want, and it would show whether Ennis can take a punch from a real banger before moving up again. Skipping middleweight to grab a Canelo lottery ticket looks like a shortcut.

Canelo has his own business to handle at 168, and Ennis has done nothing at super middleweight to earn that spot. Until Ennis beats Kelly, actually gets Fundora in the ring, and proves he belongs with bigger men, all this Canelo talk is pure noise.

Sports.title: Canelo Eyes Willy Hutchinson While Osleys Iglesias Waits
Sports.content:
If Canelo Alvarez stays at 168 pounds for his next fight, IBF champion Osleys Iglesias is clearly the guy he needs to be fighting. Instead, trainer Eddy Reynoso is already floating a move back up to 175 to face newly crowned WBC light heavyweight belt-holder Willy Hutchinson, right after Canelo just recaptured the WBC super middleweight title from Christian Mbilli.

“Yes, without a doubt, Hutchinson is an option for Canelo. We’ll see,” Reynoso told ESPN KnockOut. He claimed he has been watching Hutchinson for several fights and likes Canelo’s chances, with March 2027 being tossed around for the final bout of Canelo’s Riyadh Season contract.

You can see why Reynoso would want this fight. Hutchinson doesn’t possess single-punch power in either hand the way the Cuban Osleys have. So the worst Canelo could fear is getting outboxed for 12 rounds the way Terence Crawford and Floyd Mayweather Jr. did.

Hutchinson just picked up the vacant WBC strap by outpointing Joshua Buatsi earlier this month, and he has already told talkSPORT that Canelo is too small for him. However, the WBC says Hutchinson owes two mandatory defenses, so it is fair to wonder how that fight even gets made without belt politics getting in the way. If Canelo asks the WBC to allow him the opportunity to face Hutchinson first, there’s a chance they’ll grant his request.

Canelo’s track record at 175 tells you everything about why his team might like this route. He stopped a faded Sergey Kovalev in 2019, then got schooled by Dmitry Bivol in 2022. Against Mbilli at 168, Canelo had enough left to get the win, but he fought in brief spurts.

Taking on a bigger, younger champion like 28-year-old Hutchinson gives Canelo a built-in alibi if things go wrong. If he loses at 175, he can point to the weight he was giving up and still get credit for daring to be great.

If he stays at 168 and loses to a dangerous puncher like Iglesias or even Hamzah Sheeraz, there is nowhere to hide. Fans will rake over the coals for losing, especially if it’s against Hamzah. He’s not held in high esteem by many fans for giving up his WBO belt when ordered to face Janibek Alimkhanuly.

If Canelo wants real credit at super middleweight, he should unify against Iglesias instead of picking another low-risk trip up to light heavyweight. As good as Hutchinson looked beating Buatsi in their rematch, he still isn’t widely known by many Americans. They would see him as a cherry pick by Canelo just based on being unfamiliar with Hutchinson.

Ghana News.title: A heritage special
Ghana News.content:
GH¢50 Heritage Series banknote

On the day the government’s 24-hour economy began losing its hours to a “New Economy”, the Bank of Ghana unveiled new money to celebrate our heritage. The finance minister was changing the name of the future while the governor was changing the faces of the past. A full day’s work, even if we can no longer account for all 24 hours.

In Ghana, when a public decision makes no sense, ask who stands to profit. It is not to suggest wrongdoing. It is simply a useful point at which to request the invoice.

What particular anniversary required this celebration? What made it a priority now? The Bank cited security and durability. Fair enough. But why did the Big Six group portrait have to go? Were the gentlemen helping counterfeiters?

Our history is certainly larger than six men. Many others deserve recognition. But a country should be able to enlarge its memory without first conducting an eviction.

The President’s own memory also deserves preservation.

In opposition, Mr Mahama condemned the introduction of GH¢100 and GH¢200 notes. Why introduce higher denominations when Ghana was heading towards a cashless economy? Now he has unveiled redesigned versions of those same notes. Of course, introducing denominations and redesigning them are different exercises, but his enthusiasm deserves an explanation.

Apparently, the road to a cashless economy passes through a printing press, provided one is travelling in a presidential convoy.

Then came the history lesson.

The Bank said the woman on the GH¢50 note is Theodosia Okoh. Her nephew disputed the likeness. The Bank explains that photographs were combined and her familiar head-tie replaced with a hairstyle, producing a resemblance to her sister. I call this national gaslighting: the portrait needs correcting, but the public is being asked to adjust its eyesight. Eii!!!

We invited Theodosia Okoh onto our currency, sent her to the makeup salon, and are now asking the family to identify who came out.

The woman who gave us our unmistakable flag has been honoured with a face that requires a press release.

Then there is the Zimbabwean model whose image appears in the market scene on the GH¢1 note. She visited Makola once and ended up on our currency. Generations of Ghanaian market women must wonder why nobody mentioned this opportunity.

The Big Six have lost their group portrait, while a visitor has secured a place in our national imagery. Our heritage is evidently more accessible to tourists than we realised.

One hopes the Tourism Authority is taking notes: “Visit Ghana. You may leave as legal tender.”

Presiding over this exercise is a Governor whose criminal charges were withdrawn by the Attorney-General. That is not to suggest wrongdoing. It certainly does not relieve him of the duty to account. The questions about this exercise cannot also be withdrawn by a nolle prosequi.

How much did it cost? Who received the contracts? Who researched the images? Who approved the designs? When did the work begin, and what explains the timetable?

Surely the portraits could have been checked with a little more diligence before they were presented to us. It is generally cheaper to correct a photograph before printing money around it.

But perhaps this is the heritage we are celebrating: launch first, answer questions later, and issue a press release when somebody notices the mistakes.

We have certainly preserved that tradition.

A comedy of errors indeed! But before we applaud, let us see the bill.

Kwaku Sei

Ghana News.title: FIFA immortalises Caleb Yirenkyi’s torn Black Stars jersey at World Cup museum
Ghana News.content:
FIFA has immortalised Caleb Yirenkyi’s torn Black Stars jersey from the 2026 FIFA World Cup, preserving a piece of Ghanaian football history at its museum in Zurich, Switzerland.

The jersey was damaged during Ghana’s opening match against Panama, in which the midfielder scored a dramatic last-minute winner to secure a 1-0 victory.

Yirenkyi’s match-worn shirt is expected to become part of the FIFA Museum’s permanent collection, where it will be preserved for historical purposes and future generations.

The gesture recognises a memorable moment from Ghana’s campaign at the first 48-team edition of the World Cup.

OFFICIAL: FIFA Museum has immortalized Caleb Yirenkyi’s Black Stars kit which got ripped off during the World Cup in North America. The World Football Governing body has kept the shirt in a special wardrobe for Historic reasons as it also serves as a one of the monumental factors which will remind the world about its first ever 48-team World Cup campaign. — Rahman osman (@iamrahmanosman) November 15, 2026

The jersey also joins other significant football memorabilia, including the shirt worn by former Black Stars captain Asamoah Gyan during Ghana’s 2010 World Cup campaign in South Africa.

Gyan’s jersey documents one of the most heartbreaking moments in Ghanaian football history, when he missed a last-minute penalty against Uruguay in the quarter-finals before the Black Stars lost in the subsequent shootout.

The Black Stars finished third in Group L with four points after a 1–0 win over Panama, a goalless draw with England and a defeat in their final group game.

Ghana’s campaign ended on July 4 in Kansas City following a narrow 1–0 Round of 32 loss to Colombia, with Jhon Arias scoring the winner in the 14th minute.

The Black Stars finished as Africa’s fifth-best team, recording one win, one draw and two defeats.

Ghana News.title: Ghana’s Maxwell Woledzi named MLS Defender of the Year
Ghana News.content:
Nashville SC center back Maxwell Woledzi was named the 2026 Major League Soccer Defender of the ​Year on Monday.

In his first season ‌in the league, the 25-year-old from Ghana helped Nashville set MLS records for clean sheets (17) and ​fewest goals allowed in a 34-game ​season (25).

Woledzi contributed two goals and one assist ⁠in 34 matches to help Nashville ​win the Supporters' Shield and set additional MLS ​marks for points (77), wins (23) and fewest losses (three). He led the team in clearances (44) and completed passes (2,100) and ​was third on the squad in ​aerial duels won (80).

Woledzi was the only player in the ‌league ⁠to complete more than 2,000 passes with at least 94% passing accuracy.

Teammates Jeisson Palacios and Andy Najar finished second and third ​in the voting, ​respectively. ⁠The award is voted on by MLS club technical staff, media ​and current MLS players.

Woledzi is the ​second ⁠player in franchise history to win Defender of the Year, joining back-to-back winner Walker ⁠Zimmerman (2020 and ​2021). He is the ​second African player to earn the honors after the ​Columbus Crew's Steven Moreira in 2024.

Ghana News.title: NADKANSCO commissions 100-tonne-per-day cashew processing factory in Bono East, boosting Ghana’s value-addition drive
Ghana News.content:
Managing Director of NADKANSCO Cashew Processing Limited, Belinda Akorfa Adokpa.

NADKANSCO Processing Limited has officially commissioned its modern cashew processing factory at Tuobodom in the Techiman North District of the Bono East Region, marking a significant milestone in Ghana’s efforts to expand local agro-processing, retain economic value and strengthen its position in the global cashew industry.

The commissioning ceremony was attended by His Excellency John Dramani Mahama, President of the Republic of Ghana, alongside government officials, traditional authorities, financial institutions, industry stakeholders, farmers and members of the business community.

With an installed processing capacity of 100 metric tonnes of raw cashew nuts per day, the facility is designed to operate continuously across three shifts, positioning it among Ghana’s largest investments in the cashew-processing sector.

Speaking at the ceremony, Managing Director of NADKANSCO Processing Limited, Belinda A. Adokpa, described the commissioning as a major step in the company’s transition from raw commodity trading to value-added agro-industrial production.

“NADKANSCO began in 2012 as an agro-commodity trading company. For many years, we participated in the export of raw cashew nuts. However, we recognised that the jobs, technical skills and economic value associated with processing needed to remain in Ghana. Today, we are proud to be part of the solution through this investment in local processing,” she stated.

Between 2022 and 2024, the company exported approximately 39,700 metric tonnes of raw cashew nuts, primarily to India and Vietnam.

The decision to invest in processing represents a strategic shift towards retaining more value within Ghana’s economy.

ADVANCING VALUE ADDITION AND EXPORT GROWTH

The NADKANSCO facility will process raw cashew nuts into several marketable products, including whole, split and broken cashew kernels, Cashew Nut Shell Liquid (CNSL) and cashew shell cake. The cashew kernels will be graded, hygienically processed and packaged to meet international market requirements, while CNSL will serve as an industrial raw material for products such as paints, varnishes, resins and brake linings. Cashew shell cake will also be utilised as biomass fuel, supporting the company's resource-efficiency and waste-reduction objectives.

According to the company, the factory is expected to generate more than US$40 million in foreign exchange earnings annually at the initial stage of operations, with projections exceeding US$100 million annually at full operation. Its established export network covers markets in Europe, Asia, North America and the Middle East.

STRENGTHENING THE CASHEW FARMING VALUE CHAIN

A central component of NADKANSCO’s investment is its commitment to supporting the farmers who supply the factory. The company has established the NADKANSCO Cashew Outgrower Programme (NCOP), designed to improve farmer productivity, enhance raw material quality, strengthen market access and promote sustainable farming practices. The programme is built around a registered network of approximately 6,000 cashew farmers. Under Phase One, supported by Ghana EXIM Bank, NADKANSCO targeted the training of 1,000 farmers but successfully trained 1,247 farmers across Tain, Wenchi, Nkoranza North and Techiman North within four weeks.

The training covered financial management, record keeping and good agronomic practices. Participating farmers also received agricultural tools and equipment, including pruning saws, cutlasses, knapsack sprayers, pruning scissors and Wellington boots, at no cost. Phase Two is expected to extend the programme to an additional 2,000 farmers across eight districts.

Planned interventions include farmer training in grafting and post-harvest handling, the establishment of 16 community aggregation and quality centres, GPS mapping of farms for traceability, formal off-take agreements and the provision of 20 boreholes for cashew-growing communities. The company is targeting yield improvements of at least 30 per cent among participating farmers.

CREATING JOBS AND IMPROVING COMMUNITY WELFARE

At full operational capacity, NADKANSCO projects that the factory will create approximately 1,500 direct jobs and an additional 3,000 indirect employment opportunities across farming, aggregation, transportation, logistics and related services.

The company has placed particular emphasis on employment opportunities for women and young people from Tuobodom, Techiman and surrounding communities. To support employee welfare, the facility includes an on-site crèche, a clinic providing medical services and health screenings, and free transportation for workers through four company buses.

The company has also highlighted its commitment to skills transfer, with expatriate technical experts mandated to train Ghanaian employees in processing technology, quality control and machinery operations.

Beyond the factory, NADKANSCO has donated four fully equipped ambulances to district hospitals in Atebubu, Wenchi, Kintampo and Techiman North. It has also committed five per cent of its proceeds to community development initiatives in Techiman and the communities supplying its raw cashew.

GHANA EXIM BANK’S ROLE IN THE INVESTMENT

Ghana EXIM Bank played a significant financing and developmental role in the establishment of the factory, supporting the acquisition of plant and machinery, working capital for raw cashew procurement and the first phase of the company's outgrower programme. The partnership reflects the importance of development finance in supporting Ghanaian businesses to move beyond raw commodity exports towards local manufacturing and value-added production. NADKANSCO has acknowledged the Bank’s support and reaffirmed its commitment to meeting its financial obligations while expanding the company’s contribution to Ghana’s export economy.

SUPPORTING GHANA’S INDUSTRIALISATION AGENDA

The commissioning of the factory aligns with Ghana’s broader industrialisation and economic transformation priorities, including the 24-Hour Economy, the Feed the Industries agenda and the national ambition to increase local processing of tree crops.

The company believes that increased investment in domestic cashew processing will strengthen the agricultural value chain, create sustainable employment, improve farmer incomes, increase non-traditional export earnings and position Ghana as a more competitive participant in the international cashew market. In her closing remarks, Managing Director Belinda A. Adokpa expressed appreciation to the Government of Ghana, Ghana EXIM Bank, the Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, the Tree Crops Development Authority, the Ghana Free Zones Authority, traditional authorities, financial partners, farmers and employees for their contributions to the project. She reaffirmed NADKANSCO’s commitment to building a competitive and sustainable cashew processing enterprise that creates lasting value for Ghana. NADKANSCO Processing Limited — From Ghanaian Cashew to Global Markets.

ABOUT NADKANSCO PROCESSING LIMITED NADKANSCO

Processing Limited is a Ghanaian agro-industrial company established in 2012, with roots in agro-commodity trading and a strategic focus on cashew processing and value addition.

Through its modern processing facility in Tuobodom, Bono East Region, the company seeks to transform Ghanaian raw cashew nuts into quality products for domestic and international markets while supporting farmers, creating employment and contributing to sustainable economic development.

Ghana News.title: Customs Commissioner directs ports to detain right-hand-drive vehicles without import permits
Ghana News.content:
Aaron Kanor, Commissioner of Customs Division of GRA

The Customs Division of the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) has directed all ports and stations nationwide to process or release right-hand-drive vehicles unless importers produce valid permits authorising their importation.

The directive, contained in a memorandum dated November 16, 2026, and signed by the Commissioner of Customs, Aaron Kanor, follows concerns that some right-hand-drive vehicles are being presented for clearance without the requisite approval.

The GRA has consequently instructed all sector commanders to ensure strict compliance with the directive.

This follows a JoyNews report on the use of Toyota Voxy vehicles and their involvement in an accident titled "VOXY!! Blame Game Among State Institutions As Blood Flows On Ghana's Roads."

Watch the full report below.

The memorandum draws attention to Section 58 of the Customs Act, 2015 (Act 891), which prohibits the importation of right-hand steering motor vehicles into Ghana without approval from the Minister.

It further states that prohibited motor vehicles are liable to seizure and forfeiture to the State.

According to the directive, any right-hand steering vehicle presented for clearance without a valid permit from the Ministry of Transport must be detained and dealt with in accordance with the provisions of the law.

The Commissioner has tasked sector commanders with communicating the directive to officers at all frontier stations, ports and collections under their supervision to ensure its strict enforcement.

The directive is addressed to all ports and stations.

Ghana News.title: Amputee World Cup: Black Challenge thrash Iraq to secure Round of 16 spot at Amputee World Cup
Ghana News.content:
The Black Challenge

Ghana’s Black Challenge thrashed Iraq 6-0 in their final group game of the WAFF Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico to secure qualification for the Round of 16.

Ghana headed into the encounter desperately needing a convincing victory to boost their chances of progressing to the knockout stage after suffering a 2-0 defeat to Angola and playing out a 1-1 draw with Colombia.

Coach Richard Obeng’s side made their intentions clear early on, with star player Mohammed Mubarik opening the scoring with a stunning long-range strike to give Ghana the lead.

Hamza Mohammed then doubled the advantage as the Black Challenge took control of the encounter, growing in confidence and piling pressure on their opponents.

Ghana continued their dominance after the break, adding to their tally to complete an emphatic 6-0 victory and seal their place in the Round of 16.

The result saw the Black Challenge finish second in Group D, behind Angola, who defeated Colombia 2-0 in the other group fixture.

Ghana will play USA in the round of 16 on Wednesday, November 18 as they continue their quest for a maiden Amputee Football World Cup title.

Ghana News.title: AFCON 2027Q: Somalia wins enough ‘motivation’ for Black Stars ahead of final two games – Ati Zigi
Ghana News.content:
Ghana goalkeeper Lawrence Ati Zigi believes the six points against Somalia gives the team the needed motivation ahead of the their final two games of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifiers.

Ghana recorded their first back-to-back wins in over a year following their victory over Somalia on Monday with Jordan Ayew scoring from the penalty box.

For Ati Zigi, the two games against Somalia brings relief to the team following their poor start to the campaign.

“I think with football, it's like a rollercoaster, and sometimes it goes up, sometimes it comes down. We didn't have a good start, but going into these games, we knew we wanted some points to be able to catch up, so that's why we came together as a team,” he said.

“We spoke all together, and we had one goal, to have six points, and to work together as a team, and that's what we showed today. We can be very happy going to the next game, full of motivation, and hopefully we can make the group.”

The result leaves Ghana in third place ahead of the final two games of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers campaign.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Ukraine drone attack kills two in Crimea as Kyiv targets bridge to Russia
World.content:
Moscow-installed governor says traffic suspended after second attack on bridge in two days.

Share Ukraine drone attack kills two in Crimea as Kyiv targets bridge to Russia on social media

A Ukrainian drone attack has killed at least two people in Russian-annexed Crimea as Kyiv has targeted the only bridge connecting southern Russia to the Black Sea peninsula for the second consecutive day, according to the Moscow-installed governor.

In a Telegram post, Sergei Aksyonov said traffic has been suspended after Tuesday’s attack on the Kerch Bridge.

The segment of the bridge for cars has reportedly collapsed into the sea, blocking the Kerch Strait, which connects the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov.

The bridge stretches for 19km (11.8 miles) and is also used by trains.

Also on Tuesday, Moscow attacked two bridges in Kyiv, Russia’s Ministry of Defence said.

Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said in a Telegram post that ⁠the Northern and ⁠Southern bridges had been hit and the subway ⁠system ⁠had also been damaged. He added that water and power supplies had been ‌partially cut.

The Russian Defence Ministry said it also targeted Ukraine’s military infrastructure in attacks on Monday night, including facilities used to produce cruise missiles and long‑ and medium‑range drones. The ministry said transport and energy facilities were also targeted as well as port infrastructure and ships used by the Ukrainian military.

Putin-Xi-Trump meeting

The exchange of attacks comes just days before a meeting of Presidents Vladimir Putin of Russia, Xi Jinping of China and Donald Trump of the United States in China’s Shenzhen region.

The Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs said Thursday’s talks will focus on topics of “groundbreaking significance”, including “safeguarding world peace”.



Trump has made securing an end to the war between Russia and Ukraine a key part of his presidency. Despite another round of talks held in the United Arab Emirates last week, US mediators have failed to make a breakthrough.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had warned that Kyiv would carry out attacks on Russia in the days before the meeting.

World.title: Bahrain thwarts drone attack; Iran claims targeting US military radar
World.content:
The IRGC says the attack is part of efforts to counter ‘hostile activities of US forces in the region’.

Bahraini air defence has thwarted a drone attack, according to the Gulf country’s state television, after Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) launched a barrage of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs).

The IRGC said on Tuesday that it carried out a drone attack on a US radar system at the Isa airbase in Bahrain.

The reported attacks in Bahrain – home to the US Navy’s Fifth Fleet – come amid stalled diplomatic efforts to end the US-Israel war ⁠on Iran, which began ⁠on February 28 and has affected the entire Gulf region and beyond.

It is the latest of several Iran-claimed attacks on US radar systems in Bahrain in recent days.

The IRGC said the attack was “part of efforts to counter the hostile activities of US forces in the region”, according to a statement carried by Iran’s state broadcaster IRIB.

Blasts echoed over the Bahraini capital, Manama, after residents received a mobile phone alert warning of a “potential threat”. Explosions were heard after the Ministry of Interior’s alert urged residents to “proceed to the nearest safe location”. It later issued an “all clear” message.

In a statement, the ministry said “precautionary measures remain in place” and urged the public to exercise caution.

Recent attacks

On Sunday, the IRGC launched six drones at a US air defence radar system at Bahrain’s Riffa airbase, which hosts US forces, in response to what it described as hostile US actions.

On Friday, the IRGC also claimed to have targeted a US early-warning radar system in Bahrain, but the US military denied that the facility had been hit, saying it intercepted two Iranian drones without damage or casualties.



“Since Friday, it seems that the rules of engagement have changed,” said Al Jazeera’s Resul Serdar, reporting from Tehran, stating that a pattern has emerged, with Iran now trying to restore deterrence.

“First, Iran warned that if the US escorts ships carrying oil that do not coordinate with Iran [through the Strait of Hormuz], then Tehran would attack US military installations. Now, Iran is saying its attack on a US radar system in Bahrain is because of the US’s continued violations of Iranian airspace.

It is not a response to a specific US attack, but rather the continued violation of its airspace.”

Bahrain has faced renewed security concerns amid escalating tensions between Washington and Tehran.

World.title: Portugal coach Jorge Jesus responds to criticism from Ronaldo’s mother
World.content:
Ronaldo’s mother Dolores Aveiro said she was glad to see Jesus suffer his first defeat after her son had been ‘deceived’ by him.

Share Jesus on Portugal criticism: ‘Now I have to respond to Ronaldo’s mother?’ on social media

Portugal coach Jorge Jesus believes he will still be responding to questions about Cristiano Ronaldo next year, after he was asked for his thoughts on scathing comments by the football great’s mother.

“Now I have to respond to Cristiano Ronaldo’s mother?” Jesus asked on Tuesday, addressing the media before Portugal’s final Nations League group fixture away to Wales.

“I don’t know when it is going to stop. If you guys ask the questions, I have to answer. If you ask about Ronaldo next year, I will answer.”

Jesus’s frustration stemmed from his lingering tensions with Ronaldo following the recent international retirement of football’s all-time greats.

The 72-year-old head coach responded to comments from Ronaldo’s mother in the wake of the team’s latest defeat – their first since the 41-year-old forward quit national duties.

Jesus wondered when he would stop being peppered about Ronaldo after a 4-1 Nations League defeat to Denmark prompted criticism from the five-time Ballon d’Or winner’s mother, Dolores Aveiro.

Aveiro said she was glad to see Jesus suffer his first defeat since taking charge after the World Cup as Ronaldo had been “deceived” by the former Benfica boss.

Ronaldo’s decision to hang up his boots for country followed a falling out with Jesus, who was previously the superstar’s coach at Saudi club Al-Nassr.

The ex-Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus star accused Jesus of broken promises after he was asked to warm up during a match against Norway in September without being introduced as a substitute.



Ronaldo left the team camp and was handed a 30-day suspension and a token fine.

He apologised and was expected to return to the Portugal squad, but instead brought down the curtain on a 23-year international career.

His 234 appearances and 146 goals are both world records in the men’s game.

Ronaldo’s lack of mobility was often pinpointed as a factor in a richly talented Portugal squad falling short in recent major tournaments.

Jesus’s side had made a perfect start with four consecutive wins prior to Saturday’s shock defeat to the Danes.

“After the game against Denmark, everyone is asking me about different individuals, not about the team or winning here,” added Jesus.

“We played one bad game and it’s harder to move on when we have a result like that, but we are going to try and win the game.”

Portugal only need a point in Cardiff to secure top spot in Nations League group A4 against a Wales side that will finish bottom of the section.

“You were all having a go at him for playing, and then as soon as he retires, suddenly it’s all hell breaking loose!” Wales boss Craig Bellamy told the Portuguese media.

“He is one of the best players that has ever played the game. We’re all going to miss him.”

World.title: The new French malaise
World.content:
Fifty years ago, Alain Peyrefitte, who served as a spokesperson for French President Charles de Gaulle, published a book entitled Le Mal français (The French Malaise). In the book, Peyrefitte wrote that the progress of the French nation was impeded by the lack of trust – within society and between society and state institutions. In reaction, the state exercised excessive control through rules, bureaucracy and centralisation, which resulted in stagnation.

Today, the French malaise persists, but its symptoms are quite different from the ones observed by Peyrefitte. We now have the dramatic protests by French students as well as workers and other disaffected groups, which at times have turned violent.

But these demonstrations are only the tip of the iceberg. The malaise runs much deeper.

A threat to the Republic

Following the events of October 17, in which symbols of state authority were attacked – including the town halls of Limoges and Marseille and an official building in Lyon – and businesses were looted, French President Emmanuel Macron stated that these acts sought “to tear down our institutions”.

The use of such strong words reminds one of the rhetoric employed by the French government during the protests of May 1968, when students challenged the established order, and their actions were portrayed as an “attack on the Republic”.

There is, in fact, a tendency to compare the current wave of demonstrations with the events of May 1968. Yet the two movements differ. The protesters of 1968 were calling for more freedom, while today’s protesters are demanding equality and dignity. The former demonstrations were led by privileged youth; the latter are driven by those who have been left behind.



Perhaps a more relevant episode to examine is the upheaval of 2005 in the suburbs of Paris and other major cities following the deaths of two teenagers, Bouna and Zyed, who were pursued by the police.

For three weeks, residents of impoverished neighbourhoods, living on the fringes of society both geographically and socially, expressed their anger at police violence and their own marginalisation.

Two elements of the French malaise were already apparent at the time. First was the deep divide between two segments of society: the prosperous urban population and the marginalised, racialised poor, living in the underdeveloped and underserviced outskirts.

The second was the French police itself, which has overwhelmingly focused on policing the latter with ever-growing brutality.

In any country, a citizen-oriented police force can help build the bonds that unite a nation. But in France, the police is tasked with defending the state, not protecting the citizens.

It does not contribute to the cohesion of a nation. It does not abide by proportionality in the use of force or opt for de-escalation; it openly practises a discriminatory approach to policing which differentiates between affluent neighbourhoods and impoverished areas, between the white majority and the communities of colour.

It is no wonder that upwards of 60 percent of the police and military forces of France vote for the far right.

The French archipelago

In 2019, French political scientist Jérôme Fourquet wrote a book entitled The French Archipelago: The birth of a diverse and divided nation. In it, he argues that France has undergone a societal shift which has fundamentally altered people’s relationship with themselves and with the “other”. As a result, French society has split into small “islands” which are increasingly isolated from one another.

This transformation cannot be attributed solely to immigration. It is, above all, the result of the secession of the elite, which has grown distant and indifferent to the fate of the rest of the nation. This includes the political left, who are now commonly referred to as the gauche caviar (the caviar left).

It has been the elite’s abandonment and self-isolation that has caused the revolt of the masses, rather than the other way around.

The institutions that traditionally fostered socialisation between various groups, bestowing a sense of belonging, including schools, summer camps and compulsory military service, are no longer functioning effectively, or are cancelled.

In this fragmented society, one segment has been picked as a scapegoat for all problems, diverting attention from the real roots of the malaise.



Islamophobia is flourishing in France, as is the belief in the “Great Replacement”, a conspiracy theory that people of colour are meant to “replace” the white majority. Islamophobia has even become institutionalised through legislation and a political culture that has transformed blasphemy into something resembling a duty.

The paradox is that France – compared with its neighbours – has a smaller immigrant population while it espouses a much louder rhetoric about “integration”.

And there is a considerable gap between rhetoric and reality. While those in power demand that people of immigrant background “integrate”, very little is done by the state to actually drive this process.

As a result, some French citizens feel they are French only on paper. They understand that citizenship cannot be reduced to a political discourse. Without genuine access to rights, which necessarily entails social justice and human dignity, there can be no meaningful citizenship.

In 2005, a group of activists went as far as declaring themselves the “Natives of the Republic” and calling for its decolonisation. Indeed, anyone familiar with French society can recognise that France has reproduced a colonial order within.

The country that gave birth to the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen has failed to treat some of its own people as full citizens. And that stands at the core of the new French malaise.

The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.

World.title: Will Netanyahu lose this time?
World.content:
The Israeli prime minister has manoeuvred out of tough situations before to retain power. But he may find it hard this time.

I have been covering Benjamin Netanyahu for more than 30 years. I was in Washington when, as a young opposition leader, he worked hand in glove with the Republicans to embarrass Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin and sabotage the Oslo Accords. I have seen him cornered before. I have never seen him cornered like this.

The numbers are merciless. His bloc won 53 seats, eight short of a majority. Sixty-seven members of the new Knesset recommended former army chief Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, who now has up to 42 days to form a government. For Netanyahu, they may be the longest 42 days of his political life.

The stakes are political, but above all personal. His corruption trial continues, and he faces a possible prison sentence. His pardon request has been gathering dust on President Isaac Herzog’s desk for months. Eisenkot’s bloc has already tabled bills for a state commission of inquiry into the October 7 attacks and for prime-ministerial term limits.

A state inquiry would strip him of the title he covets the most: “defender of Israel”. For Netanyahu, the chair is not a job. It is a lifeline. His trial, under way since May 2020, is in its final stretch. A sitting prime minister can be removed only after a final conviction.

From his office, he can stall hearings and lean on the justice system. Out of office, he is just another defendant.

To survive, Netanyahu does not need to build a government. He needs time to keep his rivals from building one. To buy it, he is pulling three levers.



The first is his proposal for a “national unity government” of all the parties that support Israel as the nation-state of the Jewish people. Translation: the Arab parties, representing 21 percent of the population, are out. The Jewish supremacists, Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, are in. So are the anti-Zionist Haredi parties. This is unity, Netanyahu-style.

He has gift-wrapped the offer in the old rhetoric of the Iranian nuclear threat, with one catch: He would not give up the premiership or agree to a rotation.

Eisenkot has called the offer “another spin”, yet he has agreed to negotiate with Likud. He knows a refusal would only feed the spin machine: They will talk to Arab supporters of Hamas, but not to Jewish patriots, the Netanyahu camp would claim.

He also knows to beware of a diversion designed to burn through the days the president has allotted him.

The second lever is incitement. At the Knesset’s opening session, Netanyahu branded Ra’am and the Joint List “terror supporters” and “haters of Israel”. A government depending on them, he declared, “must not be formed”. The goal is to strangle an Arab-backed government in its cradle, and to scare the Haredi parties, which are currently part of his bloc, away from joining the “enemy”.

But this time the incitement has a hole in it. Ra’am leader Mansour Abbas says Netanyahu’s confidant Natan Eshel sounded him out on the bill to bar an indicted politician from serving as prime minister. Joint List lawmaker Ahmad Tibi went on live television with WhatsApp messages he said came from Eshel. “Terror supporters”, it seems, are good enough for a quiet chat.

The third lever is escalation. According to media reports, Netanyahu has been pressing US President Donald Trump for another wave of strikes on Iran. A return to full-scale war could help him form an emergency government.

In a media interview, former Prime Minister Ehud Barak laid out the scenario: a blatant provocation that forces Iran to respond, and a war that would disrupt or prevent the establishment of a new government. Lebanon, Gaza or the West Bank could serve just as well. The mantra is well-known: The enemy must see that we are united.

Here, too, there are limits. A former chief of staff of the army, Eisenkot spent many years in uniform and has no shortage of sources in the army. They are likely telling him there is no urgent need for another round of war with Iran. And Trump has hinted that he wants that war over.

If all three levers fail, Netanyahu has a familiar fallback: another election, next spring. Between 2019 and 2022, he dragged Israelis to the polls five times rather than give up the chair. Tibi has revealed that one of Netanyahu’s ministers tried to convince him his party would be better off “going to elections” than joining Eisenkot’s bloc.



Eisenkot has a problem of his own. He campaigned on three pledges: no Netanyahu, no Haredi parties, no Arab parties. He cannot keep all three. Politics is the art of choosing which promise to break.

The first path available to Eisenkot runs through the Haredim. His bloc has 48 seats; Shas and United Torah Judaism (UTJ) would add 13, for exactly 61, the number he needs to secure a majority in the 120-seat Knesset. A softened draft law is reportedly on the table. But UTJ’s rabbis want all 48 members of the bloc to sign a pledge exempting Haredim from military service, with an override clause to shield the law from the Supreme Court. Eisenkot has pledged not to back down on military service for all.

The second path is a minority government, backed by the Arab parties from outside the coalition. Eisenkot is reportedly willing to do it, and so is one of his allies, Yair Golan, leader of the Democrats. Another ally, Naftali Bennett, is believed to oppose it. The big obstacle is Yisrael Beytenu leader Avigdor Lieberman, who rules out the Arab parties, a minority government and new elections. Three noes in a single breath.

The third path is Likud without Netanyahu, or with him in a diplomatic role. No Likud lawmaker has broken ranks so far. And for Netanyahu, a junior partnership would be not a retirement plan but a launching pad: From inside the cabinet, he could stall the bills on a state inquiry and term limits, undermine the government and bring it down at a moment of his choosing. Just ask Benny Gantz, whose 2020 rotation deal with Netanyahu never brought him to the prime minister’s chair.

This is a game of chicken. Netanyahu is betting that Eisenkot’s partners will squabble over the draft, the Arab parties and the portfolios until the clock runs out, forcing a seventh election since 2019 — one he would fight from the Prime Minister’s Office, his finger on the trigger. Eisenkot’s best weapon is the one Netanyahu fears the most: a government, any government, sworn in before the 42 days are up.

Eisenkot’s camp has already taken over the Knesset building. Netanyahu’s camp will do everything it can to keep it from taking over the government buildings. They will not give up without street battles.

The last time incitement spilled into the streets, in November 1995, it ended with the assassination of Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin. It paved the way for the comeback of the Israeli right, led by a young, charming Revisionist.

Will November 2026 mark the end of the Netanyahu era and a return to Rabin’s path of peace?

The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.

World.title: Asian love ballads test Eurovision’s winning song formula.
World.content:
Fans gathering ahead of the inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia finale on Saturday in Bangkok.

Simon Robinson, one of the fans who traveled to Bangkok for the Eurovision Song Contest on Saturday, said that his history with the competition is nearly as long as its seven-decade run.

He was eight years old when he first watched it with his family in Yorkshire, England, when Britain's Mary Hopkin finished in second place behind Ireland’s Dana.

“I really liked the concept of bringing Europe together after the war,” said Mr. Robinson, 63, who now lives in Melbourne, Australia. He described the contest’s annual broadcast as a social activity for his family and neighbors.

“Eurovision helped to create the European identity,” he added.

Other fans had their own motivations for traveling to see the contest’s first Asian edition.

Some are Europeans living in Asia, on the hunt for nostalgia, while others are Americans who were eager to experience their first Eurovision.

Lee Hudson, an American television executive based in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, said that he gets emotional when he talks about Eurovision, which he has watched since 2012.

“The only reason I know any music from European countries is because I heard them on Eurovision,” he said. “Eurovision Asia makes sense because the musical cultures are distinct.”

Mr. Hudson said he still listens to Loreen’s “Euphoria,” which won the competition for Sweden in 2012.

It was also the first Eurovision that Drew Andrea watched from his home in Sydney. A year later, he got a passport to fly to Sweden for the 2013 edition, and has attended every final since. Coming to Bangkok for Eurovision Asia was much more affordable, he said.

“Asia understands the brief — the kitschy costumes, the dance music,” he said.

His top picks among the Asian performers were the Philippines’ Carmelle and Vietnam’s Toc Tien. “I think they hit the nail on the head with the song, staging, costume and traditional elements,” he said.

Luca Cian, a professor of marketing at the University of Virginia who grew up in Italy, said that Eurovision built a global fan base by offering a shared cultural experience.

“Millions of people across Europe watch it at the same moment,” he said. “Families have watch parties with food and drinks. There are public discussions. Rituals create community.”

Carmen Chung, a British accountant, said she hijacked her family’s holiday in Bangkok to attend Eurovision Asia with her brother Garry Chung, a banker who lives in Hong Kong. “We were raised on Eurovision,” she said of their childhood in Yorkshire.

European acts, she said, tend to copy whatever style of music won the previous year. “This year, because there are no expectations, everyone has just done their own thing,” she said. She and her brother said they were rooting for Bangladesh’s Beatmosphere, a beatboxing group that will perform an a cappella love song.

Martin Green, the director of the Eurovision Song Contest, said that about half of the tickets for Saturday’s final were purchased by “super fans” from outside Asia. Organizers have kept the inaugural show modest, with 11 participating countries and a 5,000-seat venue.

Mr. Andrea said he didn’t mind the small scale.
