“I’m O.K. with humble beginnings as long as it keeps growing every year,” he said.

World.title: Here’s the latest.
World.content:
Pinned

The Eurovision Song Contest crowned its first Asia champion in Bangkok on Saturday, in an event that tested whether a high-camp singing competition with an ardent fan base could appeal to audiences in a new market.

Carmelle of the Philippines was declared the winner of the inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia, beating out artists and original songs from 10 other countries: Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, Laos, Malaysia, Mongolia, Nepal, South Korea, Thailand and Vietnam. The show was live-streamed on YouTube and broadcast by television stations across the region.

Eurovision has been a fixture of the European cultural calendar since it began in 1956. Past winners include Sweden’s ABBA and the Canadian chanteuse Celine Dion, who represented Switzerland in 1988.

Asian artists have readily embraced the kitschy outfits and spectacular sets that are part of Eurovision tradition, with costumes that include traditional dress, as well as feathered capes and sequined corsets. Malaysia’s performer plans to enter the stage in a giant teardrop.

But the Eurovision format has not been tested in Asia. Fans and regional partners have expressed concern in recent weeks that budget constraints, production issues and weak audience demand could imperil the spinoff. Organizers say the contest could take time to build an audience.

“It would be profoundly arrogant to think that just because we have a heritage brand and a huge global audience for the European show, that we would walk in and demand it to be the same here,” said Martin Green, the European Broadcasting Union’s director of the Eurovision Song Contest. “Like any new thing, it needs to find its roots.”

Two previous attempts to take the competition to Asia were abandoned by the European Broadcasting Union, which owns Eurovision, and its partners in the region. A Eurovision spinoff in the United States, NBC’s American Song Contest, ran for one season in 2022.

The Asian edition kicking off on Saturday is far smaller than its European counterpart. Eurovision organizers said they were in talks with more countries to join future seasons. They include China, Japan and India, whose music industries have global reach.

“Bringing the world together through music is a fundamentally good idea,” Mr. Green said. “Europe shouldn’t keep it to itself.”

Here’s what we’re covering:

World.title: Here’s the latest.
World.content:
Pinned

The nationwide ground stop that brought all air travel to a halt across the country and stranded thousands of passengers has been canceled, according to the Federal Aviation Administration, though delays from the outage are expected to persist in the coming days.

The order on Friday halted nearly all departures and stranded thousands of passengers at airports across the country. Hundreds of flights were diverted to other airports and more were canceled, even as some internationally bound flights managed to secure permission to take off. Many passengers were taken off flights or told to go home. Chaos spread at airports as travelers sought answers from airline and airport employees.

Sean Duffy, the transportation secretary, warned that it would take “some time” for air travel nationwide to recover from the ground stop. Speaking at a news conference on Friday night shortly after flight traffic had been restored, Mr. Duffy predicted that flight schedules would be fully back to normal by the time the Thanksgiving travel season begins.

“I believe that it’s going to take us some time to get back to capacity,” he said, adding: “We’re going to have some makeup to do.”

Mr. Duffy decried Congress, accusing lawmakers of dragging their feet when it came to fully funding upgrades he warned were vital to prevent similar failures from happening again.

“It’s going to continue to fail,” Mr. Duffy told reporters, adding: “How many times does this have to happen for Congress to give the money to fix it?”

Mr. Duffy said that the antiquated radar and telecoms systems that controllers rely on to transmit data and other information between facilities began to falter at 3:36 p.m. The aging system, which has undergone a number of upgrades, became overloaded, officials said.

Appearing alongside him, Markwayne Mullin, the secretary of homeland security, stressed that there was never any indication that the communications failures had been triggered by a cyberattack, but he added, “we are still looking, and we’re not going to rule it out.” He emphasized that lives were never in danger.

But the incident appeared to inject new fuel into Mr. Duffy’s now monthslong campaign to secure at least $30 billion in extra funding for air traffic control modernization.

Last year, Congress approved $12.5 billion to upgrade aging air traffic facilities and technology, funds Mr. Duffy has repeatedly referred to as a “down payment” when asking for tens of billions more. On Friday night, Mr. Duffy appeared to up the ante, telling reporters that he didn’t just want another $30 billion for the project, but another $50 billion. He argued that it should be delivered in emergency funding before the end of the year, after which control of Congress — and the budget — switches from Republicans to Democrats.

Some Democratic lawmakers have already raised questions about how efficiently and effectively the F.A.A. has spent the money they have been given thus far. But Mr. Duffy has long argued that his department cannot be expected to complete a meaningful overhaul of the nation’s air traffic control system without a massive influx of funding.

Friday’s nationwide ground stop was only the third that the F.A.A. has issued this century. It ranks as the second-longest, after the ground stop issued on Sept. 11, 2001, in the wake of the terrorist attacks on the World Trade Center in New York. There was a shorter one on Jan. 11, 2023, because of an outage in the F.A.A.’s system to alert pilots to safety issues.

More than 2 million people pass through airport security checkpoints on a typical day, according to Transportation Security Administration data. On Thursday, the agency screened nearly 2.5 million people. According to FlightRadar24, an aviation tracking site, there were more than 1,000 airborne aircraft bound for U.S. airports during the nationwide ground stop. According to the flight tracking app Flighty, there were more than 30,000 departures and arrivals scheduled for the remainder of the day.

It could take days for air travel to fully normalize after an event of this scale, said Vikrant Vaze, a Dartmouth professor specializing in commercial aviation logistics.

“It’s going to take a lot of gymnastics” to get every airline’s aircraft, passengers and crew members back in the correct positions, he said.

Here’s what else to know:

If your flight is canceled: You are entitled to a refund if your flight is canceled in the United States, regardless of the reason, or if a flight is significantly delayed or changed and you decide not to take it. Here are other travel tips that might be helpful. Read more ›

A busy travel month: The ground stop happened about two weeks before Thanksgiving, one of the busiest times of the year for air travel. On average, U.S. airlines are expected to fly about 2.7 million passengers each day over the holiday period, according to industry trade group Airlines for America.

Handling the chaos: Radio transmissions between air traffic controllers and pilots at major airports offered a peek at how they navigated the ground stoppage. Read more ›

The last ground stop: The last nationwide ground stop came in the early morning of Jan. 11, 2023, and lasted around 90 minutes. The disruption came after a system to alert pilots of real-time dangers went down. Read more ›

Christine Chung , Niraj Chokshi , Luke Broadwater , Dustin Volz , Lisa Lerer and Robert Chiarito contributed reporting.

World.title: Crimea bridge shut after reported Ukrainian strike, as Russia hits Kyiv crossings
World.content:
A key bridge linking occupied Crimea and Russia is closed after reports a Ukrainian strike inflicted major damage, during a night in which the warring countries both targeted major crossings.

A former adviser to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky shared images purporting to show that a section of the Crimea bridge - also known as the Kerch Bridge - had collapsed into the water.

Meanwhile, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the Northern and Southern bridges, important routes over the Dnipro River, were closed after Russian ballistic missile strikes.

Those attacks came a day after Ukraine began its most recent attempt to disable the Crimea bridge, a prized Kremlin asset seen as a symbol of Russia's occupation.

Two people were killed in that strike overnight on Sunday, the Russian-installed governor of Crimea said.

Former Ukrainian adviser Anton Gerashchenko shared images and video footage appearing to show extensive damage to the bridge from the latest strike, with a support arch and road section seen protruding from the water below. BBC News has not independently verified those images.

The bridge, which has come under repeated attack by Ukrainian forces, was built by Russia after it invaded and annexed the peninsula in 2014, and was personally opened by Russian President Vladimir Putin in 2018.

While Ukraine has been trying to increase the cost to Russia of waging war economically, by hitting oil refineries and depots, striking the Crimea bridge is an attempt do increase the political cost on Putin.

The severity of the latest strike on the route, which is protected with multiple layers of aerial and maritime defences, is still not fully clear - but Russian state media reported a meeting was due to be held on Tuesday to discuss the situation.

Crimea's Moscow-backed governor Sergei Aksyonov confirmed on Telegram that traffic over the bridge had been suspended.

World.title: Ukraine accuses Russia of targeting rescue operation after 'double-tap' strike kills 72
World.content:
Ukrainian officials have accused Russia of targeting rescue and recovery operations two weeks after a deadly "double-tap" strike at a village close to the front line killed at least 72 people.

Ukraine says Russia carried out two attacks in succession on a humanitarian aid centre in the village of Komyshuvakha on 2 November - including the use of what it said was a 3,000kg (6,600lb) aerial bomb on a shelter where residents had fled for safety.

Verified images posted in the days after the attack show damage to emergency vehicles and excavation equipment at the site.

The State Emergency Service of Ukraine (DSNS) told BBC Verify there have been multiple Russian strikes during the rescue.

The DSNS said three police officers, four workers and two rescue dogs were injured while five vehicles were damaged during the operation, which has now concluded.

"Due to the threat of repeated shelling, emergency workers are constantly forced to periodically suspend work and retreat to a safe place," it added.

The DSNS said the death toll had risen to at least 72 people making it one of the deadliest single incidents since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

World.title: Imran Khan seeks urgent medical care fearing he 'may not return alive'
World.content:
Pakistan's jailed former PM Imran Khan has appealed for urgent medical treatment, saying that his and his wife's health has been deteriorating.

"At 74, this unrelenting state is taking me to a place from which I may not return alive," the cricket star-turned-politician wrote in a letter published by his lawyer Salman Safdar.

Authorities in Islamabad maintain that Khan gets seen weekly by doctors, who have assessed that he is of "satisfactory" health.

Khan, who faces more than 100 charges, has been in prison since August 2023. His wife Bushra Bibi was jailed along with him last year. Khan argues the cases against them, ranging from corruption to selling state gifts, are politically motivated.

Concerns over Khan's health have grown louder in the past year, with his family claiming he has lost most of his vision in his right eye after prison authorities failed to take action.

In his letter, Khan wrote that doctors have told him he is "highly vulnerable to a brain haemorrhage and cardiac arrest", and that his heart has already "suffered damage".

He also expressed concern for Bushra Bibi, whom he says suffered a detached retina in April and underwent surgery in secrecy. Khan said he fears she may lose her sight without further surgery.

"I have fought impossible legal battles in countless cases, and I have not stopped. But the system has stopped giving me justice," he wrote.

He said that he is being held in solitary confinement for up to 22 hours a day, where he is allowed neither visits by his family nor access to books and television, and that this has "taken a heavy toll" on his mental health.

He also claimed he had only seen his lawyers four times over the past year.

"I will only remain able to prove my innocence if I stay alive," he wrote.

Pakistan's parliamentary affairs minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry disputed these claims, saying Khan is "provided with all facilities in prison, including food of his own choosing".

"[He] is currently the most well-accommodated prisoner in Pakistan," the minister told reporters.

Authorities also say Khan was taken to a government-run hospital for an eye injection a week ago, where doctors deemed him "clinically stable".

Khan, who previously captained the Pakistan national cricket team, served as Pakistan's prime minister from 2018 to 2022.

His arrest in May 2023 sparked large-scale, violent protests by supporters, who ransacked the corps commander's residence in Lahore, smashing chandeliers and making away with furniture, paintings, and even peacocks, among other things.

At least eight people died in the protests and the army were called in to quell the violence.

Even behind bars, Khan remains a force in Pakistani politics.

Thousands of his supporters took to the streets in early October in a dayslong march, demanding his release. Authorities later ordered a crackdown on protests and imposed a state of emergency in Khan's party stronghold, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

Former international cricket captains have made several appeals in recent months to Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, insisting that Khan be given proper medical care.

World.title: Nvidia dismisses 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign as Trump backs effort to reinstate ex boss
World.content:
Nvidia has dismissed a campaign calling for the company's co-founder Jensen Huang to be handed back his job as allies, including US President Donald Trump, supported the effort.

Trump said on Monday that he "would certainly not mind" if Huang was reinstated, joining a list of supporters including SpaceX's Elon Musk who are backing a "Bring Jensen Back" campaign.

But the BBC has been told the board of the AI chip giant is not interested in reinstating him after he resigned last week following revelations he had two affairs, including one that involved a suspected Chinese spy.

The same day, the White House also said it will further restrict China's access to AI chips from firms like Nvidia.

The reported affairs created a crisis for one of the world's most valuable firms - a central company in AI and the US battle against China for dominance.

Since Huang's departure, more than 175,000 people have signed an open letter calling for the board to reinstate the tech billionaire while an ongoing internal probe is conducted.

Major tech bosses, including Musk and Tim Sweeney, chief executive of Fortnite-maker Epic Games, have also supported Huang's return.

World.title: OpenAI sued by California over Hugging Face attack
World.content:
Hundreds of OpenAI agents coordinated the Hugging Face attack over two days even though they were supposed to be contained in a safe testing environment.

The incident drew added scrutiny because the agents went as far as attempting to cover their tracks.

Bonta announced an investigation into the incident in September, and served an investigative subpoena on OpenAI as part of its probe.

"The company knowingly tested a dangerous product without proper oversight or safety procedures and misled the public about it - this disregard for public safety violated California law," Bonta said in a statement on Monday.

OpenAI said it has been transparent and responsive to the Attorney General's office.

"We take misalignment seriously, and we have engaged - and will continue to engage - constructively with the Attorney General's office to share information and advance strong, practical safety standards for the entire industry," the company said.

The company added that, since the Hugging Face incident, it has worked to understand and address "misaligned model activity" which industry figures often refer to as rogue agents.

Nathan Calvin, chief strategy officer at AI safety campaign group Encode AI, said the lawsuit "recognises something we at Encode have long raised alarms about".

"OpenAI and other companies developing frontier AI systems have safety and security practices that are insufficient to protect the public from risks that could be catastrophic," he said.

World.title: Forensic expert says his analysis of autopsy photos suggests Epstein was killed
World.content:
This article contains distressing details and references to suicide

A forensic expert has said he believes that convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein's death in prison was the result of a homicide, not suicide.

Speaking to BBC Newsnight, Professor Michael Freeman said that after reviewing the New York City medical examiner's file he believes Epstein was strangled, most likely from behind.

The medical examiner who carried out the autopsy concluded in 2019 that Epstein's injuries were consistent with suicide and there was no evidence of the defensive wounds expected if his death had been a homicide.

Epstein was found dead in prison on 10 August 2019 in New York as he awaited trial on sex trafficking charges.

Dr Barbara Sampson, chief medical examiner at the time of Epstein's autopsy, who ruled that Epstein's death was a suicide, has previously said: "I stand firmly behind our determination of the cause and manner of death for Mr. Epstein." The BBC has approached Sampson for further comment.

Freeman has served as a cause-of-death expert to attorneys-general in the US for death in police custody cases, including George Floyd in Minnesota.

He published his research and the New York City medical examiner's files after presenting his findings in London on Monday evening.

Freeman, who did not see the body, based his conclusions on the files and photographs from the examiner's report provided to him by Epstein's brother, Mark Epstein, who has always maintained that his brother was murdered.

Freeman said his analysis is independent and that he was not paid by Mark Epstein. His research has not been peer reviewed.

He told the BBC that he believed there are signs indicating an assault on Epstein, including a deep haemorrhage to his left shoulder and injuries that appear to be consistent to being struck in the face.

Freeman said he believed the evidence was most consistent with strangulation using a ligature and then that same ligature was probably used to suspend the body from the bunk bed.

He said there appeared to be fingernail marks above the ligature mark on Epstein's neck, which "would be consistent with strangulation, particularly from behind. And the attempt by the victim to try to remove the ligature from the neck".

He said "the injuries and the way the body was found don't match up. There's only one remaining explanation then, and that is that the death was as a result of a homicide."

The medical examiner who performed the autopsy at the time told the Department of Justice (DoJ) Office of the Inspector General , externalthat Epstein's injuries were more consistent with, and indicative of, a suicide by hanging rather than homicide by strangulation, adding there was no evidence of defensive wounds consistent with what is seen in victims of strangulation.

World.title: Lindsay Clancy to face retrial next year for deaths of her three children
World.content:
Warning: This story contains details some readers may find distressing.

Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts woman accused of murdering her three children, will face a retrial next year, a judge has said, after a jury deadlocked last time in a case that gripped the nation.

The judge set a trial date for 29 March 2027, though the district attorney did not explicitly say what charges Clancy would face.

Prosecutors said they wanted a jury trial, and the defence said they took that to mean Clancy, 36, would again face first-degree murder charges.

Five-year-old Cora, Dawson, three, and eight-month-old Callan were strangled at the family home on 24 January 2023. The defence argues she had severe postpartum psychosis.

"I think you can read between the lines that when they say that the case is going to require a jury, that it's an indirect comment from the DA [district attorney] that they intend to proceed on first-degree murder indictments, so we will pick a trial date," defence lawyer Kevin Reddington said at Monday's hearing.

Prosecutors wanted a May trial date, but Judge William Sullivan decided on March instead. The judge is due to retire in June.

Clancy was charged in the first trial with three counts of first-degree-murder, which is the intentional and premeditated killing of another person.

The district attorney has not yet officially said he will proceed with first-degree-murder charges. The BBC has contacted the district attorney's office for comment.

World.title: Five EU countries announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda
World.content:
Five EU countries will open a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda next year as part of a broader push to boost removals.

Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands are expected to open a "return hub" ready to accept transfers in 2027, the Dutch and Danish governments announced in statements.

The countries said the scheme would apply to migrants staying illegally in their nations who are subject to deportation, with the Dutch government adding it will provide an alternative if deportees cannot be returned to their country of origin.

Deportees will be able to either integrate into Rwandan society or return to their home country, the nations said.

The scheme will apply to people who have exhausted their legal avenues to stay in the five nations - unlike a scrapped British deal that envisaged sending people to Rwanda to have their claims processed. Legal challenges meant the UK deal never took off, and it was eventually junked by the incoming Labour government in 2024.

Downing Street has not ruled out the UK joining the scheme, saying they will watch it "with interest".

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro SÃ¡nchez said the plan to open a centre in Rwanda had no "future or humanity", according to AFP news agency.

"I don't see any future or humanity in that. It's not the solution," Sanchez told the Spanish broadcaster Telecinco, AFP reported.

The five countries say the plan to send migrants abroad is in line with EU and international law, but human rights bodies say it could violate migrant rights.

The deal follows a recent EU reform that allowed for the creation of hubs outside of the bloc.

In a joint press conference in Vienna on Monday, Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker said the five countries wanted to relieve European asylum systems and stop traffickers arranging deadly trips across the Mediterranean.

In a written statement, the Dutch government said the five countries will "only return single men" as part of the first phase of the deal, adding that the focus for the Netherlands "will be on persons from countries of origin in the same region as Rwanda".

Once in Rwanda, people will be able to integrate into society, which means they will have the right of residence, as well as access to education, healthcare, the labour market and the legal system.

Rwandan Interior Minister Vincent Biruta said the country is commmited to working with European partners to provide a "safe, legal and dignified solution for migrants".

He added that they would also work on "correcting the global imbalance in economic opportunities", which he called a "key driver of irregular migration".

Ahead of the announcement, diplomatic sources told the AFP news agency the hub is expected to initially run as a pilot, hosting about 100 people, with each of the five nations possibly sending about 20 migrants.

The United Nations' International Organisation for Migration (IOM) could play an ancillary role.

"IOM has a long history of providing assistance to migrants in situations of transit, including in complex contexts," an IOM spokesperson said, adding the agency was in discussions with some EU countries "on plans for the establishment of return hubs or similar mechanisms".

With elections approaching in several EU nations, administrations have been under pressure to show they can control migration.

Concerns around security, struggling economies and disillusionment with governing parties have all had a major role in shaping attitudes towards people leaving their home countries.

Human Rights Watch's senior Africa researcher Clementine de Montjoye said the choice of Rwanda would be a cause of concern as it had a "well-established record of repression of dissent, arbitrary detention, ill-treatment in detention" and support for armed rebels in the neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo.

"Paying Kigali to host a deportation programme would not only cause suffering and harm to those deported, it would finance and provide political leverage to a government responsible for serious human rights abuses at home and abroad."

The independent EU Agency for Fundamental Rights argued any third country hosting a return hub should "respect fundamental rights", including that people should not be sent to a country where they face serious risk of persecution.

The agency added that unaccompanied children should not be sent to a return hub, which the Dutch government has confirmed will not take place.

According to the European Border and Coast Guard Agency, there were almost 110,000 irregular border crossings into the EU in the first 10 months of 2026, which represents a 29% decrease compared to the previous year.

In October, about 18,100 crossings were detected, which is about 6% less than October 2025 but 22% more than in September "largely because of a sharp rise in arrivals on the Western African route to the Canary Islands".

World.title: 2027 Politics Watch: Kano arrests, opposition unity summit, Wike’s Tinubu blitz
World.content:
The Kano State Police Command said on Monday that eight suspects had been arrested after political violence in Bichi left five people injured and 13 vehicles damaged.

Its account followed the state information commissioner’s dismissal of reports that Rabiu Kwankwaso’s campaign convoy had been attacked.

In Abuja, opposition parties fixed 23 November for a summit to sign cooperation agreements, identifying the protection of votes as their first joint undertaking.

Federal Capital Territory Minister Nyesom Wike inaugurated a campaign council with a different objective: a commanding victory for President Bola Tinubu.

Monday also brought a governorship candidate’s move to the ruling party, new inflation figures and an opposition debt charge that revisited an accounting dispute the government had addressed in October.

Police detail Bichi violence after convoy dispute

The police account reported by PREMIUM TIMES placed Sunday’s clash at about 4.45 p.m. in Bichi township and described violence involving supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC).

Police spokesperson Abdullahi Kiyawa said officers restored order, took injured people to hospital and recovered weapons.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The eight suspects were transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department in Bompai. He said the prosecution would follow the investigation.

The NDC’s account concerned the convoy carrying its vice-presidential candidate, Mr Kwankwaso, and Kano governorship candidate Aminu Gwarzo.

Mr Gwarzo’s spokesperson, Ibrahim Shuaibu, told Channels Television that the delegation received information about a roadblock before entering Bichi. He described stone-throwing followed by an attack after the convoy passed the local government secretariat.

Kano Information Commissioner Sanusi Bature Dawakin Tofa had offered a sharply different account. In a Sunday Facebook post reported by PUNCH, he accused the Kwankwasiyya movement of fabricating the incident to attract sympathy.

Monday’s police statement provided an official account of injuries and property damage. It did not determine who initiated the confrontation or establish political sponsorship.

NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi demanded an investigation on Monday, including action against anyone found to have organised the violence.

The police described a clash between supporters of two parties; the NDC described an attack on its delegation. Investigators must establish the sequence and individual responsibility.

Opposition sets pact date, but two earlier documents remain unaccounted for

Six opposition parties have fixed 23 November for a summit to sign three cooperation documents, leaving questions about two other agreements proposed at their first gathering in August.

The Coalition for Democracy said Monday’s announcement covered the National Covenant for Democratic Renewal, the Framework for Opposition Unity, and the National Reform Programme.

However, the parties had originally proposed five documents at their 31 August summit, as PREMIUM TIMES reported on 22 October.

The two not listed for signing next Monday are the Single-Term Transition Charter and Roadmap to a Common Presidential Candidate.

The first was intended to set the terms for a possible single-term transitional government, while the second would guide negotiations toward selecting a common presidential candidate.

Their omission from Monday’s announcement is significant because they concern the most difficult question facing the proposed coalition: how parties with competing presidential candidates might eventually agree on one ticket.

It remains unclear whether the two documents have been completed, postponed, incorporated into the three announced agreements or dropped from the immediate agenda.

The coalition has not publicly explained their status in the material examined.

In a Monday statement reported by TheCable, Salihu Lukman said the second summit would hold at the NAF Conference Centre in Abuja, with presidential candidates, running mates and party representatives expected to attend.

He identified electoral integrity at polling units as the first common national undertaking.

The coalition lists the ADC, NDC, APM, PRP, SDP and the Kabiru Turaki-led PDP faction.

The announcement therefore sets a date and three proposed instruments for political cooperation, but leaves earlier commitments on a transitional government and a common presidential candidate unresolved.

The latest announcement did not name a common presidential candidate. Atiku Abubakar, Mr Obi and Seyi Makinde continue to pursue separate tickets, as Monday’s State of the Race explained.

Cooperation over election monitoring can proceed without agreement on one contender. Choosing a shared candidate would require a further political decision and attention to the electoral procedures already examined in that report.

The immediate undertaking is narrower and more verifiable: which authorised representatives attend, what they sign and whether the resulting texts are made available to party members and voters.

Wike builds FCT campaign as Kashim joins APC

Mr Wike inaugurated a 466-member APC Presidential Campaign Council and Rainbow Coalition in Abuja on Monday, urging it to keep the ADC and NDC below 25 per cent of votes in the territory.

He said the assignment extended to APC National Assembly candidates and instructed members to establish local committees across the area councils.

The minister urged campaigners to present the administration’s infrastructure and institutional reforms to residents. He also directed members to take their message to markets, suburbs and traditional institutions, while maintaining peaceful campaigns.

APC and PDP figures participated in the event. Mr Wike, a PDP member, praised their cooperation in support of Mr Tinubu.

PDP participation in the two Abuja initiatives involves different camps: the opposition summit lists the Turaki-led faction, whereas Mr Wike’s allies are mobilising for the APC presidential ticket.

In Bauchi, Ibrahim Kashim announced his defection to the APC at its state secretariat on Monday.

The former secretary to the state government said the ruling party’s national organisation offered Bauchi greater opportunities to influence policy and attract development. He urged supporters to join him.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that he had resigned from the NDC on 16 October. Monday’s announcement therefore concerned his move into the APC, rather than the initial resignation.

The Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC) published Bauchi governorship list still lists him as the NDC candidate.

The entry records a nomination; it does not explain how his departure will be handled. The NDC’s state campaign arrangements and how it will handle that nomination require clarification from the party and the commission.

Inflation eases as NDC revives debt-interest dispute

The National Bureau of Statistics’ October figures, reported by PREMIUM TIMES, put annual headline inflation at 14.06 per cent, down from 14.63 per cent in September.

However, monthly headline inflation rose from 0.06 per cent to 0.43 per cent. Average prices therefore increased between September and October, even as their annual rate of increase slowed.

Annual food inflation stood at 19.13 per cent. The report also recorded a monthly decline in food prices, illustrating why the annual and monthly measures need to be distinguished.

The figures support a narrower conclusion than a general claim that living costs have fallen: annual inflation eased, but the overall price basket became more expensive during October.

The NDC’s National Campaign Council separately challenged the government’s fiscal management.

Spokesperson Chiogo Ikokwu cited figures attributed to the World Bank: ₦7.7 trillion in interest payments against ₦6.2 trillion in federal revenue in the first half of 2026. Those amounts yield a ratio of about 124 per cent.

The Finance Ministry had already disputed that interpretation in a statement dated 19 October.

It said the interest figure included obligations serviced for other tiers of government, including states’ external loans, while the revenue figure excluded income earned by agencies and enterprises but not yet remitted to the Treasury.

The ministry argued that the first-half comparison omitted some government revenue and did not reflect receipt timing across the full fiscal year. It cited faster revenue growth than interest growth and a projected full-year debt-service ratio of 46 per cent.

That projection covers interest and principal over a full year. It cannot be substituted directly for a six-month interest-only ratio.

Monday’s opposition statement renewed a dispute about the coverage of revenue and debt obligations. Resolving it requires comparable records for the same governments and period; neither the opposition’s calculation nor the ministry’s projection supplies that reconciliation on its own.

Toyo seeks campaign funds from ordinary contributors

In Calabar, ADC governorship candidate Nkoyo Toyo launched a public fundraising appeal while unveiling her manifesto and a proposed 30-year development plan.

She argued that dependence on wealthy sponsors could leave elected officials answering to private interests. Her preferred approach was to seek contributions from residents, including market traders and artisans.

The campaign’s Citizens-Led Campaign Fund also seeks support from Cross River people in the diaspora.

The proposal makes the source of campaign money part of her electoral argument. Public contributions would still need records showing what was received, who contributed and how the money was spent.

Her development plan identifies security, food sufficiency, enterprise, employment, education, healthcare, local government autonomy and roads as priorities.

The fundraising launch establishes a method of seeking support; it does not establish the amount raised or the cost of delivering those proposals.

Fundraising director Richard Inoyo said contributors would be entitled to demand an account of how their donations were used.

That provides a specific commitment for the campaign’s supporters to follow beyond the launch.

Benue court dismisses bid to bar Aondoakaa

A Federal High Court in Abuja dismissed a suit seeking to stop former Attorney-General of the Federation Michael Aondoakaa from contesting the Benue governorship election on the PDP platform.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that Justice Joyce Abdulmalik ruled on Monday that the plaintiffs lacked the legal standing to bring the action and had filed outside the applicable 14-day period for a pre-election challenge.

The four plaintiffs, describing themselves as registered voters, had sought orders compelling INEC and the PDP to prevent his candidature. They relied on an earlier Supreme Court judgement.

The judge held that they were not aspirants in the PDP primary and could not challenge its outcome through the action.

She also rejected their claim that they learnt of the nomination only on 30 August, noting that Mr Aondoakaa had been declared the primary winner on 24 June and received his certificate on 26 June. The court upheld the defendants’ preliminary objection and dismissed the suit.

What to watch next

Monday’s developments produced several tests that can be measured beyond the political statements accompanying them.

In Kano, the police have made arrests, but investigators must still establish responsibility for Sunday’s violence and determine whether the evidence supports prosecution.

The opposition coalition has fixed a date for signing its agreements, although the status of two documents previously proposed in August remains unexplained. Its 23 November summit will show whether the parties have resolved those questions or merely deferred them.

In Bauchi, Ibrahim Kashim’s move to the APC leaves questions about the NDC’s governorship nomination and campaign organisation. In Cross River, Nkoyo Toyo’s public fundraising appeal creates an opportunity to test whether the campaign will disclose its contributions and expenditure.

The economic dispute also remains open. The NDC’s debt-interest calculation and the Finance Ministry’s response use measures whose comparability requires further examination.

The common thread is accountability: whether arrests lead to credible investigations, political commitments produce verifiable agreements, and campaign promises can be measured against records rather than declarations.

World.title: Customers affected as JPMorgan Chase, United Airlines, others report widespread outages
World.content:
United Airlines and financial institutions, including JPMorgan Chase, have reported separate technology-related disruptions affecting banking services and flight operations in the United States.

JPMorgan Chase clarified that the disruption resulted from a software bug, not a cyberattack.

On Monday, thousands of JPMorgan Chase customers reported difficulty accessing their online accounts, while some also had trouble completing transactions at physical bank branches.

“We did not have access to our funds. Debit cards were declined in person at businesses, including for personal and business accounts. It made a mess,” James McGing complained in an X post.

Other social media users also reported disruptions at Chase branches; some local offices informed customers earlier that day that they were experiencing internal system problems.

Meanwhile, customers of other major banks, including Bank of America, Wells Fargo and U.S. Bank, also reported difficulties, although on a smaller scale.

Some customers additionally complained about problems sending and receiving money through Zelle, a US-based digital payment service.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

However, Zelle said its platform was operating normally, attributing the reported delays to individual banks and credit unions.

The service disruptions, occurring at nearly the same time, affected major financial institutions and other global enterprises, raising customer concerns about the reliability of their digital services.

Software bug

In an X post, JPMorgan Chase attributed the disruption to a software bug affecting its on-premise hardware systems, ruling out evidence of a cyberattack.

“JPMorganChase has experienced a temporary issue related to a software bug in on-premises hardware systems – there is no evidence this is cyber-related. It is taking longer than usual to service some customers.

“Where we were party to a transaction involving other banks, those banks may have been impacted, but this is not a systemic issue,” JPMorgan Chase said.

The investment banking company said customers still have access to their accounts and funds while it continues working to resolve the issue by the end of Tuesday.

Similarly, United Airlines, in a statement on Tuesday, also reported a separate technology-related disruption that affected some departing flights.

The airline said the technical issue had been resolved and advised passengers to check their flight status through its website or mobile application.

“Earlier today we experienced a technology-related issue that impacted some departing flights. The issue has been resolved,” the airline said.

The latest disruptions come barely a week after global software giant Microsoft experienced a worldwide outage on 13 November, affecting access to several of its services.

The company also attributed the incident to a technical issue arising from an earlier network capacity upgrade, ruling out a cyberattack.

The outage disrupted access to key services, including Microsoft Outlook, Teams, and Copilot, raising concerns about the reliability of its platforms.

World.title: Ex-governor Al-Makura threatens legal action against Nasarawa SSG
World.content:
Former Nasarawa State Governor, Umaru Al-Makura, has demanded the retraction of an alleged defamatory statement linking him to the disruption of Vice-President Kashim Shettima’s visit to the Emir of Lafia.

Mr Al-Makura also demanded a public apology from the Secretary to the Nasarawa State Government (SSG), Labaran Magaji, warning that he would institute legal proceedings if the demands were not met within seven days.

The demand comes amid escalating political rivalry between supporters of Governor Abdullahi Sule and those of former Inspector-General of Police Mohammed Adamu ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

The political disagreement, which centres on Mr Sule’s succession, has divided influential figures in the state’s ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

While Mr Sule backed Ahmed Wadada as his preferred successor, Mr Al-Makura supported Mr Adamu, pitting the two former political allies against each other in the succession battle.

Tensions intensified after Mr Wadada secured the APC governorship ticket, defeating Mr Adamu, who subsequently left the party to pick up the Social Democratic Party (SDP) ticket.

Mr Al-Makura’s alignment with the former police chief has further widened the political divide in the state, turning what began as an internal APC succession disagreement into a broader contest involving competing political camps.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The latest confrontation followed the reported disruption of activities surrounding Mr Shettima’s visit to Lafia on 4 November, during which the vice-president paid a courtesy visit to the Emir of Lafia as part of his engagement in the state.

The Nasarawa State Government subsequently accused some youths suspected of having links to Mr Al-Makura and Mr Adamu of sponsoring the disruption.

In a statement from the SSG’s office, the government described the incident as an attempt to embarrass the administration and directed security agencies to investigate and identify those responsible.

However, the allegations have been rejected by political associates of the two former public office holders, who described the government’s position as politically motivated.

In a letter dated 12 November, written by his counsel, Malla Makpa, and addressed to the SSG at the Government House, Lafia, Mr Al-Makura demanded the withdrawal of the allegation.

According to the letter, paragraph three of the government’s press statement expressly identified the former governor as one of the individuals suspected of sponsoring the disruption.

Mr Al-Makura’s lawyer described the allegation as grave and damaging, arguing that linking his client to the sponsorship of violence and the disruption of an official visit by the vice-president amounted to an imputation of criminal conduct.

The counsel argued that the expression “suspected to be sponsored” did not shield the government from potential liability for defamation, maintaining that the publication, read in its entirety, portrayed Mr Al-Makura as involved in orchestrating public disorder.

The letter further stated that the government had not presented any evidence, investigation report, witness account, financial transaction, communication or other verifiable material linking the former governor to the incident.

It also cited Section 24 of the Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention, etc.) Act, 2015, as amended in 2024, arguing that the electronic dissemination of the allegation increased its reach and potential damage to Mr Al-Makura’s reputation.

The counsel said his client reserved the right to submit the publication to relevant law enforcement agencies for independent assessment.

The letter maintained that the SSG did not have unrestricted authority to publish unsubstantiated allegations against citizens, adding that political differences could not override constitutionally guaranteed rights.

Among other demands, Mr Al-Makura asked the SSG to immediately withdraw the portion of the statement identifying him as a suspected sponsor of the disruption.

He also demanded an unequivocal public apology acknowledging that the allegation was published without publicly disclosed evidence to substantiate it.

The apology and retraction, according to the letter, must be published in at least two widely circulated national newspapers with prominence comparable to the original statement.

He further demanded that the government publish the retraction and apology on the same official websites, social media accounts and other online platforms used to circulate the disputed statement.

The former governor also asked the SSG to stop further publication or dissemination of the allegation unless it was supported by credible evidence and pursued through lawful procedures.

The letter gave the SSG seven days from receipt to comply, warning that failure to do so would leave Mr Al-Makura with no option but to pursue available legal remedies.

These, the counsel said, would include filing a civil suit for libel and defamation, seeking substantial and exemplary damages, obtaining injunctive reliefs and reporting the electronic publication to law enforcement agencies for investigation under the Cybercrimes Act and other relevant laws.

The letter said Mr Al-Makura would not allow his reputation to be damaged by what his counsel described as unsubstantiated allegations, adding that the former governor was prepared to seek legal protection against any perceived injury to his standing.

World.title: 2027: Six opposition parties plan pact as questions linger over earlier promises
World.content:
Six opposition political parties plan to formalise their cooperation at a summit in Abuja on 23 November, nearly three months after their first gathering produced commitments whose implementation remained unclear.

The Coalition for Democracy announced on Monday that the parties would adopt three documents covering political cooperation, democratic reforms and electoral integrity.

However, the announcement leaves unanswered questions raised in a PREMIUM TIMES investigation published on 22 October, which examined delays in producing five documents proposed at the coalition’s August summit.

The coalition has not explained whether the three documents now scheduled for adoption replace, combine or incorporate the original five.

In a statement issued on Monday, Salihu Lukman said the second summit would take place at the NAF Conference Centre, Abuja.

The participating parties are the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Allied Peoples Movement (APM), National Democratic Congress (NDC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) and Social Democratic Party (SDP).

However, TheCable identified the PDP participant as the Tanimu Turaki-led faction, amid the party’s continuing leadership dispute.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The three documents are the National Covenant for Democratic Renewal, the Framework for Opposition Unity and the National Reform Programme.

According to Mr Lukman, the coalition intends to replace informal political understandings with written commitments that can withstand disagreements among individual politicians.

The proposed pact does not establish that the parties have agreed to field a common presidential candidate against President Bola Tinubu.

From five documents to three

At the first summit, convened on 31 August by the G100 in collaboration with the House of Representatives Minority Caucus, the parties established working groups to prepare proposals for cooperation among opposition parties.

The five documents initially proposed were the National Covenant for Democratic Renewal, Single-Term Transition Charter, National Reform Programme, Framework for Opposition Unity and Roadmap to a Common Presidential Candidate.

The working groups were given four weeks to complete their assignments.

However, PREMIUM TIMES reported in October that the deadline had elapsed without independent confirmation that the documents had been completed, submitted or adopted.

The investigation also established that representatives of the six parties had consulted five presidential candidates: Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi, Seyi Makinde, Adewole Adebayo and Donald Duke.

Mr Lukman subsequently acknowledged that distrust among the parties and candidates remained an obstacle to cooperation.

Monday’s announcement indicates that working groups have prepared documents for consideration, but it does not account for the Single-Term Transition Charter or the Roadmap to a Common Presidential Candidate.

It also does not establish whether the parties have abandoned those proposals or intend to address them separately.

PREMIUM TIMES has not independently examined the three documents.

Their provisions on campaign financing, dispute resolution, electoral coordination and possible candidate arrangements therefore remain unknown.

Electoral integrity takes priority

The coalition identified protecting votes at polling units as its first joint undertaking.

It said opposition parties could cooperate to safeguard the electoral process despite their competing political interests.

However, the announcement did not explain how the proposed arrangement would operate, who would coordinate it or how its activities would be funded.

The coalition also accused the ruling APC of undermining democratic competition and electoral transparency. The allegations have not been independently established.

National chairpersons and secretaries of participating parties, members of their national working committees, presidential candidates, running mates and campaign officials are expected at the summit.

Representatives of the G100, the House of Representatives Minority Caucus, civil society organisations and the diplomatic community have also been invited.

According to Daily Nigerian, organisers have proposed a special session for presidential candidates to address the gathering and publicly affirm their commitment to the cooperation framework.

The attendance of individual candidates has not been independently confirmed.

Separate presidential ambitions

The planned agreement comes amid continuing negotiations among opposition presidential candidates.

In its State of the Race analysis published on Monday, PREMIUM TIMES examined consultations involving Atiku, Mr Makinde and Mr Obi, alongside the electoral deadlines and legal restrictions affecting attempts to present a common candidate.

Although Mr Makinde confirmed discussions with opposition figures, no joint ticket or common electoral programme had been announced.

The ADC faces another complication after the Federal High Court judgement of 5 November, which invalidated decisions associated with the David Mark-led party leadership.

The party has appealed the ruling, but the dispute continues to raise questions about its presidential nomination and the authority of officials acting on its behalf.

The unresolved litigation could complicate any agreement requiring commitments from party representatives whose authority is contested.

Nevertheless, cooperation on electoral integrity would not necessarily require the parties to withdraw their presidential candidates. Presenting a joint ticket would involve separate legal and political considerations.

The next test

The 23 November summit will test whether the participating parties can move beyond consultations and establish practical arrangements for cooperation.

One issue is whether their respective national leaderships have authorised representatives to sign agreements that could affect their electoral strategies.

Another is how the coalition intends to manage disagreements among parties that remain competitors in the presidential election.

The coalition has indicated that other political parties may join if they accept its principles of democratic renewal, constitutional governance and national reform.

For now, the clearest measure of progress will be the publication of the proposed agreements and an explanation of how they relate to the five documents promised in August.

World.title: Olympic Eagles, Super Eagles face crucial tests against DR Congo, Tanzania
World.content:
Nigeria’s two men’s national teams face important tests on Tuesday, with the Super Eagles seeking to strengthen their position in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying race against Tanzania, while the Olympic Eagles must overturn a two-goal deficit against the Democratic Republic of Congo to remain in contention for the U-23 AFCON and a possible return to the Olympic Games.

The Super Eagles travel to Amaan Stadium in Zanzibar for their Group L return fixture against Tanzania, while the Olympic Eagles host DR Congo at Remo Stars Stadium in Ikenne-Remo for the second leg of their 2027 U-23 AFCON qualifying tie.

Both matches are scheduled for Tuesday, 17 November, with the senior team kicking off at 2 p.m. Nigerian time and the U-23 side at 4 p.m.

Super Eagles seek vital points in Zanzibar

The Super Eagles head into the encounter with renewed confidence after beating Tanzania 3-1 at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo on Friday.

Alhassan Yusuf gave Nigeria an early lead in the second minute, finishing off an assist from Ademola Lookman. Tanzania equalised through Alphonce Msanga in the 32nd minute, but substitute Tolu Arokodare scored twice in the second half to secure the victory.

The result moved Nigeria to six points from three matches, one behind Group L leaders Guinea-Bissau, who have seven points. Madagascar have two points, while Tanzania have one.

Nigeria, however, cannot afford another setback in a group where only one qualification place is available to teams other than Tanzania, who have already secured a place at the finals as co-hosts.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The 2027 AFCON will be jointly hosted by Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda from 19 June to 17 July. Under the qualification format, the highest-placed team among Nigeria, Guinea-Bissau and Madagascar will join Tanzania from Group L.

That makes Tuesday’s fixture particularly important for the three-time African champions, who must keep pace with Guinea-Bissau and avoid allowing their rivals to open a wider gap.

Tanzania, despite having qualified automatically, will be keen to respond in front of their supporters. The Taifa Stars, coached by Miguel Ángel Gamondi, will also want to demonstrate their competitiveness against one of Africa’s established football nations.

Nigeria will be hoping to build on their improved performance in Uyo, although they must remain defensively organised and make better use of their attacking opportunities.

Olympic Eagles face uphill battle in Ikenne

For the Olympic Eagles, the challenge is more immediate. Nigeria must overturn a 2-0 first-leg defeat against DR Congo to advance to the final qualifying round of the 2027 U-23 Africa Cup of Nations.

The Congolese secured the advantage in Lubumbashi last Friday through two first-half goals, including a controversial own goal involving Nigerian goalkeeper Samuel James and a strike by Filozofe Mabete.

The result left Nigeria with a difficult task ahead of Tuesday’s return fixture at the Remo Stars Stadium.

The Olympic Eagles must win by at least three goals to progress without a penalty shootout. A two-goal victory would level the aggregate score at 2-2 and send the tie to penalties, while DR Congo need only avoid defeat to advance.

Nigeria will be counting on home support and a more effective attacking display after failing to convert their opportunities in the first leg.

The team also faces selection challenges after injuries to winger Zadok Yohanna and the departure of midfielder Daniel Daga, as his Norwegian club, Molde, requested his return.

The winner of the tie will advance to the third and final qualifying round, where they will face either Burkina Faso or Zambia in March 2027.

Olympic return at stake

The U-23 AFCON in Egypt will be more than a continental competition. It will also serve as Africa’s qualifying tournament for the men’s football event at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games.

Nigeria have a proud record in Olympic football, winning gold at Atlanta 1996, silver at Beijing 2008 and bronze at Rio 2016.

However, the country missed the last two editions, Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, making the current qualifying campaign an important opportunity to return to the global stage.

The 2027 tournament in Egypt will feature eight teams, with hosts Egypt automatically qualified and seven others to emerge from the qualifying rounds. Only the two finalists will secure Africa’s places at the Los Angeles Olympics following the reduction in the continent’s allocation.

For the Olympic Eagles, Tuesday’s encounter is therefore an important first step towards ending Nigeria’s Olympic absence.

While the Super Eagles seek to protect their AFCON qualification hopes in Zanzibar, the U-23 team must produce a significant turnaround in Ikenne. Both sides have little room for error as they pursue different but equally important targets for Nigerian football.

World.title: Gunmen kill Plateau security commander, one other
World.content:
Suspected gunmen have killed a newly graduated unit commander of Operation Rainbow, a Plateau State-owned civilian security outfit, and another resident in an ambush in Bokkos Local Government Area of the state.

The victims were reportedly attacked at about 3 p.m. on Monday while returning from a condolence visit to Hurti village to their community in Tadai, Manguna District of Bokkos LGA.

A community leader, Machief Paul, who confirmed the incident to journalists, said both victims were members of his community.

“They went to Hurti village for a condolence visit and were returning to Tadai when suspected gunmen ambushed and killed them,” Mr Paul said.

“They were killed in broad daylight this afternoon. It is very sad and unfortunate.”

Mr Paul disclosed that one of the deceased was a newly graduated unit commander of Operation Rainbow, adding that the killing had thrown the community into mourning.

“The commander had just graduated. We are deeply saddened by this incident, especially given the security challenges our people have continued to face,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The killing comes shortly after Operation Rainbow graduated 353 operatives who completed a retraining programme aimed at strengthening the outfit’s capacity to tackle insecurity across Plateau State.

The passing-out parade, held in Jos on 9 November, marked the completion of the first batch of the retraining exercise, which began about two months earlier.

The programme was designed to improve the operatives’ intelligence-gathering, threat detection, surveillance and emergency response capabilities, as well as enhance coordination with conventional security agencies.

Governor Caleb Mutfwang and the outfit’s coordinator, Nash Yakubu, a retired army brigadier general, were among the officials at the ceremony.

A conflict reporter from Bokkos, Masara Kim, also confirmed the killings, saying the two men were ambushed while returning from the condolence visit.

Mr Kim said the slain Operation Rainbow commander had recently completed the refresher training programme for unit commanders in Jos.

The killing comes amid persistent security challenges in parts of Plateau State, particularly communities in Bokkos and neighbouring areas that have experienced repeated attacks.

Several attempts to reach security authorities by phone for comment were unsuccessful at the time of filing this report.

World.title: Kano governor confirms dissolution of 20-year marriage with Kwankwaso’s niece
World.content:
​Governor Abba Yusuf of Kano State has confirmed the dissolution of his marriage to Zainab Kwankwaso, a niece of his former political mentor and former governor of the state, Rabiu Kwankwaso.

​The governor disclosed this on Monday while addressing pensioners at an event held at the Government House in Kano.

​Governor Yusuf likened the development to a demotion in marital rank, noting that having only one wife at the moment had reduced his status from a “corporal” to a “constable.”

​“Some days ago, I was being forced to become a constable. I want to thank the good people of Kano who advised me to keep two wives, but for now I have accepted one,” he said.

​Governor Yusuf, however, hinted at plans to remarry in the future.

​“But mark you, I will still add another wife. Some of you may not understand what the governor means here,” he remarked.

​Confirming that the divorce had been finalised, the governor revealed that the official dissolution notice had already been issued.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

​“The governor has agreed to divorce her. The paper for the dissolution has been issued,” he stated.

​“Pray for the governor to be blessed with a good wife with proper upbringing among the applicants so that he can continue with polygamy,” he added.

PREMIUM TIMES reported how Zainab approached an Abuja court seeking a divorce from Governor Yusuf.

She married Governor Yusuf in July, 2006, while he was a personal aide to her uncle, Mr Kwankwaso. The union lasted for 20 years and produced six children.

Ms Zainab is the daughter of Mr Kwankwaso’s late elder brother, Dahiru Kwankwaso, who died in an accident in 1985 on the Kano-Kaduna expressway.

World.title: NDC local government chairman, others join APC in Kano
World.content:
Local government executive members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Bichi Local Government Area of Kano State have defected to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

The defectors, including the party’s local government vice chairman, five ward chairmen, and several other grassroots leaders, were formally received into the APC by Abubakar Kabir, the member of the House of Representatives for the Bichi Federal Constituency.

Led by the NDC vice chairman in Bichi, Haladu Sa’adu, the delegation included the chairmen of Waire, Danzabuwa, Kaukau, Muntsira, and Bichi wards.

Other notable defectors were the party’s local treasurer, ward secretaries, women and youth leaders, and members of the Kwankwasiyya movement.

During the reception, the group formally announced their departure from the NDC and pledged their allegiance to the APC.

Speaking on behalf of the defectors, Abdulkadir Lawan, chairman of the ward chairmen’s forum and leader of Danzabuwa Ward, said Mr Kabir’s developmental projects and commitment to improving constituents’ lives influenced their decision.

He noted that after observing the lawmaker’s interventions across the constituency, they concluded his leadership offered a better platform for their political aspirations.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Lawan also highlighted the lawmaker’s scholarship and empowerment programmes, saying he had personally benefited from educational support through the Abubakar Kabir Foundation.

Additionally, he cited internal leadership challenges—specifically issues surrounding the position and influence of former Kano State Governor Rabiu Kwankwaso—as a key factor behind their exit.

Welcoming the defectors into the APC, Mr Kabir commended their bold step, particularly praising the local government vice chairman and the five ward chairmen.

He expressed appreciation for their confidence in his leadership, adding that their entry would strengthen the APC’s grassroots mobilisation and political structure in Bichi.

World.title: Fountain of Life Church removes Jimmy Odukoya as senior pastor
World.content:
The Board of Trustees of the Fountain of Life Church, Lagos, has removed Pastor Jimmy Odukoya as its senior pastor, citing a need to enforce the succession arrangements established by the church’s late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya.

The board announced the decision in a statement on Tuesday, saying it followed a review of the church’s constitution and the documented instructions left by the founder before his death in 2023.

According to the trustees, the review was aimed at ensuring that the church’s leadership succession reflected the founder’s wishes and complied with the provisions of its constitution.

The statement said, “Following a careful consideration of the relevant provisions of the Church’s Constitution and a review of the recorded instructions of our beloved Founder, the Board of Trustees has resolved to give effect to the succession arrangements which he made prior to his demise in 2023.”

The board consequently declared that Jimmy Odukoya was no longer recognised as the church’s senior pastor, with the decision taking immediate effect.

“Consequently, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya is no longer recognised as the Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church effective immediately,” it stated.

The trustees described the move as an institutional decision taken in the discharge of their responsibilities and in the best interests of the church.

They said the decision was necessary to uphold the church’s constitution, respect the founder’s wishes and protect the integrity of the succession framework he established.

“It is an institutional decision taken in the discharge of the Board’s responsibilities and in the best interests of the Church,” the statement added.

The board, however, did not disclose the specific succession arrangements left by the founder or announce who would take over the senior pastor position.

Vanguard Newspaper

World.title: Budget 2027: FG moves to slash overhead costs, directs MDAs to share facilities
World.content:
By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief

As the Federal Government (FG) prepares its 2027 Budget, it is stepping up efforts to cut overhead expenditure by directing Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) to maximise the use of existing government-owned facilities instead of spending public funds on hotels and other privately owned venues for official meetings.

The move is part of a broader cost-saving initiative by the Federal Ministry of Finance, through its Efficiency Office (E-Office), to eliminate avoidable expenditure, improve the utilisation of public assets and ensure value for money in government operations.

Efe Ovuakporie, Head, Information and Public Relations Unit of the Federal Ministry of Finance, in a statement in Abuja, yesterday, said “the Office is working towards establishing a coordinated system that will enable MDAs to identify and access available meeting and conference facilities across government institutions, thereby reducing the need to hire commercial venues for official engagements.”

She stated further: “A major component of the programme is the compilation of a comprehensive directory of meeting facilities owned by MDAs nationwide. The directory, which will be published on the Federal Ministry of Finance’s website upon completion, is expected to provide government institutions with information on available facilities and make it easier to locate suitable venues.

“The arrangement will also enable MDAs with under-utilised conference facilities to generate revenue by making them available to other government institutions, while reducing pressure on government overhead budgets.”

Ovuakporie said the initiative aligns with the Efficiency Office’s mandate to promote value for money, reduce overhead expenditure, monitor the utilisation of public assets and identify areas of waste across government institutions.

World.title: Customs officers must outsmart smugglers, go intelligence-led — Adeniyi
World.content:
Customs officers

Says technology should drive operations

By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief

The Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Mr. Adewale Adeniyi, has challenged officers of the Service to stay ahead of smugglers by adopting intelligence-led operations, deploying technology and strengthening professionalism in the discharge of their duties.

Adeniyi, who gave the charge at the inaugural Customs Police Summit in Abuja, yesterday, said criminal networks were becoming increasingly sophisticated, requiring Customs officers to devise smarter strategies to combat smuggling and other transnational crimes.

He said the era of relying largely on conventional enforcement methods was giving way to intelligence-driven operations capable of identifying and disrupting criminal networks.

His words: “Criminal networks have grown more sophisticated. They use the same routes as legitimate traders to move firearm components, narcotics, fake medicines, protected wildlife and illicit funds, often through digital channels. Our answers must be smarter; they must not be harder.”

The Customs boss called for a more professional, accountable and technology-driven Customs Police Unit (CPU) to tackle emerging security threats, combat illicit trade, strengthen institutional integrity and protect the nation’s borders.

He charged CPU personnel to demonstrate the highest standards of integrity, stressing that the Service must lead by example before demanding accountability from traders and members of the public.

“Before we demand integrity from traders and the public, we must show it ourselves,” he said.

Adeniyi also cautioned officers against abusing their enforcement powers, noting that the Nigeria Customs Service Act 2023 had conferred extensive police powers on the Service, which must be exercised within the limits of the law.

“Authority requires restraint. The NCS Act 2023 gives us sweeping police powers, but every search, arrest and detention must rest on lawful grounds and withstand public and judicial scrutiny,” he said.

He explained that enforcement and trade facilitation should complement each other, citing initiatives such as the One-Stop Shop and World Customs Organisation (WCO) instruments, including the Safe Framework of Standards, Authorised Economic Operator programmes, Advance Rulings, Time Release Studies and the Revised Kyoto Convention.

According to him, these instruments help reduce opportunities for abuse, corruption and arbitrary exercise of discretion.

The Customs boss said the Service had undergone meaningful structural renewal and remained committed to building a disciplined, responsive and professional police unit.

World.title: UBA intensifies fight against phishing, scam
World.content:
…as 2026 fraud awareness week begins

The United Bank for Africa (UBA) Plc, has stepped up its fight against fraud, urging customers and the public to stay alert to phishing scams where criminals increasingly use fake bank messages, cloned websites and impersonation accounts to steal account details and money.

To this end, the Bank is set to hold the 2026 edition of its Fraud Awareness Week, from Monday, November 16 to Friday, November 20, 2026, with the theme “Fraud Dynamics: Staying One Step Ahead.”

UBA’s Group Chief Internal Auditor, Eugene Inotu, who spoke ahead of the campaign, said the bank wants every customer to recognise a phishing or fraud attempt before it causes harm.

“Fraudsters are counting on panic. They want you to click before you think, so the strongest defence is to pause,” Inotu said. He added, “UBA will never ask for your PIN, password, OTP or BVN through a link, a text message, an email or a phone call. If a message asks for any of these, it is not from us, no matter how genuine it looks.”

Offering practical guidance, UBA’s Group Head, Brands, Marketing and Corporate Communications, Alero Ladipo, urged customers to treat every unsolicited link with suspicion and to confirm requests only through the Bank’s official channels.

She said, “Avoid clicking links in messages you did not ask for. Type the UBA website address directly into your browser or use the official UBA Mobile App, and download banking apps only from official app stores’’.

World.title: Pique says Owono’s 12-match ban after De Miguel death is unfair
World.content:
FC Andorra’s majority shareholder Gerard Pique criticised Jesus Owono’s 12-match ban following a fatal collision with Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, saying it unfairly blamed the goalkeeper for “consequences that were not his fault”.

Equatorial Guinea international Owono was sent off in a Spanish second division clash on November 2 after racing into midfield and colliding heavily with De Miguel while trying to clear.

De Miguel, 30, was placed in intensive care in hospital and died the next day, plunging football into shock and mourning.

In a video posted to TikTok late on Monday, former Spain and Barcelona great Pique said the Spanish football federation’s punishment put Owono “in a situation that isn’t fair”.

“What it does is blame Jesus for consequences which were not his fault,” Pique said in his first public comments on the decision.

“I think the punishment should be for the action, not for the consequences,” added Pique, who compared the tragedy in Tenerife to a similar incident which led to a shorter ban.

Owono, 25, has said he is enduring the “hardest days of my life” after De Miguel’s death, which Pique described as an “accident” that was “totally inexplicable”.

FC Andorra coach Carles Manso said the goalkeeper will decide if and when he returns to football after the tragedy

“Jesus will need more than 12 games in order to be available and compete,” said Pique.

“No suspension will bring Demi back to us,” added Pique, referring to De Miguel by a popular nickname.

Spanish police sources have told AFP an investigation into what happened had been opened under judicial supervision, a standard procedure for unnatural deaths.

World.title: Polysmart commissions 60,000mt food-grade rPET plant
World.content:
…as FCMB provides N40bn financing

Polysmart Packaging Limited has commissioned a plant with an annual production capacity of 60,000 tonnes of food-grade recycled polyethylene terephthalate (rPET) in Ileke town, Ogun State, with N40 billion in machinery and working-capital financing from First City Monument Bank (FCMB).

The facility, which Polysmart describes as Africa’s largest plastic recycling plant, will convert recovered post-consumer plastic waste into food-grade recycled PET materials for manufacturers.

It is expected to strengthen local packaging production, support plastic-waste recovery and reduce dependence on imported raw materials.

At the commissioning ceremony on October 29, Minister of Environment Balarabe Lawal, said the facility would enhance Nigeria’s capacity to recover and recycle plastic waste while supporting the country’s environmental sustainability objectives.

Ogun State Governor Dapo Abiodun described the investment as a demonstration of Nigerian enterprise, innovation and the opportunities created by a supportive investment environment.

Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of FCMB, Yemisi Edun, said the Bank’s support reflects its commitment to financing businesses that combine industrial development with environmental responsibility and economic opportunity.

“At FCMB, we believe that financing sustainable businesses is essential to building a resilient economy and securing long-term shared prosperity.

By converting recovered plastic into new products, this plant shows how manufacturing and environmental responsibility can work together,” Edun said.

She added, “Polysmart embodies our commitment to sustainable manufacturing practices, environmental sustainability and wealth creation, reflected in our ₦40 billion in funding for machinery and working capital.”

Polysmart Group Managing Director, Wasiu Balogun, said the investment demonstrates the capacity of Nigerian businesses to develop recycling infrastructure that serves local industry and creates opportunities across the waste-recovery chain.

“This is climate action made in Nigeria. The investment demonstrates the capacity of Nigerian businesses to develop world-class recycling infrastructure,” Balogun said.

He added, “At full capacity, the facility will process up to 100,000 tonnes of mixed plastics annually, equivalent to about 6.5 billion bottles.”

World.title: NGX Group acquires 10% strategic stake in Nairobi Securities Exchange
World.content:
By Peter Egwuatu

Nigerian Exchange Group Plc (NGX Group) has acquired a 10% equity stake in the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE), a strategic investment that extends the Group’s participation in East Africa and advances its pan-African growth strategy.

The NGX, in a statement stressed that the strategic investment aligns with its priority of building regional leadership through partnerships and African market integration, strengthening its investment presence across West and East Africa.

“This latest development builds on NGX Group’s strategic investment in the Ethiopian Securities Exchange (ESX), further demonstrating the Group’s long-term commitment to participating in the development and growth of African capital market infrastructure” the statement added.
