On the strategic rationale, the NGX explained that the acquisition provides it with exposure to one of East Africa’s most established capital markets, broadening its investment portfolio beyond Nigeria and positioning the Group to benefit from the long-term growth of the region’s capital markets and increasing financial integration across the continent.

Commenting on the investment, Alhaji Umaru Kwairanga, Group Chairman, NGX Group, said: “African capital markets are at an inflection point, where integration is moving from aspiration to architecture. Exchange groups that commit patient capital to market infrastructure will help shape how capital flows across the continent. Our investment in the Nairobi Securities Exchange is a disciplined, long-term step in that direction, strengthening the financial linkages between West and East Africa while creating opportunities for sustainable shareholder value.”

Temi Popoola, Group Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, NGX Group, said: “This investment reflects our strategy to build a more diversified and resilient exchange group with a stronger presence across African markets.

Kenya is a cornerstone of East Africa’s financial ecosystem, and our investment in NSE provides exposure to its long-term growth potential while broadening our sources of investment returns beyond Nigeria. Both markets have already shown what closer collaboration can achieve for issuers and investors and a shareholding relationship gives that collaboration permanence. We remain focused on disciplined capital allocation and investments that deliver sustainable value to our shareholders over the long term.”

World.title: Inflation rate moves in divergent positions
World.content:
Drops year-on-year, rises month-on-month

By Elizabeth Adegbesan

The National Bureau of Statistics, NBS, has disclosed that Nigeria’s headline inflation rate dropped to 14.06 percent in October 2026 from 14.63 percent in the previous month.

NBS stated this in its latest Consumer Price Index, CPI, Report noting that food inflation also declined to 19.13 percent from 19.59 percent in September.

However, Month-on-Month, MoM, inflation rate rose by 0.43% in October, up by 0.38 percentage point from 0.06 percent recorded in September 2026.

This increase also reflected in the MoM trend in food inflation for October.

NBS stated: “In October 2026, the Headline inflation rate stood at 14.06 percent, down from 14.63 percent in September 2026 and stood at 18.97 percent in the same month of the preceding year (October 2025).

“Looking at the movement, the October 2026 Headline inflation rate showed a decrease of 4.9 percent compared to the October 2025 (18.97 percent) Headline inflation rate.

“On a month-on-month basis, the Headline inflation rate in October 2026 was 0.43 percent, which was 0.38 percent higher than the rate recorded in September 2026 (0.06 percent).

“This means that in October 2026, the rate of increase in the average price level was higher than the rate of increase in the average price level in September 2026.”

On food inflation, NBS, said: “The Food inflation rate in October 2026 was 19.13 per cent on a year-on-year basis and stood at 16.3 per ent in the same month of the preceding year (October 2025). “However, on a MoM basis, the Food inflation rate in October 2026 was -0.75 percent , up by 0.80 percent points from September 2026 (-1.55 per cent).

“This can be attributed to the rate of change in the average prices of the following products: vegetable oil (75cl), Titus sardines (125g), green peas (Prepacked), mackerel frozen, croakers (apo), rice local, catfish fresh, beef tripes, palm oil (75cl), millet flour (sold loose), etc”

In October 2026, food inflation on a year-on-year basis was highest in Ondo (31.74 percent), Lagos (31.43 percent), and Imo (29.75 percent), while Nasarawa (3.7 percent), Bayelsa (7.11 percent) and Kano (7.13 percent) recorded the slowest rise in food inflation on a Year-on-Year basis.

“On a MoM basis, however, October 2026 food inflation was highest in Yobe (18.41 percent), Kebbi (16.45 percent), and Borno (13.96 percent), while Lagos (-5.93 percent), Plateau (-5.83 percent), and Benue (-5.49 percent) recorded the slowest rise in Food inflation on a Month-on-Month basis.”

World.title: NSITF Takes Employees’ Compensation Scheme to Informal Sector, Enrolls 2,133 MSMEs
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Dike Onwuamaeze

The Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF) has registered 2,133 Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) between January and September 2026 as part of its efforts to bring more Nigerian workers in the informal economy under the Employees’ Compensation Scheme (ECS).

The Managing Director and Chief Executive of NSITF, Mr. Oluwaseun Faleye, disclosed this while addressing participants at the 40th Lagos International Trade Fair being held at Tafawa Balewa Square, Lagos.

Faleye said the registration of the additional enterprises reflected the NSITF’s determination to extend the benefits of social protection beyond large corporations and established institutions to smaller businesses and workers who are often more exposed to occupational and economic vulnerabilities.

Speaking on the theme, “The Employee at the Centre of Growth, Secured by the Employees’ Compensation Scheme,” Faleye stressed that sustainable economic development could only be achieved when the people responsible for creating wealth and driving enterprise were adequately protected.

Faleye used the occasion to educate traders, artisans, small-business owners, market operators, transport operators and entrepreneurs on the benefits of the scheme, particularly those who might not fully understand its provisions or registration requirements.

He said that the scheme provided for medical treatment and healthcare, compensation for temporary or permanent disability, rehabilitation and vocational support, as well as benefits for eligible dependants in cases of death arising from work-related injuries or diseases.

Faleye stressed that employees were not expected to contribute towards the cost of their protection, as the law placed the responsibility for the one per cent contribution on employers.

He urged employers, particularly operators of small businesses and informal-sector enterprises, to understand that their obligations under the Employees’ Compensation Act did not disappear because they operated from market stalls, workshops, small shops or modest production facilities.

“If you employ people, their safety and welfare matter, and the statutory obligations under the Employees’ Compensation Act remain relevant,” he said.

The NSITF chief executive said the expansion of social protection was particularly important given the dominant position of informal employment in Nigeria’s labour market.

He remarked that many of these workers operated outside conventional social protection arrangements, with some unaware of the existence of the Employees’ Compensation Scheme and others lacking sufficient information about its benefits and accessibility.

He said the NSITF had consequently intensified efforts to engage MSMEs as an important pathway towards extending social protection to the wider informal economy.

According to him, the fund would continue taking its message to markets, workshops, trade associations, business clusters and other locations where Nigerians work and earn their livelihoods.

World.title: Rotary District 9111to Celebrate Humanitarian Champions
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

The Rotary International District 9111 is set to celebrate outstanding humanitarian contributions and promote the power of impactful storytelling at the 2026 Humanitarian Reporting and Awards (HRA) ceremony, scheduled for Thursday, December 3, 2026 in Lagos.

The prestigious ceremony, which will commence at 10:00 a.m, is themed, “Getting Better Mileage for Rotary’s Humanitarian Activities.” It is designed to recognise individuals whose contributions have made meaningful differences in the lives of others, while highlighting the crucial role of the media and public communication in amplifying humanitarian efforts.

The distinguished Publisher of Ovation International Magazine, Chief Dele Momodu, will chair the occasion, while Publisher of TheCable, Mr. Simon Kolawole, will deliver the keynote address as guest speaker.

The event will also feature an impressive array of distinguished personalities as special guests of Honour. They include: Chief Femi Adesina, former Special Adviser on Media and Publicity to the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria and former Managing Director of The Sun Newspapers; Mrs. Funke Egbemode, former Commissioner for Information, Osun State, and former Managing Director of New Telegraph Newspapers; and Mr. Gbenga Adefaye, Provost of the Nigerian Institute of Journalism and former Editor of Vanguard Newspapers.

Adding a unique blend of glamour, entertainment and inspiration to the ceremony, some of Nigeria’s most celebrated showbiz personalities, including Ali Baba, Charles Inojie, Gbenga Adeyinka, Julius Agwu, Segun Arinze and Omo Baba, among others, will be in attendance and honoured for their invaluable contributions to humanity.

The District Governor of Rotary International, District 9111, Rotarian Bukola Bakare, will serve as the chief host.

Beyond the glamour and recognition, the 2026 HRA Ceremony promises to be a powerful celebration of Rotary’s enduring philosophy of Service Above Self. It will provide a platform to acknowledge humanitarian champions, encourage greater collaboration between Rotary and the media, and explore innovative ways of communicating Rotary’s life-changing interventions to a wider audience.

The ceremony is also expected to reinforce the importance of effective humanitarian reporting in inspiring public participation, attracting support for worthy causes and ensuring that the stories of hope, compassion and transformation generated by Rotary reach far beyond the communities where its projects are implemented.

In an invitation to Rotarians across the districts, the Chairman of the HRA 2026 Organising Committee, Azuh Arinze, expressed delight at the forthcoming event, describing it as an opportunity for Rotarians to come together in fellowship, celebrate humanitarian excellence and collectively strengthen the visibility and impact of Rotary’s service initiatives.

He warmly called on all Rotarians to attend in large numbers, support the initiative and celebrate individuals whose commitment to humanity continues to make the world a better place.

“ This promises to be more than an awards ceremony. It is a celebration of Service Above Self, a recognition of humanitarian impact and an opportunity to explore how Rotary can tell its story better and achieve greater mileage for its life-changing interventions,” Arinze stated.

He further urged Rotarians and other stakeholders to embrace the occasion as a collective responsibility to amplify the Rotary story and inspire even greater acts of service

The 2026 Humanitarian Reporting and Awards Ceremony is expected to attract Rotarians, media professionals, public relations practitioners, entertainment industry stakeholders, humanitarian advocates and other distinguished guests from across the country.

World.title: APC Chieftain Tackles Amaechi, Says Delegating Duties Shows Leadership, Not Ineptitude
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

A member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Rivers State, Princewill Dike, has dismissed former Minister of Transportation and African Democratic Congress (ADC) vice-presidential candidate Chibuike Amaechi’s criticism of President Bola Tinubu’s leadership style, describing delegation of responsibilities as a hallmark of effective leadership.

Dike, a member of the Presidential/Rivers Rainbow Coalition Campaign Council, was reacting to Amaechi’s account of working with Tinubu during the 2015 presidential campaign, in which the former minister reportedly questioned the president’s approach to assigning responsibilities.

Dike, in a statement issued yesterday, said interpreting delegation as a sign of incapacity was a “fundamental misunderstanding” of leadership.

“To interpret the delegation of responsibilities as a sign of ineptitude shows a misunderstanding of the principles of leadership,” he said.

According to him, effective leaders are distinguished by their ability to identify competent people, assign responsibilities, and harness their expertise to achieve results.

“No successful leader can personally undertake every responsibility,” Dike said.

He cited biblical examples, including Moses’ delegation of administrative responsibilities following Jethro’s counsel in Exodus 18, as evidence that shared responsibility was a long-established leadership principle.

“Moses accepted the advice and appointed leaders over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens, thereby establishing a system of shared responsibility that made administration more effective and reduced his burden.

“Delegation of duties is key in governance,” he said.

Turning to the 2027 elections, Dike urged opposition politicians to focus on presenting credible economic and development policies rather than personal attacks on Tinubu.

He said those seeking to govern Nigeria should demonstrate preparedness by offering Nigerians “concrete policy proposals” capable of addressing the country’s challenges.

Dike also expressed confidence in Tinubu’s political prospects, while describing the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, as an important factor in the political calculations ahead of the 2027 presidential election.
