World.title: 5 takeaways from interview with Spanish election favorite Feijóo
World.content:
POLITICO’s interview with Feijóo revealed a cautious leader who abides by his deals with the far-right Vox party, with which he is likely to form a coalition if he wins later this month.

He signaled he would seek to repair the toxic relationship between Spain and Donald Trump under Sánchez — but was at pains not to appear too deferential to a U.S. president who is deeply unpopular in Spain.

Here are the five key takeaways from the interview.

Time to probe the national accounts

Feijóo said he didn’t “believe the data” on public spending and pledged to conduct an audit of Spain’s accounts within his first 100 days in power.

Referring to 2011, the last time the People’s Party succeeded the Socialist Party and had to revise the budget deficit upward, Feijóo said he would take “this history into account.”

“I know full well that they lied to us in 2011,” he added.

World.title: More than cash: EU defense spending push is ‘game-changer’ for industry, says arms boss
World.content:
Routila, who took over Patria in April, said it was extremely important that the EU’s next Multiannual Financial Framework “will lead to something. And something is not regulation only, something is clear products.”

Like many other defense companies, the Finnish group has seen sales and profits soar following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. That war also saw Finland break with its past military nonalignment and join NATO in 2023.

The need to continue supplying Ukraine and the uncertainty about the U.S. commitment to European security under President Donald Trump are adding to the pressure to rearm.

A firefighter works to put out a fire at a residential building in Kyiv after a Russian attack, on Nov. 12, 2026. | Sergii Volskyi/AFP via Getty Images

The scale of the European rearmament means there is a need to dramatically increase production. Routila argued that this would not be a major obstacle once companies receive more orders and greater long-term investment certainty.

“It’s a problem that is solvable,” he said, comparing the scale of defense firms to the much larger vehicle industry. “The automotive companies, they make millions of vehicles a year. We make thousands of vehicles per year. So the magnitude of volume is different.”

Patria has already increased its production, but “I would not say that we are yet working on top limit of our capacity. If there’s a good customer, we can still get orders,” he said.

World.title: I took the EU selection test. Here’s how it went.
World.content:
With just 1,490 places on the final reserve list, competition has never been tougher. The cost is high: months, if not years, of studying and stress. But the payoff could be a job for life and a monthly starting salary of around €6,000, almost tax-free.

Last week, I was one of hundreds of thousands of candidates from across the EU to sit the hour-long first round, hoping to advance in the so-called competition. Here’s how it went.

The run-up

Preparing for the reasoning tests involves navigating a hefty application manual, intense studying, and joining Facebook groups.

Understanding the application process and how the tests work can feel like a test in itself. Candidates are expected to pore over the 24-page “Notice of Competition,” the subsequent “Notice amending the Notice of Competition” — yes, you read that right — and a 28-page document explaining how to take the online tests. And that’s all before you even start studying.

Anyone hoping to pass knows they need to practice. With frequent flashbacks to my high-school years, I sat down to remind myself how to calculate percentages, interpret bar charts, and work out which shape comes next in a sequence.

I’ll be honest: I took a fairly relaxed approach to preparing. But I did spend about 20 minutes a day practicing and revisited tips and tricks I’d learned in previous EU tests in the week leading up to the exam.

World.title: EU’s Kallas fights to find a role in Ukraine peace talks
World.content:
After weeks of agonized debates over who should lead U.S.-brokered talks between Russia and Ukraine, European Council President António Costa announced in Dublin last week that the team would include national security advisers from France, Germany, Poland, Italy and the U.K., plus representatives from the European Commission and Council. Kallas was not among them.

The foreign ministers of Spain and Lithuania both criticized this approach as they arrived at a gathering in Brussels on Monday. “Europe needs one voice. We cannot speak with 27 microphones,” said Lithuanian Foreign Minister Kęstutis Budrys. “We need one and for that we need a clear mandate, clear procedures, [for] how we are agreeing on our joint position.”

‘Part of a mega-trend’

Some EU diplomats point to Kallas’s criticism of U.S. President Donald Trump’s administration as part of the reason she isn’t on the negotiation team. Others say the team is deliberately made up of national security officials who report directly to leaders, noting that U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has not been involved in recent rounds of talks.

While one national official involved in talks with Russia said Kallas was too divisive to be included, two EU diplomats argued the choice reflected a broader downgrading of foreign policy officials in global affairs. They were granted anonymity to speak frankly about the negotiating strategy, like others in the story.

“This is part of a mega-trend that’s hard to fight,” said one of the diplomats. “More and more international questions that were once handled by foreign ministers are now being handled by prime ministers or presidents.”

The key for Kallas and EU foreign ministers is to seek relevance by providing “geopolitical strategic perspective” on issues, even if they aren’t being directly consulted, the diplomat said.

World.title: French presidential rivals take aim at Le Pen in debate
World.content:
The most heated moment came when Le Pen detailed her plans to require charities that receive public money to refrain from meddling with politics.

“Your model is the same as that of your friends, Mr. Orbán and others, which is ultimately to shut up and stop those who do not think like you,” said Attal.

“You’ve got a list,” retorted Mélenchon, when Le Pen said she would deliver a list of charities she believed were too political.

Le Pen appeared to be playing it safe during the debate, trying to avoid being dragged into a damaging fight with her opponents. Her most pointed attacks targeted Attal, who is the leader of President Emmanuel Macron’s party Renaissance and was briefly prime minister in 2024.

“I don’t have any lessons to learn from someone who spent 10 years creating the biggest debt in the history of this country,” Le Pen said to Attal.

Le Pen and Mélenchon, who is polling in second place and could end up facing the far-right leader in the presidential runoff, avoided directly confronting each other during the debate.

World.title: Trump kicks off Asia tour ahead of major talks with Putin, Xi in China
World.content:
Skip next section Trump hints at possible meeting with North Korea's Kim Jong Un in China

11/17/2026 November 17, 2026 Trump hints at possible meeting with North Korea's Kim Jong Un in China

US President Donald Trump suggested he might meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in China, in remarks made before departing for his Asia tour. Trump met Kim three times during his first term in office.

"We may meet with Kim Jong Un also, so that'll be good," Trump told reporters, adding that whether Kim would make the trip was "up to President Xi" of China.

Meanwhile, China said it has "no information" on whether Trump would meet Kim.

Trump's remarks came just as North Korean state media reported that Kim and his family, accompanied by party officials, travelled to a tourist zone near North Korea's northern border with China on Sunday and Monday.

Pictures showed Kim sitting on an armchair, grinning with a cigarette in his hand and sunglasses on at what appeared to be a ski resort.

Kim Jong Un was reportedly at a ski resort at North Korea's northern border with China on Sunday and Monday Image: KCNA/REUTERS

While Trump has built up meetings before which didn't take place, analysts say the likelihood of Kim's appearance went up after ⁠Russia's ⁠Interfax news agency quoted the Kremlin saying Russian President Vladimir Putin could meet Kim if the North Korean leader attended this week's APEC summit.

The Kremlin "wouldn't do that unless they were certain he was going to meet," said Sydney Seiler, a former US national intelligence officer for North Korea, now at the Center for Strategic and International Studies. "I'm pretty confident something's underway."

World.title: Canada, China agree to ease tariffs amid trade rows with US
World.content:
The Canadian and Chinese leaders have vowed closer cooperation as both nations seek to reduce reliance on the US. Canada's government said it had agreed to further reduce tariffs on a range of products.

Talks between Chinese President Xi Jinping and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen have produced deals to further reduce tariffs, Ottawa said on Tuesday.

The agreements reflect a growing rapprochement between the two countries after years of strained relations, thanks totrade tensions with Washington leading both Canada and China to seek to reduce dependence on the US.

At the talks, Carney hailed "greater predictability and stability" in ‌relations with China, while Xi said the cooperation between his country and Canada would "benefit not only our two countries but also Asia-Pacific and the world."

Carney said Canada had already made faster-than-expected progress toward its goal of boosting exports to China "by 50% by the end of this decade."

What have China and Canada agreed on?

According to a statement from the Canadian government, China is to reduce tariffs on Canadian pork, fish and seafood.

In exchange, Canada will prolong the current tariff exemptions for Chinese steel and aluminum for another two years.

The two leaders also agreed to cooperate more closely on economic and financial matters, and to work together in the fields of education and environmental protection.

Canada is too reliant on the United States, Carney tells DW To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Growing China-Canada rapprochement

Xi and Carney already declared their intention to enhance bilateral ties during talks in Beijing in January.

There, they struck a deal that foresaw a reduction in tariffs on Canadian agricultural products, while Chinese electric vehicles gained easier access to the Canadian market.

Critics in Canada have, however, pointed out what they see as dangers to the country's security and values through the closer ties to Beijing.

Among other things, Canadian intelligence believes that China interfered in at least two federal elections, something Beijing denies.

World.title: India news: Modi to attend ASEAN, Quad meet in Manila
World.content:
Skip next section Andhra Pradesh to be hit by third cyclone 'Akvan'

11/17/2026 November 17, 2026 Andhra Pradesh to be hit by third cyclone 'Akvan'

Cyclone Akvan is expected to bring heavy rainfall to several parts of Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu Image: ANI/IMAGO

The southern state of Andhra Pradesh is bracing itself for the cyclone Akvan — the third to hit the state within three weeks.

The system is moving north-northwestwards over the central parts of the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal. It is expected to get stronger over the next two days as it moves towards the Andhra Pradesh coast.

Akvan is expected to make landfall on November 20 as a "very severe cyclonic storm," according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD).

The IMD has issued a red alert for several districts, warning of extremely heavy rainfall on November 20.

As a precautionary measure, the IMD has suggested a total suspension of fishing operations near the Bay of Bengal until November 20.

The cyclone will bring heavy rainfall to parts of the adjoining states of Odisha and Tamil Nadu.

World.title: Mongolian President Khurelsukh to resign amid corruption allegations
World.content:
Khurelsukh has said he will step down over accusations that he profited from a government railway project, but said he had been "falsely accused."

Mongolian President Khurelsukh Ukhnaa said Tuesday that he would resign after the opposition Democratic Party accused him of profiting from a government railway project.

At a press conference, Khurelsukh said he was being "falsely accused and defamed" but would resign in order to "restore my good name."

He has pledged to cooperate with investigators.

Before the resignation takes effect, it must first be accepted by parliament, the State Great Khural.

What are the accusations against Khurelsukh?

Nyambaatar Khishgee, the ex-mayor of Ulaanbaatar, the country's capital, on Saturday accused Khurelsukh of receiving $25 million (around €23 million) linked to the Tavantolgoi-Gashuunsukhait railway project.

The railway connects the Tavantolgoi coal mine with the Mongolian port of Gashuunsukhait on the Chinese border, a central hub for the export of coal from Mongolia to China.

The former mayor belongs to the president's party, but is part of a different faction within it.

The opposition Democratic Party picked up on the accusations and called on Khurelsukh to step down.

According to the allegations, Khurelsukh received the money in bribes from the conglomerate Bodi International LLC, which received the contract to construct the railway without a competitive tender.

Bodi on Monday denied having paid any cash bribes to obtain the contract.

Infighting in Khurelsukh's party

Khurelsukh, from the Mongolian People's Party, has been president since 2021.

But infighting has caused disruption in the party in recent years, with three prime ministers taking office in just nine months.

Khurelsukh paid a state visit to Germany from October 19 to 22 this year.

World.title: Japan scrambles jets to counter suspected Russian aircraft
World.content:
Japan said it lodged a "very stern protest" with Moscow after two suspected Russian aircraft violated Japanese airspace.

Japan scrambled fighter jets in its airspace after two suspected Russian aircraft entered its territory on Tuesday morning, an incident that could further strain ties between the two countries.

Tokyo said it had lodged a "very stern protest" with Moscow after the incident.

Japan lodges protest against Russia over alleged airspace violation

The aircraft entered Japan's airspace near Okinoshima in southwestern Japan shortly after 4:00 a.m. local time Tuesday (1900 GMT Monday), Japanese ​Chief Cabinet ‌Secretary Minoru Kihara ‌said.

"The violation of our national airspace by Russian aircraft is not only a grave infringement of our country's sovereignty, but also a threat to our security and is completely unacceptable," Kihara said.

"We lodged a very stern protest with Russia through diplomatic channels and strongly demanded measures to prevent any recurrence," he said.

Japan had lodged a similar protest with Russia in 2024 after a Russian patrol plane entered its airspace three times, marking the first confirmed incursion since 2019.

Kihara said the aircraft travelled through the Tsushima Strait and went between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan before heading to the Pacific.

Strains increasing in Japan-Russia ties

Japan's relations with Moscow have soured over the past weeks after a Japanese journalist was arrested on spying allegations and after Russia seized four of Japan Tobacco's Russian assets.

Russia and Japan share a decades-old dispute over the status of a number of islands in the Pacific Ocean.

However, relations especially deteriorated further after Tokyo joined global sanctions against Moscow over its war in Ukraine.

South Korea says Russian aircraft entered defense zone

Tuesday's reported violation comes soon after South Korea said it too had deployed fighter jets and conducted tactical maneuvers after several Russian military aircraft entered its air defense zone in the early hours of Tuesday.

An air defense zone is not sovereign airspace but a buffer area in which countries identify approaching aircraft for security purposes.

Military aircraft are generally expected to notify the relevant country before entering its air defense zone, though this is not legally required.

A government meeting is expected to take place soon following the strike on the Kerch bridge, Russian state media agency TASS reported.

"A meeting of the government commission on the aftermath of the attack on the Crimean Bridge, chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin, will be held soon at Government House," TASS quoted the Russian government as saying.

"The meeting will address issues related to the restoration of the Crimean Bridge and the organization of transport links," TASS reported.

The extent of the damage caused is not yet known and Russian officials have only confirmed that a strike had taken place and that traffic has been disrupted.

World.title: Germany beat Netherlands 5-0 to win Nations League group
World.content:
Florian Wirtz scored twice as Germany cruised to a comfortable 5-0 win over the Netherlands to qualify for the Nations League quarter-finals on Monday.

Germany dominated neighbor and historic rival the Netherlands in their Nations League quarterfinal match-up at Berlin's Olympic Stadium on Monday evening.

It was the team's sixth game under head coach Jürgen Klopp and the 50th ever between the two sides.

Germany's 5-0 shellacking of the Oranje was their most lopsided victory since 1959, when they won 7-0. In all, Germany have now won 19 of those matches, the Netherlands have won 12, and 18 ended in a draw.

Speaking to German broadcaster ARD after the game, attacking midfielder Florian Wirtz — who scored twice in the fixture — said: "We hope that we can make it fun for the fans. It was definitely fun for us, especially in the second half."

Despite the loss, Xavi Hernandez's Dutch side will reach the final eight alongside Germany.

Prior to the match, Klopp had made it clear that he and his team were approaching Monday's showdown as a final after having lost to Greece 1-0 in his first home game in the job on September 27.

By night's end, Derry Scherhant and Nico Schlotterbeck each scored once and Brajan Gruda scored once and added two assists on top of Wirtz's double.

Klopp has been high on Wirtz, who has come under fire for not delivering at Liverpool since his arrival there in June 2025, and his bet seems to be paying off with the 23-year-old now scoring four goals in his last four games for Germany.

"We don't care who we play. We want to play attacking football. We want to score goals and dominate the opponent. And I think we did that perfectly," said Wirtz on Monday evening before adding: "We want to keep going next year. We want to get better. I think we've taken some great steps in our development as a team."

World.title: United Airlines resolves tech outage that delayed flights
World.content:
United Airlines said a system outage that delayed departures has been resolved. The disruption came on the heels of a stoppage that halted all flights to and across the US for five hours last week.

United Airlines said it has resolved a "widespread system outage" that affected hundreds of departing flights on Monday.

Flight tracker FlightAware said 418 United flights were delayed on Monday afternoon.

The issue comes three days after a malfunction in the Federal Aviation Administration's network grounded flights across the US on Friday.

What did United Airlines say about Monday's tech issues?

United Airlines said there was "no indication" that Monday's outage was the result of a cyberattack.

There was also no indication that the issues affecting United Airlines on Monday were related to Friday's nationwide shutdown.

US lifts nationwide air travel ground stop, but disruptions continue To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

United Airlines said later on Monday that it had "resolved a technology issue that delayed flight departures."

The airline added that airborne flights, as well as those operated by its regional brand United Express, were not affected.

The disruption on Friday and Monday highlights how vulnerable air travel is to tech failures.

Disruption follows other recent major tech meltdowns

United Airlines' computer problem comes amid other recent similar high-profile technology meltdowns, including Friday's nationwide grounding.

Thousands of people in the US said they were unable to access their online banking accounts at several large US banks after JPMorgan Chase reported a technical issue.

On Thursday, Microsoft saw a major disruption to its services, including its Outlook email and Teams messenger.

The tech company said Saturday that its services had been fully restored.

World.title: La batalla por el voto útil reabre las brechas del bloque de izquierdas
World.content:
El Frente Amplio, debilitado en las encuestas, se revuelve contra el PSOE por copiar propuestas y ocupar su espacio mientras en la derecha también se recrudece la batalla entre PP y Vox

Pedro Sánchez quiere repetir la hazaña de 2023 con un esquema de campaña bastante similar a aquel, con una llamada a la movilización de la izquierda para frenar la llegada de la ultraderecha al poder. Sin embargo, hay cambios muy importantes en la política española sobre aquellas elecciones en las que casi todas las encuestas apuntaban a una mayoría absoluta del PP y Vox que nunca llegó.

La principal novedad es que, mientras las cosas siguen más o menos como estaban en la pelea por el primer puesto entre los dos grandes partidos —están en números similares a los de 2023, muy cerca entre ellos y alrededor del 30%—, por debajo, en la batalla por el tercer puesto, Vox duplica o incluso triplica al Frente Amplio, cuando hace tres años hubo un empate técnico con Sumar.

Además, esta vez, al contrario que en 2023, el PSOE se está comiendo casi todo el voto de Sumar, con un Sánchez más a la izquierda que nunca, que se define como zurdo, levanta el puño izquierdo en los mítines y anuncia medidas que han sido bandera de Sumar, como la prestación universal por crianza.

Sánchez, además, se ha traído a Madrid este lunes a Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, el gran referente de la izquierda mundial, también del mundo del Frente Amplio, con el que siempre tuvo relaciones estrechas el PT, el partido que fundó el mandatario brasileño. Lula ha apoyado sin disimulo al presidente. “Es muy importante, Pedro, que tú ganes las elecciones”, le dice en un vídeo que ambos grabaron fuera de La Moncloa, como parte de un acto organizado por sus partidos. Todos estos movimientos conducen necesariamente a una concentración de voto de la izquierda alrededor del PSOE que detectan las encuestas y que está intentando frenar el Frente Amplio.

Este domingo, la presentación del programa del PSOE, lleno de medidas que compiten con el Frente Amplio, desató definitivamente las hostilidades entre los dos socios de coalición, que han convivido estos años con tensiones, pero tratando de evitar que se desatara la guerra. Si en 2023 ese tándem Sánchez-Yolanda Díaz fue muy eficaz y funcionó, especialmente en el decisivo debate a cuatro en el último jueves de campaña, esta vez parece más difícil y el Frente Amplio ha empezado ya a rebelarse contra el PSOE al comprobar en los sondeos ya en campaña que le está arrebatando buena parte de su espacio.

En los debates sectoriales hasta ahora se ha evitado el choque entre los dos miembros de la coalición, pese a las diferencias, pero si la sangría de votos del Frente Amplio hacia el PSOE sigue este ritmo, es posible que las cosas cambien para cuando llegue el decisivo debate a cuatro la próxima semana, a cuatro días de las elecciones y esta vez con Ada Colau en el lugar de Díaz.

Tanto Pablo Bustinduy como Colau atacaron al PSOE este lunes para mostrar diferencias, pero sobre todo reapareció con ese perfil la propia Yolanda Díaz, que después de la retirada de su candidatura para liderar la Organización Internacional del Trabajo parece dispuesta a volver a la campaña y tratar de reactivar un voto al Frente Amplio que las encuestas dan mucho más bajo de lo esperado.

Mientras distintas fuentes del Frente Amplio consultadas se muestran indignadas porque creen que el PSOE “se ha pasado de frenada” con su intento de captar votantes de la izquierda para garantizarse el objetivo de lograr ser el primer partido y ganarle al PP, los socialistas niegan radicalmente que esta sea su estrategia. “Nosotros no vamos a por ellos. Es igual que en 2023. Sánchez habla bien de Ada Colau en las entrevistas, no va al choque, y el esquema es el mismo. Si la gente está concentrando el voto en el PSOE, será por la debilidad del Frente Amplio, no porque les estemos arrinconando nosotros”, señalan fuentes del cuadro de mandos de la campaña socialista.

La candidata a la presidencia del Gobierno por Frente Amplio, Ada Colau (a la izquierda), junto a la vicepresidenta segunda y ministra de Trabajo y Economía Social, Yolanda Díaz (a la izquierda), protagonizan una charla sobre vivienda dentro de la campaña electoral, este lunes en Madrid. Claudio Álvarez

En el Frente Amplio lo ven de manera muy diferente. “El PSOE ha medido fatal su intento de OPA hostil. Ahora tiene tres consejos de ministros para aprobar la prestación universal por crianza o el registro horario, o se les va a volver en contra como un bumerán. Pensando en matarnos, nos han regalado una batalla preciosa”, señalan desde el corazón de la campaña del Frente Amplio. Esos consejos amenazan con ser tensos porque ahora la rivalidad electoral es ya muy evidente.

La propia Díaz, que habitualmente ha evitado los choques con Sánchez porque creía que era la mejor manera de cuidar la coalición, entró de lleno en esa batalla al regresar a la campaña y recordó que es el Ministerio de Economía, con Carlos Cuerpo al frente, quien ha impedido que Trabajo aprobara ya un real decreto, sin necesidad de convalidación parlamentaria, para implantar el registro horario obligatorio en todas las empresas españolas y así luchar de forma más decidida contra las millones de horas extras no pagadas que hay cada año en España, un fenómeno muy superior al de otros países del entorno europeo. “No doy crédito. Si quieren aprobar el registro horario, el decreto está listo y podemos hacerlo ya”, sentenció Díaz en redes sociales.

La batalla es muy evidente. Díaz se apresuró a anunciar que este martes ella misma llevará al Consejo de Ministros la subida del 5,3% del Salario Mínimo Interprofesional (SMI). En otras ocasiones ha sido Sánchez el que ha anunciado esa subida en mítines del PSOE, pero esta vez la que fuera candidata de Sumar en 2023 se ha adelantado precisamente para intentar que les quede claro a los españoles que esta es una política impulsada por Sumar, que ahora se presenta como Frente Amplio. Sánchez también jugó después en esa carrera, anunciando en Tele5 que este martes se subirá el salario de los funcionarios un 4,5%, una competencia que es del socialista Óscar López.

Díaz comparecerá este martes tras el Consejo de Ministros, probablemente con López, y es presumible que siga ahí esta competición que ya se ha visto en el pasado precisamente con el salario mínimo. El ejemplo más claro fue un choque entre Yolanda Díaz y Pilar Alegría, entonces portavoz del Gobierno, en una rueda de prensa tras el Consejo de Ministros en la que estaba en discusión si el SMI debía pagar o no el IRPF. Finalmente, Díaz acabó ganando esta batalla y el SMI sigue sin tributar.

Mientras, en el bloque de la derecha también hay hostilidades claras entre el PP y Vox por el voto fronterizo, pero con una situación completamente diferente: ahí es el supuestamente pequeño, Vox, el que le está comiendo votos al grande, el PP, y los populares hacen todo tipo de movimientos para intentar frenarlo, especialmente endurecer cada día un poco más sus mensajes antisanchistas y también contra la inmigración.

Además, ahora el PP ha girado también hacia un asunto que fue muy exitoso en la campaña autonómica de 2023, que quedó resumida con el grito “que te vote Txapote”. Feijóo ha cambiado su agenda de campaña para ir a Guipúzcoa a trasladar apoyo a su candidato, Jon Echevarria, después de que un grupo radical impidiera un acto suyo en Hernani. Los dos bloques viven, pues, tensiones internas, pero la clave de las elecciones sigue siendo si hay movimientos entre ellos, y de momento la mayoría de los sondeos señalan que hay bastante estabilidad. La izquierda necesita un movimiento fuerte para romper el pronóstico generalizado de mayoría absoluta de la derecha y ultraderecha.

World.title: La estafa de la tienda en línea falsa
World.content:
Supuestos comercios ‘online’ lanzan ofertas agresivas para atraer a los compradores, especialmente durante el Black Friday y la Navidad, pero detrás de cada ganga se esconde un engaño

Los ciberdelincuentes crean negocios ficticios en internet desde los que lanzan ofertas para engañar a los consumidores y conseguir su dinero o sus datos personales y bancarios. El éxito de esta estafa reside en que ofertan artículos muy demandados, como dispositivos electrónicos o productos con cualidades casi milagrosas a precios muy bajos. Una vez realizada la compra, el consumidor nunca recibe el producto o le llega uno distinto o de escaso valor. Y sin posibilidad de reclamación alguna, porque los datos de contacto también son falsos.

El Instituto Nacional de Ciberseguridad (INCIBE) colaboró en el cierre de 4.600 sitios web en España (.es), en 2025, la mayoría relacionados con comercios ficticios. Meta, la empresa matriz de Facebook e Instagram, retiró 159 millones de anuncios fraudulentos, muchos de ellos ofertando productos engañosos, el año pasado.

TÉCNICAS DE MANIPULACIÓN

Urgencia Los ciberdelincuentes crean la sensación de que, si no se compra ya, se perderá la oportunidad de adquirir un producto con una gran rebaja Familiaridad Suplantan a marcas populares, como grandes multinacionales de la moda, la electrónica, además de supermercados Escasez y oportunidad Simulan que la página solo dispone de un número limitado de existencias para generar una sensación de pérdida de oportunidad si no se compra Prueba social Convencen al comprador de que todo el mundo está comprando con falsos reclamos

Ciberexperto Nombre Jordi Sánchez Cargo Experto en fraude de CaixaBank “Antes de comprar una ganga, conviene parar un instante y cerciorarse de que la página es legítima. Lo lograremos comprobando la url y buscando información en internet” 0:00 CÓMO RECONOCER UNA TIENDA FRAUDULENTA 1 Desconfiar de precios muy bajos. Si un artículo se oferta a un precio muy alejado del habitual posiblemente sea una estafa 2 Comprobar las valoraciones y las opiniones. Ayudan a hacerse una idea sobre la fiabilidad del negocio. Desconfiar si todos los comentarios son muy recientes. Hacer una búsqueda si se tienen dudas 3 Acceder escribiendo la dirección web en el navegador. Evitar entrar en los comercios en línea a través de enlaces recibidos por correo electrónico, SMS o redes sociales 4 Desconfiar de comercios que ofrecen métodos de pago poco habituales o muy limitados. Los comercios legítimos suelen ofreces las opciones de pago más populares 5 No dejarse presionar por ofertas por tiempo limitado. Los ciberdelincuentes apremian a la víctima para que se decida a comprar sin reflexionar

No todas las tiendas falsas funcionan igual. Las más comunes son las tiendas que anuncian productos que no existen; también existen tiendas de falsificaciones, que envían un producto de peor calidad que el comprado. Jordi Sánchez, experto en fraude de CaixaBank, señala que este fraude también se extiende a páginas de alquileres vacacionales, donde no solo se intenta robar el dinero de la víctima sino sus datos personales. “Los delincuentes piden la numeración de la tarjeta, pagos mediante Bizum, una copia del DNI...”, explica.

En caso de tener indicios de que se ha comprado en una tienda falsa. Se debe contactar con el banco. Si se han facilitado datos de la tarjeta, habrá que contactar con el banco para que se tomen las medidas pertinentes. Conviene guardar todas las pruebas y acudir a la Policía Nacional o a la Guardia Civil.

Estafas en las plataformas de venta legítimas. No solo las tiendas pueden ser falsas, con frecuencia, los ciberdelincuentes lanzan sus estafas a través de plataformas de compraventa legítimas. Se aprovechan de que el consumidor confía en ellas y buscan maneras de sortear las medidas de seguridad que establecen para proteger a los usuarios. Se pueden dar dos casos: que el vendedor publica un anuncio de un artículo que no posee o de un artículo que se anuncia como original y es una falsificación. El falso vendedor suele pedir al comprador que se cierre la operación fuera de la plataforma, a través de un programa de mensajería instantánea y que se haga el pago mediante canales alternativos a los ofrecidos por la plataforma, de manera que evita los mecanismos de protección que ofrece la plataforma para pagar.

OTROS CASOS DE TIENDAS FRAUDULENTAS

World.title: Mi hija comparte un piso con tres estudiantes en Madrid por el que pagan 2.254 euros, un 15% más que el año pasado. ¿Es legal la subida?
World.content:
Los lectores envían sus preguntas al consultorio de vivienda de EL PAÍS en colaboración con Legálitas

Pregunta. Mi hija está estudiando en la Comunidad de Madrid y vive de alquiler en un piso de cuatro habitaciones con otras tres compañeras. Pagan 2.254 euros al mes sin incluir gastos. El propietario las obliga a pagar 11 meses, aunque sólo estén 10 meses y no las deja hacer contrato anual. Este curso las ha subido el 15% para poder renovar (el año pasado pagaban 1.960 euros). ¿Es legal tanta subida?, ¿hay alguna ley que proteja de este abuso? ¿El nuevo decreto aprobado las beneficia en algo? S. Viñas

Respuesta. Para determinar si el incremento del 15% de la renta es legal, debemos analizar, en primer lugar, la naturaleza del contrato suscrito, distinguiendo entre un arrendamiento de vivienda habitual y un arrendamiento de temporada por motivos de estudios.

La nueva regulación de los arrendamientos temporales, introducida por el Real Decreto-ley 29/2026, establece en su artículo 9 bis de la Ley de Arrendamientos Urbanos que estos contratos deben responder a una causa de temporalidad debidamente justificada, como puede ser la realización de estudios universitarios, y que su duración será la libremente pactada por las partes, generalmente sin exceder de 12 meses.

Por tanto, no resulta necesariamente ilegal que el propietario exija la formalización de un contrato de 11 meses, aunque las estudiantes únicamente tengan previsto ocupar la vivienda durante 10 meses, siempre que dicha duración haya sido libremente acordada entre las partes.

En cuanto al incremento de la renta, que pasa de 1.960 a 2.254 euros, lo que supone una subida del 15%, la nueva normativa establece límites a los incrementos de renta entre contratos temporales sucesivos sobre una misma vivienda, que no podrán superar el porcentaje fijado por el IRAV. No obstante, esta limitación no resulta automáticamente aplicable a su caso, sino que será necesario comprobar si concurren los requisitos legales relativos a la sucesión de contratos. En este caso, parece que los contratos no se formalizan de manera sucesiva.

Asimismo, el artículo 9 bis establece que, cuando se celebren más de dos contratos temporales consecutivos entre las mismas partes y sobre una misma vivienda, o se supere injustificadamente el límite de duración de 12 meses, el arrendamiento quedará sometido al régimen jurídico de los arrendamientos de vivienda habitual, con las garantías y derechos que reconoce la Ley de Arrendamientos Urbanos para esta modalidad.

Si tiene dudas, sugerencias o simplemente quiere contarnos su caso, puede enviarnos un email a vivienda@elpais.es .

World.title: Registrations to vote in Senate elections doubles since 2023
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

More than 80,000 Dutch citizens living abroad have registered to vote in next year’s provincial elections, more than double the number that signed up in 2023.

The electoral commission set up a special electoral college for non-resident citizens four years ago following a campaign by the lobby group Stichting Nederlanders Buiten Nederland (SNBN).

People living on the Caribbean islands of Bonaire, Sint-Eustatius and Saba were also given a vote for the first time.

Foreign residents do not choose representatives for a provincial assembly, but their vote counts towards the make-up of the Senate, which is indirectly elected by the 12 provinces in June.

So far 82,500 people have registered to vote in the 2027 election, which takes place on March 17, according to the city council in The Hague, which is responsible for the electoral college.

Dutch citizens can register until February 3 through the council’s website.

Four years ago 37,173 foreign citizens signed up. GroenLinks won the largest share of the overseas vote with 18.5%, while D66 took 16.3%.

The Labour party (PvdA), which has since merged with GroenLinks to form Progressief Nederland, took 8.4%, giving the left-wing combined list more than a quarter of the vote.

Not all parties in parliament contested the vote: the far-right PVV, farmers’ party BBB, the ChristenUnie and Denk were all absent from the ballot paper in 2023.

The BBB became the largest party in the provinces and Senate, taking 19.2% of the overall vote.

World.title: Jetten cabinet survives crisis as coalition agrees to carry on
World.content:
Rob Jetten’s minority cabinet will stay in office after four days of crisis talks. The three coalition parties have agreed to patch up the row over the 2027 tax plan and keep going.

The centrist D66, right-wing liberal VVD and Christian Democrat CDA said on Monday night that “intensive talks” had brought about a “restoration of trust”, public broadcaster NOS reported. No other party will be brought into the coalition.

The government information service RVD announced the deal at around 10pm, after more than nine hours of talks at the Catshuis, the prime minister’s official residence in The Hague.

Debate demanded

Opposition leaders were quick to react to the news. PRO leader Jesse Klaver said it was “totally irresponsible” for the VVD to vote against its own cabinet’s tax plan. “The big question for the whole country is: do we still have a cabinet?” he said. He wants a debate in parliament.

The local authorities’ association VNG, backed by the logistics lobby Evofenedex and the property developers’ association Neprom, had already urged the cabinet to sort out its differences and serve its full term.

Ministers are holding an extra cabinet meeting on Tuesday morning to hear what exactly was agreed. Jetten and his deputy prime ministers, Dilan Yesilgöz (VVD) and Bart van den Brink (CDA), are expected to explain the deal afterwards. MPs are likely to debate the situation on Wednesday, after Klaver’s request.

The three parties have also brought in Sybrand Buma, vice-president of the Council of State and a former CDA leader, to help them reach working agreements with opposition parties on the budget. Buma will mainly advise and won’t be making deals himself, NOS reported, quoting sources in The Hague.

Tax deal row

The row broke out when D66 and the CDA made a deal with left-wing PRO and pan-European party Volt. The deal raises wealth tax by €1 billion and uses the money to cut income tax.

The VVD said the deal broke the coalition agreement. On Thursday its MPs voted against the whole tax plan, which scraped through with the smallest possible majority, 76 of 150 seats.

The next day Yesilgöz called the minority cabinet a “failed experiment” that needed a “fundamental reset”. Jetten said the parties had to have “fundamental talks” to make improvements on a substantive, political and personal level.

The leaders spent the weekend at the De Zwaluwenberg estate in Hilversum, then moved to the Catshuis on Monday. According to NOS, they discussed breaking up the coalition or carrying on without the VVD, but both options were later dropped.

The coalition has just 66 of the 150 seats in parliament, so it needs opposition votes in both houses to pass legislation. The senate is due to vote on the tax plan in the week before Christmas.

World.title: Dutch progress in Nations League despite 5-0 drubbing in Germany
World.content:
The Netherlands came crashing down to earth after hammering Greece as they were outclassed and outmuscled by Germany in Berlin.

Oranje went into the final match of the Nations League group stage with high hopes of recording their first win over their old rivals in seven matches stretching back to 2019.

Instead they suffered their second worst defeat ever at the hands of Germany, but still progressed to the knockout stages thanks to their thumping 7-0 win in Amsterdam on Friday.

Coach Xavi Hernandez was forced to make one change in midfield as Jurriën Timber replaced Barcelona’s Frenkie de Jong, who pulled out with an obturator muscle strain.

Germany shaded the first half and went ahead five minutes before the break when Freiburg striker Derry Scherhant cut in from the left hand side and beat Bart Verbruggen with a curling strike into the top corner.

Scherhant had struck the post minutes earlier, while the Dutch might have taken the lead earlier when Crysencio Summerville slipped in the penalty area as he tried to control a cross by Cody Gakpo.

But in the second half the Dutch fell apart. In the 60th minute Florian Wirtz shoved Denzel Dumfries off the ball and had space to tee up a left-footed shot from the edge of the area that gave Verbruggen no chance.

Nico Schlotterbeck added a third from a free-kick five minutes later, before Wirtz drifted past Gakpo on the right side of the penalty area to score his second.

The humiliation was complete when Brajan Gruda capped a fine attacking performance by firing in a rebound.

Dumfries made no excuses afterwards for what he admitted was a “terrible performance”. “We gave the ball away too easily, left too much space and were too weak in the challenges,” he told NOS. “We can’t let that happen.”

World.title: Outcry over “cruel” plan to send failed asylum seekers to Rwanda
World.content:
Some 46 human rights, civil society and trade union organisations have signed a letter objecting to the “cruel” plan presented by the Netherlands and four other EU member states on Monday to begin sending asylum seekers whose applications have been rejected to Rwanda.

The plan, presented in Vienna on Monday, will pave the way for people to be sent to “deportation hubs” in Rwanda, on the idea that it will help secure national borders and break apart human trafficking networks. The reality, the signatories say, is that this is just a euphemism for forced deportation and will deteriorate security.

Dutch foreign affairs minister Tom Berendsen joined counterparts from Austria, Denmark, Germany and Greece at the conference. The letter of objection notes that the vulnerable people will be sent to a place that they have never been to, have no connection to, and which has a serious ongoing record of human rights violations.

“It signals that member states accept the risk of serious human rights violations against one of the most marginalised groups in society, in return for a deterrence goal that evidence clearly suggests they will not reach. Such cruel measures drive people into further insecurity, and risk making migration routes more dangerous,” the letter states.

Berendsen said at the press conference after the event that “effective return is important” and that through the deal the Netherlands is “taking a concrete step towards a better migration system by establishing a return hub in Rwanda.”

He also spoke of the need for economic development in Rwanda, though how the deal will work is unclear. According to broadcaster NOS, Rwanda wants economic support in return, and the five countries will share the costs, which have not been made public. Rwanda will initially offer around 100 places, and only single men will be sent at first.

A spokesperson from asylum foundation Stichting Vluchteling told Dutch News: “We are against this concept as a humanitarian organisation. Member states are responsible for these people. We’re very concerned about the situation in Rwanda. We see human rights abuses on press freedom. We don’t believe there will be the possibility for independent monitoring from member states.”

The spokesperson said the talk of improving human rights through this agreement was nothing but “pretty words”.

They said that the move sends a signal that Europe does not want to accept its responsibility for asylum seekers. “This is super dangerous. Even if one person is sent over the next couple of years, it sends a signal that we don’t want you here and that we’re willing to go quite far to remove you.”

There is a critical shortage of asylum beds in the Netherlands, with many taken by people whose applications have been rejected but are stuck in legal limbo. But the spokesperson said “this is not a numbers crisis, it’s a political crisis. The focus should be on obligations that member states have, which is that we’re responsible for people who are rejected.”

The letter also warns that the EU’s proposed new rules for border agency Frontex would allow it to support returns to non-EU countries, including a possible role in running “return hubs”. Frontex already operates with “a de facto lack of accountability”, the organisations say, and the proposal would remove the obligation to assign at least one fundamental rights monitor to each operation.

The Dutch foreign ministry’s own country report on Rwanda, which the immigration service IND uses to assess asylum claims, records extrajudicial killings, enforced disappearances and torture in unofficial detention centres.

The letter also warned that “by relying on third countries to take on its protection obligations, the EU makes itself dependent on non-EU states, enabling third countries to leverage migration in line with their own political agenda.”

World.title: King raises history of slavery at ceremony to mark First Salute
World.content:
King Willem-Alexander has acknowledged the role of the Dutch Caribbean islands in the transatlantic slave trade during a ceremony to mark the 250th anniversary of the Netherlands’ recognition of the United States.

The king was speaking on Statia Day, a national holiday on the island of Sint Eustatius to mark the First Salute, when a Dutch cannon was fired from Fort Orange to return a salute from the American ship Andrew Doria.

The event on November 16, 1776, is seen as the first formal recognition of the USA by a foreign power after the Declaration of Independence in July that year.

At the time the island was a Dutch colony with around 70 slave plantations. Today it is a special municipality of the Netherlands with a population of around 3,300.

During his speech on Monday, the king referred to the recently published study into the royal family’s role in slavery, which concluded that the house of Oranje-Nassau earned more than €500 million from the colonies since the 17th century.

Prime minister Rob Jetten had also been due to attend the ceremony, but he was forced to stay in the Netherlands for crisis talks with his coalition partners after last week’s budget vote brought his cabinet to the brink of collapse.

Common history

“The First Salute is a milestone in history, but our common history goes far wider,” the king said. “There is also the story of Statia as a place to commemorate slavery.

“In the 17th and 18th centuries several thousand people from west Africa landed here. After an inhumane journey of two months, packed into the bowels of ships with no more than two square metres per person, there was no salute for them on their arrival.”

He said that he had been moved by the results of four years of research into slavery, led by Leiden university professor of colonial history, Geert Oostindië, which he commissioned and paid for.

“I know that life on this isolated island is not easy for many people,” he said. “Groceries are expensive, there are few jobs to be had and healthcare is limited.” He added he would continue to work for “fair opportunities and a good life for everyone.”

World.title: More than 14,000 bogus police officers recorded this year so far
World.content:
The number of cases of people being approached by bogus police officers is continuing to rise despite efforts to warn elderly residents to watch out for doorstep conmen.

In 2023 police received just over 500 reports of people being tricked by criminals posing as officers who tried to persuade them to hand over cash and valuables, but in the last three years the number has exploded.

Police suspect that organised gangs are behind the trend, which saw the number rise to 13,000 last year and 14,176 in the first 10 months of 2026. Nearly 3,300 official crime reports have been filed of theft by bogus police officers, suggesting around a quarter of attempts are successful. The oldest victim was 103.

Criminals typically appear on the victim’s doorstep and tell them that thieves are operating in the area. They then offer to take in cash and other valuable items such as jewellery for safekeeping.

Some offenders dress in clothes resembling police uniforms, while others wear casual clothing and tell their victims they are working with CID.

Police said genuine officers will never offer to take away items from householders and anyone with doubts about an officer on the doorstep should call 112 to find out if police are making enquiries in their neighbourhood.

Information campaign

Last year police and Omroep MAX, which broadcasts daytime TV programmes on NPO, ran an information campaign highlighting the doorstep techniques used by bogus officers.

“We do a lot of work to prevent and detect these offences,” said Sybren van der Velden Walda, national co-ordinator for high impact crime. “But it’s evidently so lucrative that criminals keep posing as police officers to rob people.”

So far this year 783 people have been arrested on suspicion of pretending to be police officers, one of whom was a 13-year-old boy who stole a bank card and €20,000 worth of jewellery. Police say it is likely he was working for gangsters.

“We see it is a vulnerable group who are recruited by organised criminals to do things like this,” said Van der Velden Walda.

He added that the prevalence of bogus officers was making it harder for his colleagues to carry out genuine police work.

“Elderly people won’t open the door any more because they don’t trust police at the door,” he said.

World.title: Preventative health made accessible for internationals
World.content:
For many new internationals, going to a Dutch doctor, or huisarts, takes a bit of time getting used to. With a more hands-off approach to healthcare than in many other countries, you often don’t get to your huisarts until you have symptoms you want checked.

But what if you want to understand your health before symptoms appear? Knowing what to check, and which lifestyle changes could make a difference, isn’t always straightforward.

Enter Blue Health Intelligence, a health-tech startup that offers a 360-health check, providing insight into cardiovascular health, metabolism and liver and kidney functions within an hour, sharing results immediately in a consultation with a doctor.

“In countries such as Japan, Germany and the UK, periodic health checks are already embedded in the healthcare system, but that is not yet the case in the Netherlands,” says Onno Huyghe, CEO and co-founder of Blue Health Intelligence. “By gaining earlier insight into their health, people can stay healthy for longer and health issues can be prevented. We aim to make prevention more accessible to many people.”

According to the World Health Organization (WHO), approximately 1.8 million deaths from noncommunicable diseases are avoidable each year in Europe. About 60% are linked to changeable risk factors – such as tobacco and alcohol use, high blood pressure, unhealthy diets, obesity and physical inactivity – while the remaining 40% could be prevented or delayed through timely diagnosis and high-quality health care.

For €299, you get a 360-degree health check that uses hundreds of data points, the results of which are discussed immediately on-site with a doctor and uploaded to the Blue app. The 10 tests administered include an ECG, 3D body scan, blood analysis and an ultrasound.

“You don’t always realise how much your health risks increase as you get older,” says customer Petra. “For me, the health check at Blue Health was a real eye-opener. Under professional guidance, you’re efficiently taken through all the tests in a short time.”

If something is discovered, Blue Health Intelligence offers a free follow-up before passing that information on to your huisarts.

As common as an annual dental check-up

“Our participants gain a comprehensive understanding of their health and potential health risks,” says Leanne Verdonck, physician and co-founder of Blue Health Intelligence. “Our goal is for a regular health check to become just as common as going to the dentist.”

At its modern, state-of-the-art facility on Amsterdam’s Prinsengracht, Blue Health Intelligence has made preventative healthcare affordable. It follows the growing trend in the health and wellness sector of getting insight into people’s potential health risks, advising them on healthy lifestyle changes in a personalized plan that is then shared in the app.

Having recently secured €3.4 million in funding, Blue Health Intelligence plans to expand its capacity in Amsterdam and even internationally, including in Paris and Milan, while continuing to develop its preventative health platform.

More than 2,500 people have already booked a health check with Blue Health Intelligence. Due to high demand, bookings are now offered through a waitlist. If you choose to join, Blue will contact you when it’s your turn to book, with appointments a few days away.

Click on the link if you want to join.

World.title: Dutch influencer still held by ICE with no reason given, family
World.content:
Dutch influencer and OnlyFans model Vera Dijkmans, who was arrested five days ago by US ICE agents, remains in custody without any reason given for her detention, according to her family, who also say she is being held in dire conditions.

Dijkmans has millions of social media followers and often does promotional work with UFC fighters. She was arrested at Newark airport where she’d travelled to from Miami for an event.

Her details don’t show up on the ICE database and no details have been made public as to why she was detained. Her mother, who has travelled there to protest for her release, said “we fear for her life”, adding that “she is in a room with twelve other women, receives little food and drink, and there is barely any fresh air. The conditions are inhumane,” AD reported.

Dijkmans is staying in the US on a B2 visa that allows you to be in the country without working for up to six months. She had applied for a permanent residency there and may have missed an appointment for that application procedure, her mother speculated to AD.

The US government warned people this year that using social media for commercial purposes was not allowed on a tourist visa.

ICE, which was expanded by the Trump administration to round up and deport people from the country who do not have the correct paperwork, often targets people who have failed to comply with visa rules.

Delaney Hall, the immigration detention centre in Newark where Dijkmans is being held, is run by private prison company GEO Group, which was awarded a 15-year, $1 billion contract by ICE in 2025 to detain up to 1,000 people there. It is notorious for its harsh conditions.

The Dutch foreign affairs ministry told AD it is aware of Dijkmans’ situation and is providing consular assistance, though it did not say what that entails.

World.title: Kraków church holds mass for perpetrator of deadly attack just metres from where he shot victims
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The historic St Mary’s Basilica in Kraków has hosted a holy mass for Michał Oksiński, the man who carried out the recent attack in the city and later died of injuries sustained in a shootout with police. The six people who died in the attack and more than a dozen who were injured were shot by Oskiński on the square where the church stands, some of them just a few metres from its doors. St Mary’s Basilica says that the mass is “an expression of the Christian faith in God’s mercy” and “in no way indicates justification for the crime”. On the afternoon of 7 November, Oksiński launched his attack on Kraków’s famous market square, which was packed with locals and tourists. He shot at random from his car while driving through the square and surrounding streets before police managed to bring his rampage to an end. Later that same day, the dead bodies of Oksiński’s parents and sister were found in his home. They had each been shot in the head while sleeping. Two days after the attack, Oskiński himself died in hospital. On Sunday, Łukasz Wantuch, a former city councillor, shared a photograph of an announcement that there would be “a holy mass for the late Michał Oksiński and the deceased members of his family” at the Roman Catholic St Mary’s Basilica on Monday morning. The church, built in the 14th century, is one of the most famous in Poland and dominates the skyline in Kraków’s historic, UNESCO-listed city centre. It stands on one corner of the market square, just a few steps from where some of Oksiński’s victims were shot. “I won’t hide the fact that I find this somewhat shocking,” wrote Wantuch. He noted that the announcement referred to the “blessed memory” (świętej pamięci) of Oksiński. However, that phrase is standard usage in Polish to refer to someone who has died (the equivalent ot the English “late”). “But perhaps that is what faith is about: praying even for a murderer,” added Wantuch. Among the more than 1,000 comments under his Facebook post, many agreed with that sentiment. “The whole of Christianity is based on forgiving the unforgivable,” wrote one. “I don’t think anyone needs God’s mercy more [than Oksiński],” said another. However, some others were critical of the fact that the mass was being held in that particular church among the dozens in Kraków. “It is the height of impudence that they’ll celebrate mass for him in the very church he murdered in front of,” wrote one commenter. Later on Sunday, St Mary’s Basilica issued a statement, signed by parish administrator Father Mariusz Słonina, saying that the holy mass “is a private initiative of one of the priests, not of St Mary’s Parish”. However, Słonina added that “praying for the deceased is an expression of the Christian faith in God’s mercy” and “in no way indicates justification for the crime, a lessening of the perpetrator’s responsibility, or a trivialisation of the suffering of the victims”. Local news service KR24 reported that uniformed police officers were posted outside the church for today’s mass while plainclothes officers were inside, with one of them right next to the altar. Three priests were present, including Słonina, who presided over the mass. Only around a dozen faithful were in attendance, with KR24 suggesting that many did not even seem aware for whom mass was being held. Separate private funeral ceremonies will take place for Oksiński, his parents and sister, who lived in the town of Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, about 160 km from Krakow. On Sunday, their family issued a statement asking the media to “respect the privacy, dignity and mourning of our family and loved ones”. Meanwhile, police and prosecutors continue to investigate the possible motive behind Oksiński’s attack, which they are treating as a terrorist offence. Last week, the justice minister said that there were “very strong traces of right-wing extremism” in the perpetrator’s online activity. Two police officers, Jakub Kulik and Artur Morański, who were seriously injured in the shootout that debilitated Okisński, have been recovering in hospital after undergoing emergency surgery. World.title: Poland detains neo-Nazi teens accused of terrorist plot
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Poland has detained and charged three teenagers who are allegedly linked to “an international neo-Nazi network” and had been planning terrorist attacks, including with the use of homemade explosives. The arrests were announced on Monday morning by Tomasz Siemoniak, the minister in charge of the security services, who revealed that the suspects are Polish citizens. Two are aged 17 and one is 16. “The teenagers not only promoted Nazi and fascist ideology but had also already taken steps toward committing terrorist offences,” wrote Siemoniak. Funkcjonariusze @ABW_GOV_PL zatrzymali 3 obywateli RP, 16-latka i dwóch 17-latków, związanych z międzynarodowym środowiskiem neonazistowskim. ▶️ Nastolatkowie nie tylko propagowali ideologię nazistowską i faszystowską, ale podejmowali już działania zmierzające do popełniania… — Tomasz Siemoniak (@TomaszSiemoniak) November 16, 2026 The National Prosecutor’s Office revealed that the trio were “fascinated by the activities of an international neo-Nazi terrorist organisation…[that] has an ideology based on hatred against people of Jewish descent, immigrants, black people, the LGBT community, politicians and state security officials”. Though prosecutors did not name the organisation, they said that members of it have been involved in planning terrorist attacks in the United States, Germany and the United Kingdom. In some countries, including the UK, Canada and Australia, it has been outlawed and designated a terrorist group. Poland’s Internal Security Agency (ABW) had found that the three suspects’ online communication indicated “an interest in constructing explosive devices, modifying weapons and using such items to carry out terrorist activities”. During a search of the home of one of the 17-year-olds (named only as “suspect 1”), officers found chemicals that are precursors for the production of explosives. That suspect has also been charged with possession of a so-called pipe bomb, which prosecutors say he wanted to “transfer to a neo-Nazi terrorist group”. Suspect 1 was found to have discussed with the other 17-year-old, named as suspect 2, how to construct an explosive device and detonate it in a specific residential building where someone they knew lived. Suspect 1 had also “incited extremist behaviour and hate-motivated violence” in his online activity, while the 16-year-old, named as suspect 3, had “promoted fascist content” (a crime in Poland) and encouraged someone to assault another person based on their race. Each suspect has been charged with three crimes, relating variously to terrorist offences, possession or attempted production of explosives and weapons, promoting Nazism, fascism and racial hatred, and inciting others to commit violence based on racial differences. Prosecutors note that Polish law generally allows people to face full criminal liability from the age of 17. The two 17-year-olds have therefore been placed in adult pretrial detention, while the 16-year-old is being held in a juvenile facility. Śledztwo w sprawie neonazistów i planowanych aktów terroru kryminalnego Szczegóły w komunikacie: ⬇️https://t.co/dQpdgiTYJD — Prokuratura Regionalna w Gdańsku (@Prok_Regio_GDA) November 16, 2026 The arrests come in the context of recent concerns over radicalisation of young people in Poland. Earlier this month, a 24-year-old carried out a terrorist attack in the city of Kraków, killing six people by firing a rifle from his car. He had earlier killed his parents and sister in their home. In the aftermath of the attack, justice minister Waldemar Żurek revealed that investigators had found “very strong traces of right-wing extremism” in the attacker’s online activity, though he emphasised that the motive was yet to be determined. In the space of a few days last month, three knife attacks took place in Polish schools, resulting in one case in the death of a member of staff. Dozens of young people were arrested in the aftermath for making threats and/or possessing weapons. In September, the security services detained three teenagers accused of being part of online groups promoting neo-Nazism and violence. One of them has been charged with planning terrorist attacks on targets including a mosque and a school. World.title: Ukraine blames Russia for graffiti glorifying WWII Ukrainian nationalists on Polish monuments
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Around a dozen public monuments in Poland, including one dedicated to the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising, have been defaced with graffiti glorifying the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA), a World War Two nationalist partisan group that was responsible for the massacre of Poles and Jews. Ukraine’s embassy in Warsaw has condemned the vandalism and blamed it on Russia, which has previously been accused by the Polish authorities of orchestrating provocative graffiti on monuments. W sobotę, 14 listopada, w Warszawie doszło do kolejnych dwóch dewastacji pomników. Napisy „Slava UPA” pojawiły się na Pomniku Bohaterów Getta przed Muzeum Historii Żydów Polskich POLIN oraz na Pomniku Żołnierzy 1 Armii Wojska Polskiego przy ulicy Andersa 13. To kolejna odsłona… pic.twitter.com/Y7NDsfpjxn — Miejski Reporter (@MiejskiReporter) November 14, 2026 The latest spate of vandalism was first reported in early November in the western city of Poznań, where three World War two memorials were painted with graffiti saying “Glory to the UPA” (Slawa UPA). While the UPA is remembered by many in Ukraine for fighting for independence from Moscow-imposed Soviet rule, in Poland it is primarily associated with leading the Volhynia massacres, in which around 100,000 Polish civilians, mostly women and children, were slaughtered as part of an ethnic cleansing operation. Local police in Poznań told the Gazeta Wyborcza daily that they were searching for a young man dressed in black who is believed to be the culprit, but have so far not been able to identify him. Similar graffiti was subsequently reported on seven monuments, including ones dedicated to Polish World War Two heroes and anti-communist protests that took place in 1970, in Gdańsk and Gdynia, neighbouring cities on Poland’s northern Baltic coast. On Friday, local police in Gdańsk confirmed that they had detained a 17-year-old Ukrainian on suspicion of “painting offensive slogans propagating hatred”. They shared blurred-out images of the suspect as well as cans of spray paint. He has been charged with promoting fascist ideology, incitement to violence and hatred based on nationality, and desecration of monuments. If convicted, he could face up to three years in prison. Previously, on Tuesday this week, MOST, a Polish-based Belarusian independent media outlet, published findings that an anonymous person on messaging service Telegram, which is popular among Russians, Ukrainians and Belarusians, had been offering $500 plus travel expenses for a job in Poznań. When an undercover MOST journalist responded to the advert, he was told that the job would involve spray painting “Glory to the UPA” on monuments. The recruiter confirmed that the job was illegal, “but if you cover your face and do everything quickly, they won’t find you”. They also revealed that similar jobs were available in other Polish cities, including Warsaw, Wrocław and Lublin. Subsequently, similar inscriptions appeared in Warsaw on the Monument to the Ghetto Heroes, which honours the Jews who rose up against their German-Nazi oppressors in 1943; a monument commemorating the Polish First Army, which fought in World War Two; and a monument to sappers who served in the war. The vandalism was condemned by Poland’s Jewish Historical Institute (ŻIH), which called it a “disgraceful attack on the memory of the victims of the Holocaust and the heroes of Jewish resistance”. Noting MOST’s findings and the vandalism of other monuments, ŻIH said that “this points to the possibility of an organised provocation intended to incite hatred and divide society”. Warsaw police told PAP that they are investigating and seeking to identify the perpetrator. An unnamed police source also told Gazeta Wyborcza they see the incidents in all four cities as related to one another, pointing to the similar style of the inscriptions. On Sunday afternoon, Warsaw’s mayor, Rafał Trzaskowski, condemned the vandalism and shared images of the municipal authorities cleaning the graffiti off the Ghetto Heroes Monument. “Given the scale of similar incidents in other cities, we must consider the possibility that this is a planned provocation,” added the mayor. “Let us not let ourselves be divided – the authorities are working to identify both those who carried out these acts and those who ordered them.” Nie ma zgody na wandalizm w Warszawie. Minionej nocy służby miejskie wyczyściły pomniki oszpecone przez wandali – między innymi Pomnik Bohaterów Getta. Sprawców szuka policja. Patrząc na skalę podobnych incydentów w innych miastach, musimy brać pod uwagę, że mamy do czynienia… pic.twitter.com/5xMgPhnHf8 — Rafał Trzaskowski (@trzaskowski_) November 15, 2026 A day earlier, on Saturday, the Ukrainian embassy had also condemned the acts of vandalism, calling them a “disgraceful provocation”. “In our view, these unlawful acts are a manifestation of the hybrid war that Russia is attempting to wage by any means in European states, and in Poland in particular,” wrote the embassy. “The objective is clear: to incite hostility between Poles and Ukrainians, undermine mutual trust, and weaken support for Ukraine.” Writing in both Polish and Ukrainian, the embassy appealed to Ukrainians “not to be tempted by offers of ‘easy money’ in exchange for painting graffiti, damaging property, or carrying out other illegal tasks” and to report any such offers to the Polish police. “Let us respect the laws of the country in which we reside, as well as historical memory and each other’s dignity,” they added. “Polish-Ukrainian solidarity is our shared strength. Let us not allow the enemy to destroy it.” Poland has been a primary target for Russia’s so-called hybrid actions in Europe, which have included acts of sabotage, espionage, disinformation and efforts to stir hostility towards Ukrainians. Such operations are rarely carried out by Russian operatives themselves. Instead, Russia often recruits people already on the ground, often members of Poland’s large Ukrainian and Belarusian migrant communities, as well as Poles themselves in some cases. In July this year, a Ukrainian teenager was indicted by Polish prosecutors on charges of painting dozens of pro-UPA slogans in public places, including on a monument to victims of the Volhynia massacres. An 18-year-old Ukrainian will stand trial in Poland accused of working on behalf of Russia to stir tension between Poland and Ukraine by painting dozens of inscriptions in public places glorifying the Ukrainian Insurgent Army, which massacred Poles in WWII https://t.co/0w0gVYiGpp — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 16, 2026 There have long been tensions between Poland and Ukraine over the massacres, which Poland recognises as a genocide. Ukraine rejects that label, and also continues to honour the UPA for its role in fighting for independence. The issue has recently flared up again this year after President Volodymyr Zelensky named a Ukrainian military unit after the “heroes of the UPA”. That sparked widespread anger in Poland and prompted Polish President Karol Nawrocki to strip Zelensky of his country’s highest honour. World.title: Polish president vetoes law on removing harmful online content, warning of “censorship”
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. President Karol Nawrocki has vetoed a government bill creating new powers to block harmful online content. Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition, argued that the measures were too far-reaching and could be abused to introduce “censorship”. Government figures have strongly criticised the president’s decision, arguing that it will leave young people in particular more exposed to dangerous content. It also means that Poland still has not fully implemented the European Union’s Digital Services Act (DSA). ❌ Nie dla cenzury Internetu! pic.twitter.com/WusnK7LImD — Kancelaria Prezydenta RP (@prezydentpl) November 13, 2026 Previously, in January this year, Nawrocki had vetoed an earlier bill intended to implement the DSA, describing the measures as “Owellian”. That prompted the government to split the legislation in two. In September, Nawrocki agreed to sign one of those bills, which appointed the president of the Office of Electronic Communications (UKE) as Poland’s digital services coordinator, responsible for overseeing enforcement of the DSA. A second bill was then needed to introduce the actual powers to block harmful online content. In October, it was approved in parliament by the ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right. The right-wing and far-right opposition either voted against it or abstained. Among the new powers included in the legislation were authorisation for the heads of UKE and the National Broadcasting Council (KRRiT) to order the blocking of online content containing violence or threats based on race, nationality, ethnicity, religion or political affiliation. It also allowed the immediate blocking, at the request of a prosecutor or the police, of content involving the acceptance of a contract to commit murder or inciting or assisting in suicide or self-harm. “Perpetrators of serious crimes should not be allowed to use the internet to spread violence and threats,” said digital affairs minister Krzysztof Gawkowski. “The state must have effective tools to quickly respond to such threats. The safety of internet users must transcend political divisions.” The government also argued that last month’s series of stabbings in schools and this month’s deadly terrorist attack in Kraków – which have raised concern about the online radicalisation of young people – have emphasised the importance of tough controls over digital content. There are "strong traces of right-wing extremism" in the activity of the man who carried out the mass shooting in Kraków, says Poland's justice minister. His search history included websites relating to Anders Breivik, the Norwegian far-right terrorist https://t.co/UhVbkWSaCq — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 10, 2026 However, on Friday, the final day by which the president had to make a decision on the bill, Nawrocki announced that he was vetoing it. He argued that “the government has clearly mixed up European obligations with its own political interests”. The measures in the bill threaten to create a “censorship official” and “essentially give the government arbitrary control and the ability to decide what we can and cannot say, write or publish, said the president. Decisions on whether content is permitted or not should be “the exclusive competence of the justice system and independent judges”, he argued. Nawrocki also said that the powers in the vetoed bill were “disproportionate”, allowing an entire domain to be blocked due to a single example of illegal content. “The security of citizens cannot be a pretext for weakening their freedoms,” said Nawrocki. “We must not create a false choice: either the security or the freedom of its citizens. A responsible state must ensure and balance both.” Dlaczego Prezydent RP Karol Nawrocki zawetował ustawę o DSA? ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/1BUJVFEftl — Kancelaria Prezydenta RP (@prezydentpl) November 13, 2026 Deputy digital affairs minister Dariusz Standerski, however, said that the president was “not defending free speech” but instead “once again siding with global [digital] platforms and allowing them to decide what users see”. “The vetoed provisions concerned illegal content, not opinions or views expressed online,” added the ministry, which also noted that all decisions on blocking content were subject to appeals and judicial review. Prime Minister Donald Tusk, meanwhile, accused Nawrocki of “waging war on the government at the expense of Polish children and Polish security”, which would both be threatened by the absence of the vetoed measures. Z prezydenckiego weta zadowoleni są hejterzy, rosyjskie farmy trolli, pedofile, ekstremalni nihiliści i lobbyści. Ofiarami tego weta są polskie dzieci, rodzice, bezpieczeństwo wszystkich obywateli. Tego nie da się w żaden sposób usprawiedliwić. — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) November 14, 2026 Aleksandra Wójtowicz, an analyst on new technologies at the Polish Institute of International Affairs (PISM), told the Fakt newspaper that the measures do “not in any way relate to alleged censorship”. They are intended to force digital platforms to remove illegal content, she explained. Wójtowicz added that the measures would actually have protected free speech by giving Polish users whose accounts were unjustly deleted by social media platforms the right to appeal against those decisions outside of the platform itself. However, Nawrocki’s veto was praised by Przemysław Czarnek, deputy leader of the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), Poland’s largest opposition party. Czarnek told TV Trwam that the proposed measures had been intended to “fight the opposition” rather than actual hate speech.
