World.title: Tallinn looks to add class for teens still not enrolled in school
World.content:
Tallinn has asked the Education Ministry to approve an extra preparatory class for 15 of 81 city teens still not enrolled despite being required to continue their education.

According to the Tallinn Education Department, 81 teens in Estonia's capital remained unenrolled as of Monday.

Of these, department director Kaarel Rundu said, 19 want to continue their education but have been unable to enroll in a suitable school, mainly due to poor academic performance or limited Estonian-language proficiency.

The department has asked the Ministry of Education and Research to approve the additional class at Tallinn Vocational College (TARK), which confirmed it is prepared to open one for 15 students.

'We have nowhere to refer them'

In the application, Rundu noted that preparatory classes at Tallinn's state schools are all already or nearly full, including with students the department has recommended for the program.

"This means there are at least 16 compulsory-school-age teens in Tallinn who should be enrolled in preparatory education, but we currently have nowhere to refer them," he said.

The education department head stressed that preparatory education provides an essential path forward for students who struggled academically in basic school, giving them a chance to continue their education.

Education Ministry communications adviser Elo Eesmäe told ERR that the ministry plans to grant the request, confirming that Tallinn's application is currently awaiting approval.

An empty classroom. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

Various circumstances

Krista Keedus, head of the Tallinn Education Department's Education Administration Unit, said efforts to find appropriate schools for students will nonetheless continue throughout the school year as their circumstances change.

Of the 81 youth listed as unenrolled in Tallinn, 31 have parents who have not responded to the department's inquiries, while four have incomplete contact information listed in the education information system.

Another three are taking paid courses that do not count as formal education, while two already have school placements that are missing from the records for technical reasons.

"At least two youth are awaiting a response about preparatory education, while six are enrolled in online schools, primarily in Ukraine, where they are already in their senior year of high school," Keedus said, listing more of the reasons students remain unenrolled in Estonia.

Health issues also a factor

Alongside various other individual circumstances, another seven young people have physical or mental health issues preventing them from starting or continuing school, the city official added.

The list also includes three teens added in the past two weeks: one after moving and two after being unenrolled from their previous schools.

The compulsory school attendance age in Estonia was only just raised to 18 this year.

World.title: Prorector: Using AI to evaluate research funding applications could affect entire system
World.content:
The Estonian Research Council is testing the use of artificial intelligence to evaluate research funding applications, prompting concerns from the University of Tartu over transparency, fairness and data protection.

The Estonian Research Council (ETAG) plans to test the use of artificial intelligence in evaluating research funding applications and has informed the University of Tartu of its plans.

In response, University of Tartu Vice Rector for Research, Professor Mari Moora told the council that while testing new technological solutions is a positive step, the experiment could affect the equal treatment of researchers, the transparency of the evaluation process and confidence in the research funding system. Its potential broader implications must therefore be considered.

"The letter sent to the research community does not make clear the nature of the planned activity — whether it is a research study, a technological validation test, an effort to develop evaluation methodology or an improvement to administrative procedures — or what specific task AI would perform in the proposed experiment," Moora said.

According to Moora, the letter also fails to explain how the use of AI would relate to the existing expert review process or what criteria would be used to evaluate the experiment's results. She believes several questions need to be clarified before the experiment begins, including how data protection and confidentiality will be ensured.

"At present, there is no information on whether the data will be processed on platforms operated by external AI service providers or in an environment controlled by ETAG, what contractual and technical safeguards will be used or how potential data protection and confidentiality risks have been assessed," the vice rector said.

She emphasized that research proposals may contain sensitive or unpublished information, making it essential to address these questions before the experiment begins.

Another concern is ensuring the quality of evaluations and equal treatment. Moora pointed out that the council has yet to explain how it intends to assess the overall impact of AI use on evaluation quality or how it will evaluate the risks of potential bias or unequal treatment.

"I believe it is particularly important to analyze the impact on different fields of research, research traditions and methodological approaches and to ensure that innovative, high-risk or unconventional research ideas are evaluated fairly even when AI is used in the evaluation process," Moora said.

Who will be responsible for AI evaluation results?

Accountability also raises questions. Moora noted that while human experts are personally responsible for their assessments, must declare that they have no conflicts of interest and risk their reputations if they act improperly, it is difficult to understand what considerations underpin an AI-generated assessment.

"If AI output influences a funding decision, it may become more difficult to assess whether that decision is justified and lawful. This, in turn, raises the question of how such a decision could be meaningfully challenged or reviewed in administrative proceedings, including how to establish whether errors of judgment or other procedural shortcomings occurred in the decision-making process," Moora said.

According to Moora, since the experiment is presumably intended to assess the potential use of AI in preparing research funding decisions, it should examine not only how the existing technological solution performs but also how it could affect the research system as a whole.

"Evaluation systems inevitably influence researchers' behavior, so attention should also be paid to the risk that researchers may begin tailoring their applications to the assumptions or expectations of algorithmic systems rather than presenting their scientific ideas in a way that best supports substantive evaluation by experts," Moora said, adding that this could limit research institutions' freedom to choose which areas of research to pursue.

The University of Tartu vice rector emphasized that her questions do not stem from opposition to the use of AI or efforts to improve research funding processes. However, she said these possibilities must be thoroughly examined, carefully considered and discussed with the research community.

The sustainability of the research funding system is another concern. Moora explained that generative AI could significantly increase the number of applications, while high-quality expert review depends on a limited pool of specialists in each field. Researchers therefore also consider it important to discuss how to maintain the quality of the funding and evaluation system if the volume of applications grows faster than the capacity to review them.

ETAg: Precisely the questions the experiment aims to answer

Estonian Research Council Director Kristiina Tõnnisson told ERR that the current phase could be described as a trial run for an experiment, using projects that have already undergone evaluation.

The council is now comparing AI-generated assessments of research projects with existing evaluations by human experts to establish a baseline for comparison.

Addressing the concerns raised by Moora, Tõnnisson said the experiment only involves projects whose principal investigators had checked with their teams to see whether anyone objected. No objections were raised. The evaluation experiment is being conducted on a couple of selected platforms. Although the council also considered developing an in-house system, it concluded that solutions developed specifically for Estonia performed considerably worse than large language models.

"So, for efficiency reasons, we decided to use large language models, but these operate in closed environments," she explained.

Regarding the risk that AI might favor familiar ideas and discriminate against original ones, Tõnnisson said the experiment is intended to examine precisely these kinds of risks. The trial should help identify which evaluation criteria AI struggles with, when it produces good summaries and when it does not.

"We hope to get more answers to these questions before we start saying that we are considering using AI to assist with evaluations in real-world situations," the council's director said.

The Estonian Research Council hopes to draw its first conclusions from the current experiment in about a month, before Christmas. It will then be able to consider whether this approach could be pursued further in the future.

World.title: Estonian-Russian border crossings have dropped considerably since 2022
World.content:
The number of times people have crossed the Russian border has fallen from over 4 million before 2022 to around 760,000 so far this year.

Estonia will close three land border crossing points with Russia from December 1, following an attempted arson at a drone company attributed to Russia's military intellegence. Those closing will be in Narva and at Luhamaa and Koidula in southeastern Estonia.

Before Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine and the coronavirus pandemic, the number of crossings was between four and five million each year.

But this dropped off considerably from 2022, when there were 1.6 million trips made back and forth across the border.

The number rose slightly in 2023 (1.8 million), before falling in 2024 (1.6 million), 2025 (1.1 million), and 2026 (760,000).

These figures do not show the number of people, but the total number of crossings in both directions.

The number of border crossings, in both directions, at the Estonian-Russian border has fallen since 2022. Source: ERR

The majority – 447,000 – of crossings take place in the northeastern border town, Narva.

The southeastern crossing points in Luhamaa and Koidula see considerably less traffic, with 138,000 and 172,000 crossings, respectively.

The pedestrian crossing at Saatse, also in the southeast, is around 4,000 this year.

The majority of crossings take place in Narva. Source: ERR

So far this year, Russians have crossed the border in the highest numbers (308,000) and Estonian citizens (179,000).

They are followed by Finns (55,000), stateless citizens (53,000) and Latvians (44,000).

Since Finland closed its border with Russia in 2023, Finns have often chosen to cross the border in Estonia.

Border crossings Source: ERR

World.title: Estonia's eastern border closure will stop bus and truck traffic to Russia
World.content:
Estonia's plan to close its land border crossings with Russia in December will force bus companies to discontinue routes from Tallinn to St. Petersburg and Moscow.

The closure of three border crossings in northeastern and southeastern Estonia will affect tourists, freight transport, and buses from December 1, following an attempted arson at a drone company attributed to Russia's military intellegence. While most trucks already use border crossings in Latvia, the situation is different for buses.

Bus company Ecolines operates one daily service on both the Tallinn-St. Petersburg and Tallinn-Moscow routes.

"We now have to sit down and do some calculations to see what this means for us. It's not just that we will have to start refunding passengers for their tickets, but it is also a very big logistical change. We have to redirect our vehicles, we have to reorganize our logistics network, the people working there, the staff, the bus drivers," said Ecolines Chairman of the Board Elis Kovaljov told Monday's "Aktuaalne kaamera".

Lux Express coach company also operates services to Russia. Board member Ingmar Roos said the border closure would not damage the company much.

The Estonian-Russian border runs through Lake Peipus. Border crossing points are highlighted on the map. Source: Helen Wright/ERR/OSM

"As things stand, just over 2,000 tickets have been purchased for journeys scheduled to take place from December 1 onward. And in fact, we have had to take into account the possibility of the border closing completely since 2022. If this happens, it is a risk we have already accounted for," he said.

The cross-border transport sector has already shrunk considerably since 2022, when Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

While around 500 companies transported goods to Russia before the war, fewer than 50 remain today. Transport businesses see an opportunity in Latvia.

"Looking at the current capacity of the Luhamaa and Koidula border crossings [in south Estonia] for trucks, fewer than ten trucks pass through per day. The few that remain are already using Latvian border crossings. The capacity of the Estonian border is very small," said Ermo Perolainen, Secretary General of the Association of Estonian International Road Carriers.

Buses could also travel to Russia via Latvia, but according to company executives, it is not that simple.

A truck at the Luhamaa border crossing point in February 2026. Source: ETV

"Lux Express does not plan to attempt to operate via Latvia, and as far as I know, the Latvian government has announced that it will not issue new route permits or extend existing ones," Ingmar Roos said.

Elis Kovaljov, from Ecolines, said the company cannot "simply change things overnight."

"We still need valid documentation and valid route permits under which we can operate. If we have route permits through Latvia, then we can certainly do that and also serve those Latvian border crossings. But let's put it this way: if a decision is made at the common European level, I don't believe Estonia will be the only country to go along with it and close its border crossings. My opinion is that the other Baltic states will follow suit," he said.

Estonian officials have also suggested Latvia close its border with Russia, but it is not yet known what decision the government will make.

"That is Latvia's decision, as all these border crossing closures are decisions for each country to make itself. Of course, this would be more painful for Russia. We can already see that the Kremlin has reacted very strongly even to the closure of Estonia's border, so yes, we should rather increase this pressure and show that every action Russia takes against us has consequences," Minister of Foreign Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200) said.

World.title: Photos: Truck crash jams outbound traffic on Tallinn's Tartu maantee
World.content:
A truck crashed into a lamppost on Tartu maantee and got stuck under an overpass Monday afternoon, disrupting outbound traffic at a busy Tallinn junction ahead of rush hour.

Two outbound lanes on Tartu maantee have been closed due to the crash, backing up traffic near Ülemiste, T1 and Sikupilli shopping malls, Ülemiste train station and Tallinn Airport.

Police received a report of a crash at around 2:30 p.m. on Monday.

Initial information suggests the truck and its trailer struck part of the overpass, bringing down an overhead road sign gantry onto the roadway.

The driver, a 37-year-old man, was sober and licensed to operate the vehicle. No one was injured in the crash.

Police at the scene have been redirecting traffic via Peterburi tee.

World.title: CNN: US intelligence points to possible Iranian plot targeting Trump officials with a 'dirty bomb'
World.content:
DUBAI: New US intelligence suggests Iran is exploring plans to target senior officials in US President Donald Trump’s administration with a so-called dirty bomb or chemical attack in Washington, CNN reported, citing seven US officials.

The plans appear intended to give Tehran options rather than signal an imminent attack. But the intelligence identifies specific locations and potential targets, prompting US authorities to strengthen contingency plans, CNN reported.

US officials see the intelligence as evidence of Iran’s willingness to escalate amid continued US military strikes and an economic blockade that senior administration officials have described as devastating.

There is no evidence that Tehran has decided to proceed with an attack, and officials remain divided over whether Iran has the personnel to carry one out.

“Whether they actually have the personnel in place to execute is a matter of debate,” one source told CNN.

White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said the administration was monitoring potential threats but stressed that “there are no credible threats to the homeland” at this time.

World.title: Iran and Oman discuss shipping amid Hormuz blockade
World.content:
The Omani and Iranian foreign ministers discussed safeguarding maritime corridors and ensuring the smooth flow of international navigation, the Omani foreign ministry said in a statement on Tuesday.

The meeting comes amid Tehran’s ongoing blockade of the crucial Strait of Hormuz, a consequence of the Middle East war.

Iran’s top diplomat, Abbas Araghchi, and his Omani counterpart, Badr Albusaidi, held talks in Muscat on diplomatic options to contain tensions and revitalize tracks of dialogue and negotiation, as reported by the Oman News Agency.

These efforts aim to expand areas of mutual understanding among the concerned parties and prevent the widening of the crisis and its repercussions.

The ministers also emphasized the importance of safeguarding the security of maritime passages to ensure the uninterrupted flow of international navigation and trade.

Iran has been conducting regular attacks on ships in Hormuz, the primary exit route for Gulf energy exports, since the war began with US-Israel strikes on February 28.

Amid the blockade, Iran insists vessels use routes it has authorized to transit Hormuz.

The situation has significantly increased oil prices, subsequently raising fuel and other costs globally.

The discussions highlighted reactivating diplomatic avenues and negotiation tracks to prevent further escalation.

World.title: Pakistan army chief and Iran FM discuss regional peace, security
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Asim Munir, the powerful army chief of mediating country Pakistan, met with Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi, the Pakistani military said Tuesday, during continued efforts to end the war between the United States and Iran.

Pakistan brokered a June accord that led to a brief halt in fighting between the United States and Iran and set a roadmap for further agreement on reopening the crucial Strait of Hormuz waterway and for negotiations on Tehran’s nuclear program.

But the truce collapsed with Washington and Tehran accusing each other of violating the agreement and prompting months of shuttle diplomacy to resuscitate the ceasefire, led principally by mediators Qatar and Pakistan.

During the meeting on Monday, “matters of mutual interest, regional security dynamics and evolving geopolitical developments were discussed,” the Pakistani military’s media wing said in a statement.

Munir “underscored the importance of sustained engagement, mutual trust and close coordination between the two brotherly countries for promoting regional peace and stability,” it added.

Araghchi arrived in Pakistan late on Sunday for a meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organization, a group of nations from Central and South Asia and the Middle East.

Pakistani Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said on Monday he had held “very candid, very frank” discussions with Araghchi, during the conference confirming that Iran had put forward a two-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz as part of efforts to end the war with the United States.

He said Washington had not yet responded.

The United States and Israel launched the war on February 28, killing members of Iran’s leadership and demanding it cease any nuclear-related activities.

The war plunged the Middle East into violence, with Tehran’s retaliatory strikes targeting Washington’s Gulf allies and sending global energy prices skyrocketing.

Tehran has insisted that Washington meet conditions including the release of frozen assets abroad, sanctions relief and an end to the US naval blockade of Iranian ports in exchange for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: Drones behind nearly 75% of civilian deaths this year in Sudan war: UN
World.content:
Geneva, Switzerland: Nearly three quarters of all the verified civilian fatalities this year in the war in Sudan were caused by drones, the UN said Tuesday.

Out of 2,230 civilian deaths that occurred between the start of January and the end of October, and confirmed by the UN human rights office OHCHR, more than 1,630 were a result of drone attacks, which have “eclipsed the use of other tactics and weaponry,” it said.

World.title: Pope Leo lands in Rome following South America visit
World.content:
Aboard the Papal Plane: Pope Leo XIV landed in Rome on Monday following a 12-day papal voyage to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru.

After departing from the Peruvian capital of Lima, the papal plane landed at Rome’s Fiumicino Airport Monday at 8:48 am local time (0748 GMT).

World.title: NATO allies to discuss US forces in Europe with Pentagon strategy chief, Pistorius says
World.content:
BRUSSELS: NATO allies will discuss Washington’s ongoing review of US troop levels in Europe with Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby in Brussels ‌on Tuesday, German ‌Defense minister ‌Boris Pistorius said.

Even though the expectation is for US troops levels in Europe to decline, it is crucial ‌to ‌prevent dangerous capability gaps ‌through talks with ‌the US, Pistorius said before a meeting with other EU ‌defense ministers in Brussels.

Pistorius also said Germany and Norway will sponsor another package of US weapons for Ukraine through the PURL mechanism, focusing mainly on air defenses.

World.title: South Korea tightens exam security after AI cheating scandal
World.content:
SEOUL: South Korea will deploy thousands of extra personnel to prevent cheating on its college entrance exam sites this week and may introduce tougher penalties, Prime Minister Han Seong-sook said Tuesday.

The announcement comes after an individual confessed on Sunday to cheating on the national tax accountant exam using artificial intelligence tools, an admission that brought panic ahead of the college test.

Known as the Suneung, the intense once-a-year exam — widely seen as a ticket to well-paid jobs and even better marriage prospects — will bring much of South Korea to a standstill on Thursday to minimize distractions.

As a measure to detect phones that have not been handed over, an emergency alert will be sent before the exam begins, Han said at a press conference.

Students will also be ordered to place their glasses on their desks so supervisors can verify they are not smart devices.

“We also strongly urge students to avoid wearing clothing with buttons wherever possible,” Han said.

Students “will be asked to roll up both sleeves, and collars, buttons and other areas will also be checked to determine whether electronic devices, including miniature cameras, are concealed,” she added.

Those caught cheating could be banned from taking the Suneung for 10 years, up from the current one-year restriction, Han said.

The government will also file criminal complaints over serious cases of cheating, including those involving smart devices.

In addition to the 75,000 supervisors deployed to 1,312 test centers nationwide, an additional 8,400 personnel will be deployed this year.

“You may feel nervous and intimidated by the unfamiliar atmosphere inside and outside examination centers and the stricter inspection procedures,” said Han, addressing the 550,000 students who will take the Suneung.

The extra staff “are minimum safeguards designed to protect the value of the hard work you have put in over the years and to guarantee a fair competition in which everyone can hold their head high,” she added.

At a meeting held Sunday, officials decided to investigate all suspected cases of cheating involving AI across national qualification examinations.

The individual who confessed to cheating said he had photographed the exam questions with a miniature camera before using AI and checking the answers on his smartphone.

Han said the government “will define such cheating as a ‘social evil’.”

World.title: China says has ‘no information’ on whether N. Korea’s Kim will meet Trump
World.content:
BEIJING: China said Tuesday it has “no information” on whether Donald Trump would meet Kim Jong Un, after the US president left open the possibility of meeting the North Korean leader on his Asia trip.

“I have no information regarding this matter,” foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular briefing, a day before Trump was expected in Shenzhen for an APEC meeting.

World.title: US dollar holds above 171,000 dinars across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra markets
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar recorded a renewed upward tick across major domestic parallel markets on Tuesday morning, November 17, 2026, holding firmly above the 171,000 IQD threshold across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra.

According to morning trading figures across key commercial hubs, physical banknote rates traded as follows:

Baghdad: Currency exchange counters posted retail selling rates at 171,050 IQD against buying offers of 170,250 IQD per $100.

Erbil: Currency desks quoted selling rates at 171,250 IQD alongside buying bids of 170,500 IQD per $100.

Basra: Foreign exchange offices matched Erbil’s selling ceiling at 171,250 IQD, with purchasing offers settling firmer at 170,750 IQD per $100.

This sustained parallel-market elevation maintains a spread of more than 19,000 dinars above the Central Bank of Iraq’s (CBI) official rate of 152,000 IQD per $100 (1,520 IQD per dollar)—a peg established following the government’s October 7, 2026 currency adjustment.

The persistent premium reflects heightened domestic political and security uncertainty alongside continued physical cash demand to settle unrecorded cross-border imports outside formal electronic banking channels.

World.title: Sirens activated after drone flew over Iraq’s Khor Mor gas field
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Warning sirens were activated at the Khor Mor gas field in Iraqi Kurdistan on Monday after an unidentified drone flew over the facility.

Two security sources confirmed the alert to Reuters, noting there were no immediate reports of a strike, casualties, or new damage.

Security officials have not identified who launched the drone. Kurdish authorities have previously attributed similar threats against the site to Iran-backed armed factions.

The overflight comes just one week after a drone attack targeted the gas field on September 8, forcing joint field operator Dana Gas to halt production entirely.

The strike hit a liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) storage tank, causing a large fire that was later extinguished.

The facility is the main source of energy for the Kurdistan region of Iraq and the largest gas field there.

Between 2,500 and 2,800 megawatts of power output had been cut off due to the stoppage of gas operations, reducing 70 to 80 percent of the energy grid’s overall capacity.

Iraqi Kurdistan’s major cities, including Erbil, Sulaimaniyah, Duhok, Bazian, and Chamchamal, were no longer receiving direct electricity supply.

The facility was temporarily closed in July due to security concerns resulting from escalating military tensions between the United States and Iran.

World.title: Iraqi security identifies two illegal oil refineries in Jurf al-Nasr
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi authorities uncovered two illegal oil refineries, storage facilities, and evidence of pipeline tampering in the Jurf al-Nasr, also known as Jurf al-Sakhar, area in Iraq’s central province of Babil.

The discoveries were confirmed following a high-level government investigation launched by Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and a parliamentary inquiry.

Six places were investigated by government detectives, who found two refineries operating illegally, oil tanks, and a tanker truck, as well as hidden changes in state oil pipelines.

A parliamentary committee examined drone footage, thermal images, and documents indicating around 25 tanker trucks, each with the capacity to carry 36,000 liters, were used within the smugglers’ network.

According to reports, the illicit operations had been ongoing since 2021, developing from exposed oil pits to covered loading points and underground storage to avoid being detected.

Following an emergency security meeting on Saturday, al-Zaidi dismissed nine senior security, intelligence, and oil-sector officials. He also ordered all individuals implicated in the smuggling operations to be referred to the judiciary for prosecution.

On Monday, government spokesperson Haider al-Aboudi announced that al-Zaidi ordered Iraqi troops into Jurf al-Nasr to restore state control and dismantle the networks.

Authorities also gave the Iran-backed armed group Kataib Hezbollah, which controls Jurf al-Nasr, until the weekend as a deadline to withdraw.

World.title: Iraq, Saudi Arabia begin replacing Iranian oil in China
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq and Saudi Arabia have begun replacing Iranian crude oil in China after Tehran’s shipments plunged under a US naval blockade, according to reports from Bloomberg and vessel-tracking data from Vortexa.

Iran’s oil exports to China fell to less than 100,000 barrels per day in October 2026 compared to roughly 1.4 million barrels per day before the outbreak of regional conflict in February.

The US maritime blockade imposed on Iranian ports along the Arabian Gulf in July 2026 severely restricted Tehran’s ability to export crude by sea.

Independent Chinese refiners have turned to trading houses like Mercuria Energy Group to source up to 20 million barrels of discounted Iraqi oil transported through the Strait of Hormuz.

Iraqi Basra grades have offered some of the most cost-effective alternatives for December 2026 arrivals, trading at significantly lower premiums over Brent than competing Russian barrels.

Saudi Arabia and Iraq are stepping in to cover the gap left by Iran, which previously made up roughly 13 percent of China’s seaborne imports.

Iraq’s oil supplies to China during September totaled 4.84 million tons, or about 1.18 million barrels per day, a 19 percent decline compared to the previous year and a 248 percent increase compared to August.

China’s crude oil imports from Saudi Arabia stood at 2.70 million tons, or about 660,000 barrels per day, marking a 62 percent decline compared to the previous year.

Chinese independent refiners increased recently their imports of Iraqi and Qatari crude to compensate for a sharp decline in Iranian oil supplies.

As their stockpiles near depletion, private refineries in China are paying considerable premiums to acquire alternatives.

World.title: Internal rift splits Kata’ib Hezbollah over Jurf Al Nasr handover
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – An internal leadership rift has emerged within Kata’ib Hezbollah over the security future of Jurf al-Sakhar (Jurf al-Nasr) as high-stakes negotiations unfold with Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s government amid escalating military mobilizations around the northern Babylon subdistrict.

According to exclusive disclosures obtained by the 964 Network, Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF/Hashd al-Shaabi) Chief of Staff Abdul-Aziz Al-Muhammadawi (“Abu Fadak”) favors reaching a negotiated settlement with the Al-Zaidi administration that would permit federal forces to enter and assume security responsibility over sectors of the area.

Conversely, Kata’ib Hezbollah Secretary-General Abu Hussein Al-Hamidawi remains firmly opposed to granting security concessions at this stage, holding Abu Fadak directly responsible for the political and legal fallout triggered after a government investigative committee entered the restricted zone for the first time in 12 years.

Sources familiar with the ongoing talks revealed that the faction’s Al-Hamidawi wing proposed deferring any handover of Jurf al-Sakhar until June 30, 2027, aligning the transfer with the scheduled expiration of the national deadline for restricting weapons to state control.

Prime Minister Al-Zaidi, however, rejected maintaining the status quo for that duration, insisting on the immediate deployment of federal security forces to hold all or key parts of the subdistrict and actively participate in security decision-making.

Al-Hamidawi’s posture reportedly hardened sharply over the past several hours due to the unanticipated consequences of Abu Fadak’s earlier understanding with Baghdad.

That initial agreement permitted federal investigators to inspect the closed territory, culminating in official findings of illicit oil smuggling, public disclosures, and judicial referrals—an outcome that left Al-Hamidawi deeply wary of authorizing any further security compromises.

The leadership split has sown operational confusion among Kata’ib Hezbollah’s field commanders and brigade leaders stationed inside Jurf al-Sakhar. Historically, the group’s chain of command relied on Al-Hamidawi setting broad strategic policy while Abu Fadak issued operational directives and execution mechanisms; their conflicting stances on a federal handover have left local units without unified instructions at a critical juncture.

Meanwhile, federal military preparations continue to intensify around the perimeter:

World.title: Rival reinforcements converge on Jurf Al Nasr as Al Zaidi sets deadline for Kata’ib Hezbollah
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Armed personnel reinforcements—believed to belong to allied armed factions—arrived in the Jurf al-Nasr (Jurf al-Sakhar) subdistrict of northern Babylon Governorate on Monday evening, November 16, 2026, to bolster Kata’ib Hezbollah positions against a potential armed confrontation with state forces, according to a security source.

In immediate response, federal command dispatched additional detachments from the Federal Police and the Counter-Terrorism Service (CTS) stationed in neighboring provinces to reinforce military units already massing around the subdistrict.

The dual mobilization follows consecutive overnight troop deployments toward northern Babylon after Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi formalized a directive ordering official security forces to enter Jurf al-Nasr and assume full security jurisdiction.

Government spokesperson Haider Al-Aboudi confirmed that Baghdad has issued a strict deadline for Kata’ib Hezbollah to withdraw from the subdistrict—reportedly expiring on Friday, November 20—while Coordination Framework figures, including Nouri Al-Maliki, Hadi Al-Amiri, and Humam Hamoudi, pursue eleventh-hour mediation to secure a phased handover and prevent open hostilities.

The standoff stems directly from the formal findings of the government investigative commission dispatched to Jurf al-Nasr on November 13, which inspected six intelligence-flagged coordinates and documented clear pipeline tampering, two clandestine refining facilities, and underground storage tanks.

Based on the report, Al-Zaidi referred implicated suspects to the judiciary, ordered security forces to block all unauthorized fuel tankers from exiting the area, and dismissed nine senior security, military, and administrative officials in Babylon—including the Provincial Police Chief and the provincial Hashd al-Shaabi commander.

Kata’ib Hezbollah flatly rejected the smuggling allegations, asserting that the field inspection uncovered no pipeline breaches and claiming that the tanks and processing equipment found on site were strictly used to supply fuel for military vehicles. Escalating its defiance on Monday via its official Telegram channel, the faction published photographs of fighters preparing drones and declared that its weapons remain an inviolable right in the hands of its fighters.

World.title: Iraq claims fourth place globally at 2026 Youth Muay Thai World Championships in Greece
World.content:
Olympia (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s national youth Muay Thai team secured fourth place globally at the 2026 IFMA Youth World Championships held in Ancient Olympia, Greece, capturing an impressive 25-medal haul against competitors from 109 countries.

According to an official statement issued by Iraqi Muay Thai Federation President Mustafa Jabbar Alak, Iraq’s medal tally broke down as follows:

Gold Medals: 11

Silver Medals: 5

Bronze Medals: 9

Staged from November 6 to 16, 2026, the tournament brought together more than 800 athletes aged 8 to 18 competing across 154 divisions in full-contact ring bouts, semi-contact technical events, and traditional Wai Kru and Mai Muay disciplines.

Alak credited the fourth-place world finish to sustained preparation by the athletes, coaching staff, and administrative leadership. He underscored that the achievement represents a major milestone for Iraqi combat sports, demonstrating the technical caliber and international competitiveness of Iraq’s rising generation of fighters on the global podium.

World.title: Zaidi invites German firms to invest in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi met with Germany’s Federal Minister for Economic Cooperation and Development, Reem Alabali-Radovan, and her accompanying delegation in Baghdad on Monday, November 16, 2026, renewing his call for German corporations to enter the Iraqi market and participate in major infrastructure and industrial projects.

According to a statement from the Prime Minister’s Media Office, discussions centered on expanding bilateral cooperation across economic, commercial, and investment sectors. Al-Zaidi emphasized the depth of Iraqi-German ties and underscored that the federal government is prepared to grant extensive incentives and administrative facilitations to streamline operations for foreign investors entering Iraq.

Highlighting Iraq’s strategic push to build a diversified, non-oil economy, the Prime Minister pointed to the flagship Development Road Project as a primary catalyst for bilateral partnership, noting the substantial commercial opportunities embedded in its planned industrial and economic cities along the transit corridor.

For her part, Minister Alabali-Radovan reaffirmed Berlin’s backing for the Iraqi government’s reform and development agenda, expressing Germany’s readiness to expand joint initiatives across key priority sectors:

Climate, Environment & Agriculture: Expanding technical and developmental cooperation to address environmental stress, climate resilience, and sustainable agricultural modernization.

Institutional Development Financing: Moving forward with signing a formal Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) linking Iraq with the German Agency for International Cooperation (GIZ) and the German Development Bank (KfW) to anchor long-term bilateral projects.

The Baghdad meeting builds directly on Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s official visit to Berlin in mid-September 2026, where he held talks with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz to deepen European trade ties and attract German industrial investment into Iraq.

World.title: Cyclone Akvan: IMD warns of extremely heavy rainfall, 145 kmph winds along Andhra coast
World.content:
Cyclonic Storm Akvan, currently positioned over the central parts of the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal, is expected to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm by the morning of November 19 before making landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast around noon on November 20, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said on Tuesday.

According to the IMD's national bulletin issued at 2:30 am IST on November 17, the storm remained nearly stationary over the previous nine hours and continued to be centred over the same region.

The weather system was located near latitude 12.2Â°N and longitude 85.7Â°E, around 610 km east of Chennai in Tamil Nadu, 630 km northeast of Trincomalee in Sri Lanka, 660 km southeast of Machilipatnam in Andhra Pradesh, 670 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam and 790 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha, according to the news agency ANI.



The IMD said the storm is likely to move north-northwestwards and strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by the evening of November 17.

It is subsequently expected to continue moving northwestwards and intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm by the morning of November 19.

According to the forecast, the system will continue its northwestward movement before crossing the Andhra Pradesh and yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni around noon on November 20.





At the time of landfall, the cyclone is expected to generate maximum sustained wind speeds of 120-130 kmph, with gusts reaching up to 145 kmph, the bulletin stated.

The IMD has issued an orange alert for the Andhra Pradesh coast and adjoining coastal areas of south Odisha, warning of the potential impact of the approaching cyclone.

Heavy rainfall warning for Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh

The weather department has forecast light to moderate rainfall at several places across north Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal on November 17 and 20, with isolated areas likely to receive heavy rainfall.

Heavy to very heavy rainfall is also expected at isolated places on November 18 and 19, potentially causing waterlogging in parts of Tamil Nadu.

For coastal Andhra Pradesh, the IMD has predicted light to moderate rainfall at several locations, accompanied by heavy showers at isolated places on November 18.

The situation could intensify on November 19 and 20, with isolated areas of north coastal Andhra Pradesh likely to receive extremely heavy rainfall exceeding 21 cm.

Odisha also likely to receive heavy rainfall

In Odisha, isolated areas are likely to experience heavy rainfall on November 18, with light to moderate showers expected at some places.

The IMD has further forecast light to moderate rainfall across most places in the state, along with heavy to very heavy showers at isolated locations between November 19 and 21.

The weather department's latest warning indicates that the approaching cyclone could bring intense rainfall and strong winds to several coastal districts, particularly in Andhra Pradesh and adjoining regions.

World.title: ‘Criminal contempt’: Calcutta High Court issues show-cause notice to Abhishek Banerjee over remarks against court
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Calcutta High Court on Tuesday issued a show-cause notice to

(TMC) MP

, holding that his statements and a social media post against the court amounted to âex facie criminal contemptâ.

Justice Krishna Rao directed the Diamond Harbour MP to explain within 15 days of the notice being issued why appropriate punishment should not be imposed on him.

Passing the order in criminal contempt proceedings initiated by the court, Justice Rao said he had examined the transcript of Banerjee's remarks and his November 7 social media post.

âThe Facebook post of the alleged contemnor prima facie amounts to interference with the administration of justice,â the judge said.



The court held that Banerjee had âcommitted ex facie criminal contempt of courtâ and directed that a show-cause notice be issued to him. The matter will be heard next on December 8.

High Court directs review of Banerjee's security arrangements

In a separate case concerning the security cover provided to the TMC MP, the High Court, led by Justice Rao, directed the West Bengal Home Department and its principal secretary to convene a meeting of the security review committee within two weeks.





The committee has been asked to examine and assess matters related to Banerjee's security arrangements.

World.title: Watch: Prince William, Kate Middleton ride electric three-wheeler at Mumbai Earthshot event
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prince William and Kate Middleton on Tuesday visited Bandra Reclamation Garden in Mumbai, where the Prince drove an electric three-wheeler with the Princess of Wales as a passenger.

The royal couple also interacted with the 15 finalists of The Earthshot Prize 2026 from across the world.

The event, set against the backdrop of the Bandra-Worli Sea Link, gathered finalists who are developing innovative answers to environmental problems.

Indiaâs representatives among the 15 finalists are Mahindra Last Mile Mobility and Mahila Housing Trust, ANI reported.

The meeting was a key engagement before the Earthshot Prize awards ceremony, which India is hosting for the first time.



Five winners will be announced later on Tuesday, and each will receive Euro 1 million to help expand their environmental solutions.

The Earthshot Prize honours innovative approaches to environmental challenges, and this year it has taken its global platform to India, spotlighting solutions aimed at protecting and restoring the planet.

On Monday, the first day of their Mumbai trip, Prince William and Kate had a packed schedule that included riding the Mumbai Metro, playing gully cricket with school students and meeting cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar.





The couple landed in Mumbai on Monday for the annual environmental awards, which Prince William founded in 2020. They attended the Earthshot Prize 2026 Impact Assembly, where the Prince talked about Indiaâs role in finding solutions to environmental challenges.

In his speech, Prince William commended Indiaâs work on clean energy and sustainable development. He also said economic growth and environmental protection could go hand in hand.

âThere is a phrase in Hindi: âRang Birangi Duniyaâ. A world full of colour. Perhaps that is how we should see the future. Not in black and white, and not presented as a series of false choices between people and the planet, prosperity and nature, but in all its colours. A world in which solutions can come from anywhere,â he said.

World.title: No froth along 52-km stretch of Yamuna in Delhi: Water minister Parvesh Sahib Singh
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Delhi water minister Parvesh Sahib Singh claimed on Tuesday that no froth was present anywhere along the 52-km section of the Yamuna that passes through the national capital.

Speaking at a press conference, Singh dismissed allegations by the Aam Aadmi Party that devotees had been made to observe

at spots where the river was covered in froth.

âSeeing that the BJP has won the hearts of Purvanchali people, AAP is pained,â Singh said, as per PTI.

âChhath was celebrated with a lot of reverence and lakhs of people were so happy with the preparations,â he added.

However, Singh noted that the Delhi government was in talks with Uttar Pradesh to tackle the issue in areas near the Okhla Barrage, which lies on the UP-Delhi border.



The Okhla Barrage is often highlighted for the recurring formation of toxic froth on the Yamuna's surface.

According to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), monitoring conducted at Kalindi Kunj, downstream of the Okhla Barrage, between 2022 and 2024 found that the sudden fall of water from the barrage agitates foaming agents present in wastewater, causing foam to form and float on the Yamuna's surface.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Surfactants found in detergents are the main foaming agents in untreated or partially treated sewage.





Separately, a study titled Study on Yamuna Frothing in Delhi, conducted by the Energy and Resources Institute (Teri) for the Delhi government's environment department, identified poor water quality as the primary trigger for froth formation. It pointed to factors including effluents containing high levels of ammonia and phosphate released from anionic surfactants.

World.title: 'I am scared once again': Bilkis Bano releases statement after SC grants bail to two convicts
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Bilkis Bano said that "familiar fears are resurfacing" after the

suspended the sentences and granted bail to two of the 11 men convicted of gang-raping her and murdering 14 members of her family during the 2002 Gujarat riots.

In a statement issued on Monday, she expressed shock and disbelief over the order, saying she was neither informed about the proceedings nor given an opportunity to be heard.

"I still cannot believe that once again, for the second time, an order has been passed by the Supreme Court without calling me up and without hearing me. I learnt of this through press reports," she said.

The Supreme Court bench of Justices M M Sudresh and P B Varale passed the order on October 28, which was uploaded on Monday.



Reacting to the development, Bilkis said she was scared for herself, her family and her children, adding that the decision had shaken her faith in the justice system.

"For 24 years I have searched for and found reservoirs of courage I did not know I had, only because a million voices of support and solidarity came my way," she said, recalling her long fight for justice following the assault and the murder of her family members.





Bilkis, who was 19 at the time of the 2002 incident, said she had spent years rebuilding her life with the support of family and friends and had hoped to find peace. However, the latest order had brought back the fears she thought she had overcome.

"Yet today I find myself losing the very justice I had fought so hard to win. Familiar fears are resurfacing. I am scared once again. For myself, my family, and my children. And I am scared of losing faith in justice, yet again," she said.

Questioning why the court had not ensured that her voice was heard before passing the order, Bilkis said she would challenge the decision.

"I will fight this order. I must," she said, adding that she was doing so for her children and the memory of her three-year-old daughter Saleha, as well as for women everywhere.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"Because no woman, no survivor, no citizen should have to endure this eternal test of belonging and equality, and fight for justice for the rest of her life," she said.

Bilkis Bano was 21 years old and five months pregnant when she was gang-raped while trying to escape the horror of the communal riots that broke out after the Godhra train burning incident in February 2002. Her three-year-old daughter was among the seven family members killed.

World.title: NMC asks all government medical colleges, attached hospitals to join road accident cashless treatment scheme
World.content:
NMC has asked deans, directors, principals and medical superintendents to accord priority to the exercise and take necessary steps to facilitate their institutionsâ participation.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The National Medical Commission (NMC) has directed all government medical colleges and their attached hospitals across the country to onboard the Centreâs PM-RAHAT scheme, aimed at ensuring cashless treatment for road accident victims during the critical golden hour.In a public notice issued on Monday, the NMC has asked deans, directors, principals and medical superintendents to accord priority to the exercise and take necessary steps to facilitate their institutionsâ participation. The move follows a request from the Union Health Ministryâs Trauma and Burn Cell to the commission on October 28 to widen the network of hospitals under the scheme.The PM-RAHAT (Prime Ministerâs Road Accident Victimsâ Hospitalisation and Assured Treatment) scheme provides cashless treatment of up to Rs 1.5 lakh per accident victim for a maximum of seven days from the date of the accident at designated hospitals. Non-designated hospitals can provide stabilisation treatment to victims, ensuring that emergency care is not delayed while patients are referred to higher-level facilities.The guidelines issued by the National Health Authority (NHA) provide for two categories of hospitals under the scheme: designated hospitals, which can provide stabilisation, trauma and polytrauma services, and PM-RAHAT Lite hospitals, which can provide initial stabilisation before referring patients to higher-level facilities.Hospitals empanelled under Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY will be deemed eligible for designation. Other hospitals can also join, provided they meet the prescribed infrastructure and clinical requirements. These include round-the-clock emergency services, an equipped ICU, emergency operation theatre, imaging facilities, blood storage and ambulance services.The guidelines also prioritise hospitals located near accident-prone stretches, including national and state highways, identified road accident hotspots and municipal roads.The scheme was launched by the Prime Minister on February 13, 2026, with the objective of removing financial barriers to emergency treatment and strengthening trauma care across the country.

World.title: India lost 1,765 elephants in 17 years, Karnataka 223
World.content:
Factoring in all causes, Odisha (371) saw the highest number of elephant deaths, followed by Assam (356) and Karnataka (223)

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is the biggest step needed to prevent elephant deaths in India? Preventing illegal electric fencing Improving railway track safety Protecting elephant corridors Strengthening wildlife protection measures 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: As many as 1,765 elephants died of unnatural causes in the country in the past 17 years, with casualties due to electrocution being the biggest reason, followed by train collisions, poaching and poisoning, a response of the Union environment ministry to an RTI query shows.Data shows that electrocution alone killed 1,185 elephants (a little over 67% of total casualties) during the 2009-26 period, a number which is more than five times the number of elephants killed by poaching (222). Train hits caused 277 deaths, whereas 81 elephants died of poisoning during the period.Factoring in all causes, Odisha (371) saw the highest number of elephant deaths, followed by Assam (356) and Karnataka (223).Cause-wise, the highest number of deaths due to electrocution happened in Odisha (238), followed by Karnataka (195) and Assam (191). On the other hand, Assam reported the highest number of deaths (90) due to train collisions, followed by West Bengal (68) and Odisha (45).âElectrocution is not an accident. It is negligence â illegal electric fences, sagging wires and uninsulated lines in elephant corridors. This needs to be stopped and action needed for the same,â said Amit Gupta, Noida-based environmentalist, who filed the RTI query.Though the ministryâs response to him remains silent on it, an official told TOI that deaths due to electrocution are both âaccidental and intentionalâ. He said that, as elephants raid crops, farmers often illegally lay live electric wires to keep away ungulates and wild pigs, resulting in the deaths of elephants. He said even as the state is the sole responder, the ministry has taken steps towards minimising such deaths and mitigating wider human-elephant conflict (HEC) episodes.The ministryâs steps include a survey of sensitive stretches of railway line, a field guide (in vernacular languages as well) for mitigating HEC, identification and validation of elephant corridors, and carrying out a long-term study to know the trends, patterns and drivers of HEC in eight vulnerable states â Assam, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu (phase II) â and preparation of Regional Action Plans focusing on HEC.

World.title: IndiGo flight to Bengaluru aborts take-off at Mangaluru Airport
World.content:
IndiGo flight suffers technical glitch in Mangalore

MANGALURU: An IndiGo aircraft operating on the Bengaluru sector from Mangaluru aborted its take-off at approximately 6.05 pm on Monday. The aircraft, carrying 229 passengers and seven crew members, subsequently returned to the bay.Following a detailed technical inspection by the airlineâs engineering team, the aircraft was declared Aircraft on Ground (AOG). All passengers subsequently deboarded.The airport and airline teams were present to assist passengers and address their queries, ensuring the necessary support was extended to them.The airline subsequently arranged a ferry flight from Bengaluru and 34 of the original 229 passengers travelled on it with the relief aircraft leaving Mangaluru Airport at 12.10am on Tuesday, said sources.A source clarified that the aircraft in question was not airborne.
