World.title: Popular websites subverted in bid to steal crypto, target iPhone users
World.content:
Malicious JavaScript was aimed at visitors to the websites of 178 organizations across various sectors through Optimizely, a website optimization platform, according to researcher Scott Helme

Some of the world’s most visited websites, including those belonging to Zoom, HSBC, Equifax, CNN, Salesforce, and IKEA, were subverted in an effort to steal cryptocurrency and infect iPhones, a security researcher said on Monday, November 16.

Malicious JavaScript was aimed at visitors to the websites of 178 organizations across various sectors through Optimizely, a website optimization platform, according to researcher Scott Helme.

The scripts attempted to replace cryptocurrency payment addresses with the attacker’s wallet, skim card numbers as users entered credit card details, steal cookies and screenshots, and plant exploit code on iOS devices.

Cybersecurity firm HudsonRock also said it had found evidence that the sites had served malicious code to their visitors.

Reuters could not immediately ascertain whether the code was successfully used in each case, or the extent of any resulting hacks.

Salesforce said it was investigating unauthorized Optimizely script changes, and had disabled them as a precaution.

Equifax also investigated the issue and ceased using Optimizely. The company said it did not find evidence of any compromise to its systems.

Optimizely, Apple, Zoom, HSBC, CNN and IKEA did not immediately respond to Reuters’ requests for comment. – Rappler.com

World.title: US presses UN agency over Taiwan flight restrictions, China hits back
World.content:
LAI CHING-TE. Taiwan President Lai Ching-te speaks at the annual congress of the ruling Democratic Progressive Party in Taipei, Taiwan, July 19, 2026.

The fight over Taiwan's use of international airspace underscores growing tensions between Washington and Beijing over China's efforts to restrict the island's room to operate internationally, from its participation in global bodies to its diplomatic ties and overseas travel by senior officials

The US is asking the UN aviation agency to push back against flight restrictions involving Taiwan, reigniting its long-running dispute with China over Beijing’s efforts to limit the island’s international engagement.

In a paper submitted for the November session of the International Civil Aviation Organization’s governing council, Washington challenged the decision by Mauritius and Seychelles to revoke permission for an aircraft carrying Taiwan President Lai Ching-te to cross portions of international airspace they manage during a planned trip to Africa in April.

The US wants the ICAO Council to reaffirm that countries responsible for managing air traffic over the high seas do not have sovereignty over that airspace and cannot use that role for political purposes. Such actions could “set a dangerous precedent” by encouraging similar disruptions or political pressure on other countries, the paper said.

China hit back at the US proposal, accusing Washington of using the Taiwan issue for political purposes and wasting international resources.

The fight over Taiwan’s use of international airspace underscores growing tensions between Washington and Beijing over China’s efforts to restrict the island’s room to operate internationally, from its participation in global bodies to its diplomatic ties and overseas travel by senior officials.

The US document “selectively and one-sidedly cites” principles including freedom of overflight over the high seas and, “under the pretext of safeguarding freedom of navigation,” smears other countries and presumes sovereign states were at fault, China’s foreign ministry said in a statement to Reuters.

“There is only one China in the world, and Taiwan is an inalienable part of China’s territory,” it added. “China urges the countries concerned to stop using the Taiwan issue for political manipulation.”

Taiwan’s foreign ministry said it thanked the US and other like-minded countries for their previous concern about the issue.

The ministry will continue to work with allied countries to keep explaining to ICAO and the international community that “China’s actions undermine the international civil aviation order and flight safety,” it stated.

The governments of Mauritius and Seychelles did not respond to requests for comment.

Taiwan is not a member of the United Nations or its agencies due to opposition from Beijing, which considers the democratically governed island part of its territory.

Taiwan rejects Beijing’s sovereignty claims and says China has no right to represent the island internationally.

Taiwan president’s flight

Taiwan’s government said Seychelles, Mauritius and Madagascar revoked permission for Lai’s aircraft to fly through airspace they manage on the way to Eswatini, one of only 12 countries with formal diplomatic ties to Chinese-claimed Taiwan.

Lai said China had used economic “coercion” to secure their cooperation, which Beijing denied. Lai eventually traveled to Eswatini the following month aboard the Eswatini king’s private aircraft, announcing the trip only after arriving.

The US paper, seen by Reuters, focuses on Mauritius and Seychelles and does not mention Madagascar.

According to the paper, Taiwan’s China Airlines had received permits for the charter flight to cross portions of the two countries’ flight information regions, or FIRs, over the high seas. Both countries revoked the permits days before departure without citing safety or operational concerns, it said.

The distinction between sovereign airspace and FIRs is central to the dispute. Countries have sovereignty over airspace above their territory and territorial waters, but the FIRs they manage can extend far beyond those boundaries over international waters.

Countries provide air traffic services in those areas for safety and operational purposes but do not gain sovereignty over them, according to the US paper.

Washington has asked the ICAO Council to express concern over the withdrawn permits and have the agency’s secretary-general seek written explanations from Mauritius and Seychelles. It also wants ICAO to determine whether any remedies are needed to ensure their compliance with international aviation rules.

The State Department expressed concern in April, saying responsibility for managing international airspace beyond a country’s sovereign territory was “solely to ensure aviation safety, not to serve as a political tool for Beijing.” – Rappler.com

World.title: Iran, Oman foreign ministers discuss safeguarding maritime corridors
World.content:
STRAIT. A vessel near the Strait of Hormuz, as seen from Musandam, Oman, August 17, 2026.

The talks take place during a visit by Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi to Oman, which holds the southern coast of the Strait of Hormuz and has played a role as mediator in the crisis that broke out when the United States Israel and struck the Islamic Republic on February 28

DUBAI, UAE – Iran and Oman discussed on Tuesday, November 17, safeguarding maritime corridors and ensuring the smooth flow of global shipping and trade, as well as revitalizing channels for dialogue and negotiations to prevent escalations, the Omani foreign ministry said.

The talks took place during a visit by Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi to Oman, which holds the southern coast of the Strait of Hormuz and has played a role as mediator in the crisis that broke out when the United States Israel and struck the Islamic Republic on February 28.

The visit comes against the backdrop of increased attacks on tankers in the strait as Tehran continues to disrupt shipping in the vital waterway while Washington maintains a naval blockade on Iran in response.

The Strait of Hormuz, a narrow chokepoint which carried one-fifth of global energy supplies before the conflict, remains a sticking point in negotiations aimed at ending the nine-month-old war that have not yielded a breakthrough yet. – Rappler.com

World.title: FACT CHECK: VP Sara’s counsel did not call for ‘People Power’ at ASEAN Summit
World.content:
The quote card attributes a call for mass action to lawyer Sheila Sison, Vice President Sara Duterte's lead counsel, but she did not make such a statement, contrary to the claim

Claim: Lawyer Sheila Sison, lead defense counsel in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, called for “People Power” during the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit to expose corruption and humiliate President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.

Rating: FALSE

Why we fact-checked this: A video was posted on November 14 by the Facebook page Jay Halago Near, a day before the Philippines began hosting the 49th ASEAN Summit.

Its thumbnail carries a quote attributed to Sison, which says, “People Power sa ASEAN Summit! Para malaman ng mundo ang korapsyon sa Pinas, ipapahiya natin si PBBM!”

(People Power at the ASEAN Summit! So the world will know about corruption in the Philippines, we will humiliate [President Bongbong Marcos]!)

The graphic has a “PH News Update” label and the word “Korapsyon? (Corruption?)” beside a photo of Marcos.

The post’s caption reads: “People Power sa ASEAN Summit? Panawagan laban sa korapsyon, umani ng atensyon! Dapat bang gawing pagkakataon ang ASEAN Summit para iparinig ang hinaing ng taumbayan? Kayo, anong opinyon ninyo?”

(People Power at the ASEAN Summit? A call against corruption draws attention! Should the ASEAN Summit be used to air the people’s grievances? What is your opinion?)

As of writing, the video has 93,000 views, 5,900 reactions, 1,700 comments, and 758 shares.

The facts: No news report or public statement shows Sison urging the public to gather for a “people power” movement during the ASEAN Summit.

Sison is lead defense counsel in Duterte’s ongoing impeachment trial, and her recent public remarks concern the case.

On November 10, she raised concerns before the impeachment court over statements that private prosecutors made to the media. On November 12, she asked the court to cancel the November 13 session. None of these accounts mentions the ASEAN Summit or any call for mass action.

Protest amid ASEAN: Protests did take place during the summit, but Sison did not lead them, and they were not a People Power call to humiliate Marcos over government corruption. On November 15, the summit’s opening day, police clashed with activists at Liwasang Bonifacio in Manila as they attempted to march toward the summit venue.

Groups under Bagong Alyansang Makabayan and the All Workers Unity coalition were protesting antiworker policies, the arrival of US President Donald Trump, and the proposed Pax Silica hub in New Clark City.

Police said the groups lacked a permit to assemble outside the Freedom Park. Nearly 300 arrests were made in Muntinlupa alone following the protests. (READ: Lawmakers, groups slam November 15 arrests: Where is maximum tolerance?)

The Palace has previously urged protesters not to “tarnish” the country’s reputation during the summit.

The Philippines, ASEAN chair for 2026, is hosting the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits from November 15 to 17. (LIVE UPDATES: 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila)

Impeachment trial: Meanwhile, Duterte’s impeachment trial continues. By the end of its 43rd day on November 12, the trial examined two major credit card purchases by the Vice President’s husband, Manases Carpio, in Japan and Malaysia, with witnesses explaining the expenses as shared dining and purchases for basketball players.

Rappler has fact-checked similar claims related to the impeachment trial.

– Cyril Bocar/Rappler.com

Efren Cyril Bocar is a journalist from Llorente, Eastern Samar who graduated with a degree in English Language Studies at the Visayas State University. Cyril is also a graduate of the Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship of Rappler for 2024.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

World.title: PCG bans travel to Fuga Island due to live-fire military drills
World.content:
Philippine Coast Guard logo. (Photo from PCG/Facebook)

TUGUEGARAO CITY- The Philippine Coast Guard barred fishermen and sea vessel operators from temporary no-sail zones off Fuga Island on November 21 and Barangay Dodan on Nov. 24 due to scheduled military live-fire exercises there.

Live ammunition will be used during the Counter-Landing Live Fire Exercises, part of the Armed Forces of the Philippines Joint Exercise Dagat-Langit-Lupa (AJEX DAGIT-PA 10-26) there, the Coast Guard said in a statement.

The exercises intend to strengthen the country’s coastal defense capabilities.

Article continues after this 

READ: Dinagat Islands gears up for live-fire war games

The restricted area off Barangay Dodan covers approximately 7,212 hectares, while vessel movement will also be prohibited in the designated waters off Fuga Island on the scheduled exercise date.

Coast Guard Station Cagayan has urged fishermen and vessel operators “to strictly observe the restrictions and avoid entering the affected waters to prevent accidents during the live-fire activities.

The 5th Infantry Division has been overseeing the Counter-Landing Live Fire Exercise (CLLFX) in Aparri, Cagayan, which is a coastal defense military exercise in Northern Luzon for maneuvers to repel simulated amphibious invasions.

During the live-fire activity, “all vessels and watercraft are prohibited from entering the designated coordinates,” the Coast Guard Station Cagayan said in a statement, adding that normal maritime traffic will resume once the drills conclude.

In a separate statement, the 5th ID said “safety measures” have been instituted to ensure “commitment to keeping communities informed and working closely with local authorities and residents before and during military exercises.”/coa

World.title: MPD to protesters: Do not breach Liwasang Bonifacio boundaries
World.content:
Police equipped with riot shields and batons immediately blocked the road in front of Liwasang Bonifacio in anticipation of their planned march to PICC. Photo by Zacarian Sarao

MANILA, Philippines — The Manila Police District (MPD) on Tuesday warned protesters not to breach the boundaries of Liwasang Bonifacio, stating that they will arrest rallyists should they proceed with their march.

The MPD said this amid an ongoing demonstration by various groups at Liwasang Bonifacio in Manila where they are protesting the arrival of United States President Donald Trump for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) Summit, as well as the proposed Pax Silica Hub in New Clark City.

“Waglalampas dito. Non-negotiable. Hanggang dito na lang,” MPD Director PBGen. Arnold Santiago told reporters in a chance interview.

Article continues after this 

(They cannot get past here. This is a non-negotiable.)

“Kung lumagpas dito hindi kami papayag, kung magkagulo man, hindi kami ang nagumpisa,” he added.

(We will not allow them to breach the boundary of [Liwasang Bonifaco]. Even if chaos ensues, we did not start it.)

Santiago maintained that while they have no intention to hurt protesters, they would have no choice but to do so once provoked.

“Kung manggugulo sila? Idi-disperse talaga, manghuhuli kami ng tao tulad noong ginawa namin nitong Linggo,” said the MPD director.

Article continues after this 

Santiago said there are currently 5,000 police officers stationed around Liwasang Bonifacio, with an additional 500 backup on standby.

Protest rganizers earlier said that they intend to push through with their march to the PICC on Tuesday afternoon.

Article continues after this 

This is despite a violent scuffle that occurred between protesters and cops on Sunday, which ignited after the demonstrators attempted to march towards the Philippine International Convention Center (PICC) which serves as the main venue for this year’s Asean Summit. /ms

World.title: Magalong says Pax Silica needs better marketing
World.content:
Baguio Mayor Benjamin Magalong on Monday, Nov.16, 2026, said the Pax Silica initiative needs a more comprehensive government information campaign. Photo of November 16, 2026 Baguio rally by Vincent Cabreza

BAGUIO CITY — Baguio Mayor Benjamin Magalong on Monday said the Pax Silica initiative needs a more comprehensive government information campaign.

Speaking after this week’s flag-raising ceremony, the mayor said the absence of clear information has fueled speculation, misconceptions, and misinformation about the initiative.

“Sa tingin ko na-identify na nila yung problema sa communication, ginagawan na nila ng paraan. So hintayin na lang siguro natin,” Magalong said.

Article continues after this 

READ: Pax Silica brings promise – but at what cost?

(I think the government has identified these gaps in communication and they are addressing them. Let’s wait)

The mayor said he does not blame groups opposing Pax Silica, particularly those raising concerns over environmental impacts, including threats to water resources.

On ancestral land claims, however, Magalong cited Clark’s established economic zone status and questioned such claims to the proposed development site.

Economics lecturer Ruel Caricativo of the University of the Philippines Baguio challenged this position in a Monday post. He took part in a Baguio rally that same day against Pax Silica and the scheduled visit of American President Donald Trump.

Article continues after this 

“Mr. Magalong seemed to have forgotten that the current Clark Economic Zone is the former Clark Airbase, which was built on stolen Aeta lands in Central Luzon,” Caricativo said.

READ: Trump visit, Pax Silica draw more protests in Baguio

Article continues after this 

He warned that the same pattern of land appropriation could be repeated in the Cordillera, Mindanao and other indigenous territories under the guise of economic development.

Caricativo said the controversy goes beyond a lack of public information, arguing that the government was promising investments, jobs, and industrialization without adequately explaining the initiative’s implications.

“To reiterate: instead of sharing relevant information about the Pax Silica, the Marcos Jr. administration peddles a lot of smoke and mirrors to misinform the public, all the while fast-tracking this deal with the US,” he said.

He said Pax Silica should be examined in the context of the Luzon Economic Corridor (LEC) and the United States’ efforts to secure strategic resources and supply chains amid its intensifying rivalry with China.

Caricativo described the LEC as part of efforts to rehabilitate former US military installations to serve American strategic and industrial interests, particularly in securing critical minerals and rare elements.

Launched in April 2024 by the United States, Japan and the Philippines under the G7’s Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment, the LEC aims to connect Subic Bay, Clark, Manila and Batangas through investments in transportation, logistics, energy, digital infrastructure and advanced manufacturing.

READ: Protesters, police clash in Manila during Asean Summit protest

The Philippine Embassy in Washington said the corridor covers areas accounting for about 50 percent of the country’s gross domestic product. It is envisioned to attract investment, generate jobs, modernize infrastructure and strengthen regional supply chains.

The partnership has since expanded to include Australia, Canada, Denmark, France, Italy, South Korea, Sweden and the United Kingdom. Priority projects include railway development, port and airport modernization, clean energy, nuclear power, fuel infrastructure, semiconductor manufacturing and digital connectivity.

A May 2026 joint statement by the three founding governments identified digital connectivity and advanced manufacturing under the corridor as key to strengthening trusted global technology supply chains, complementing Pax Silica.

Under Pax Silica, the US government has announced plans to establish a 4,000-acre Economic Security Zone in New Clark City within the corridor. The proposed industrial hub aims to strengthen supply chains for semiconductors, critical minerals, electronics and other strategic goods.

The US government has identified Philippine reserves of nickel, copper, chromite and cobalt as resources for these supply chains, alongside the country’s energy resources, workforce and strategic Indo-Pacific location.

Caricativo said the initiative should be understood within the broader competition over strategic resources, particularly as the United States seeks to strengthen its position against China, which currently leads in the extraction and processing of rare earth elements.

READ: Probe arrests in Asean rally, bishop urges CHR

He said the government’s promotion of economic benefits while fast-tracking its engagement with the US leaves communities with unanswered questions about the initiative’s implications for ancestral lands, natural resources and indigenous peoples’ rights.

World.title: Tacloban schools shift to morning in-person classes due to heat
World.content:
Students attend shortened morning classes at a public school in Tacloban City as school administrators adjust learning schedules to minimize exposure to extreme heat. Photo by Joey A. Gabieta

TACLOBAN CITY – Schools in Tacloban City have shortened classroom hours and shifted afternoon lessons to modular learning as soaring temperatures continue to pose health risks to over 55,000 students in the city’s public schools.

Under adjusted class schedules this week, face-to-face classes are held only in the morning, from 7:30 a.m. to 11:45 a.m., while afternoon lessons are conducted through printed or digital learning modules.

Class periods have also been reduced from the usual 45 minutes to 30 minutes, with students completing written activities at home.

Article continues after this 

READ: High heat index halts in-person classes in Tacloban public schools

School administrators said the adjustments were intended to protect students from prolonged exposure to high temperatures while ensuring that learning continues despite the unfavorable weather conditions.

Parents have also been advised to ensure their children drink plenty of water, wear light and comfortable clothing, and avoid outdoor activities, particularly during the hottest hours of the day.

Meanwhile, public schools in the city suspended face-to-face classes on Wednesday following projections that the heat index could reach 42 degrees Celsius.

Tacloban has been experiencing high to extreme heat over the past several days, prompting schools to adopt precautionary measures to prevent heat-related illnesses among students.

Article continues after this 

The city has 60 public elementary and secondary schools serving more than 55,000 students.

READ: Heat index in parts of Eastern Visayas expected to increase

Article continues after this 

The heat index measures how hot temperatures feel to the human body when relative humidity is considered. According to the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration, a heat index of 42 to 51°C falls under the danger category. Here, heat cramps and heat exhaustion are likely, while heat stroke is possible with continued exposure./coa

World.title: El Niño hits 9,348 families, damages 422 hectares in Iligan
World.content:
The Rapid Damage Assessment and Needs Analysis (RDANA) team visited farmers in Iligan City on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, to assess crop damage and the effects of El Niño. Photo by Iligan City Information Office

ILIGAN CITY — The prolonged dry spell from El Niño has affected 9,348 families and damaged 422 hectares of farmland in Iligan City, according to the latest consolidated findings of the city’s Rapid Damage Assessment and Needs Analysis (RDANA).

The report showed that the affected families, from 17 barangays, accounted for 11.16 percent of the city’s 83,773 households based on the 2024 Community-Based Monitoring System (CBMS) data.

The affected farmland, meanwhile, represents approximately 0.52 percent of the city’s total agricultural land area of 81,337 hectares.

Article continues after this 

READ: Food stockpiling eyed amid El Niño, other crises

The City Agriculturist’s Office (CAO) said it consolidated field reports on El Niño’s impact on agriculture, gathered starting August 13, covering 16 barangays.

The findings indicated that upland rice and corn were among the crops severely affected, particularly in hinterland communities, as the dry spell from July to September coincided with the planting season.

Kevin Fernan, the city government’s agriculture focal person, said 11 barangays had submitted resolutions reporting the effects of extreme heat and water stress on their agricultural production.

Initial assessments found no immediate concerns requiring urgent intervention regarding water sources in affected communities.

Article continues after this 

The RDANA also covered livelihood, public health, and other essential community services to determine additional needs, including food assistance and medical services for affected farmers.

READ: DA: El Niño puts food supply under pressure

Article continues after this 

Armien Alorro, head of the Iligan City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Department (ICDRRMD), said the assessment would serve as the basis for identifying appropriate government interventions and assistance.

“This will serve as the actual basis for what we need to do next. We will submit the findings for possible interventions and government support, not necessarily from the local government but also from national agencies such as the Department of Agriculture, Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources, Office of Civil Defense, and Department of Health,” Alorro said.

The assessment teams include personnel from the CAO, City Health Office, City Engineer’s Office, City Information Office, Iligan City Environment and Natural Resources Office, and ICDRRMD.

The consolidated findings will be submitted to Mayor Frederick Siao and the City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council for appropriate action and the formulation of programs, projects, and interventions.

READ: El Niño impact on PH growth may be minimal–Balisacan

The report is also expected to guide the city’s preparations for the projected super El Niño during the first quarter of 2027./coa

World.title: NBI: School shooting in Batac, Ilocos Norte foiled
World.content:
NBI Director Melvin Matibag. INQUIRER/ MARIANNE BERMUDEZ

MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) said it had foiled a school shooting allegedly planned by three minors in Batac, Ilocos Norte.

In an interview on Tuesday, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said they located the minors after receiving intelligence information from their counterpart at the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) about the supposed planned shooting.

“Immediately, we deployed our task force, the TF-NVE (Task Force on National Violent Extremism), to investigate. And it tested positive; we found three minors here,” Matibag told reporters.

Article continues after this 

“We interviewed them, and one of these subjects confessed that he actually had a plan to shoot,” he added.

READ: NBI to provide assistance in Quiboloy’s potential extradition

According to Matibag, the three individuals, all 16 years old and neighbors, planned to carry out the mass shooting on Dec. 16, the start of Simbang Gabi.

He added that the minors formed a group chat in November where they discussed planning the crime, which would target more than five students.

Matibag said he had yet to verify the students’ year levels but noted that they attended the same school where they supposedly planned to carry out the shooting.

Article continues after this 

He did not identify the school.

READ: NBI probes foreigners’ ‘fraudulently procured’ PH citizenship papers

Article continues after this 

‘Victim of bullying’

Matibag also said one of the minors claimed to have been bullied at school since Grade 7.

“So he mentioned some names, saying, ‘These guys are bullying me,’ and he watched the video of Columbine, which encouraged him to do the same,” Matibag said, referring to the Columbine High School massacre, a mass shooting and attempted bombing in 1999 in Colorado, United States.

“What is alarming is that eventually, there is encouragement to commit suicide after the shooting,” he added.

He also said the NBI had secured a gun from one of the minors, who supposedly obtained it from his parents.

“The story is, they talked to the parents about where the gun was hidden because they needed to use it. They had a film to make, so they needed props or something like that,” he said.
